`lib/health.js`:

```js
/**
 * Service health for the workbench overview.
 *
 * The panel cannot see inside the MCP client, so this module answers the
 * question from the outside: are the `mcp__rea__*` tools actually registered in
 * this process, and how many? A registered tool means the stdio server started,
 * completed the MCP handshake, and answered `tools/list`. A missing one means
 * the launch failed — wrong Node version, `npx` blocked, package resolution
 * error — and the panel must say so instead of showing a green "ready".
 *
 * Every check returns a status plus a remediation line, because "MCP 断开" alone
 * leaves the user with nothing to do.
 */

import { probeAll, providerEnvironment, CACHE_ROOT, REA_AGENTS_VERSION } from './providers.js';

/** Minimum Node version REA accepts, matching its `engines.node` field. */
const NODE_RULES = [
  { matches: (major) => major === 22, minMinor: 19 },
  { matches: (major) => major === 24, minMinor: 11 },
  { matches: (major) => major >= 26, minMinor: 0 },
];

function checkNode() {
  const version = process.versions.node;
  const [majorText, minorText] = version.split('.');
  const major = Number(majorText);
  const minor = Number(minorText);

  const rule = NODE_RULES.find((candidate) => candidate.matches(major));
  const ok = Boolean(rule) && minor >= rule.minMinor;

  return {
    id: 'node',
    label: 'Node.js',
    // `ok` drives the dot; `warn` marks a condition that limits features but
    // does not stop the server.
    status: ok ? 'ok' : 'error',
    value: `v${version}`,
    detail: ok
      ? null
      : `REA 需要 Node 22.19+ / 24.11+ / 26+，当前 v${version} 无法启动 MCP 服务`,
    fix: ok ? null : '升级 Node.js 到 22.19 或更高版本，然后重启 Harness',
  };
}

/**
 * Inspect registered tools for the REA server.
 *
 * `ctx.tools.schemas()` is the same projection the model sees, so counting
 * `mcp__rea__` there proves the agent can actually call them.
 */
function checkMcpTools(tools) {
  let schemas = [];
  try {
    schemas = tools?.schemas ? tools.schemas() : [];
  } catch {
    schemas = [];
  }

  const reaTools = schemas.filter((schema) => String(schema?.name ?? '').startsWith('mcp__rea__'));
  const count = reaTools.length;

  if (count === 0) {
    return {
      id: 'mcp',
      label: 'REA MCP 服务',
      status: 'error',
      value: '未连接',
      detail: '没有任何 mcp__rea__* 工具注册在进程里，说明 stdio 服务器没有起来或握手失败',
      fix: '检查 Harness 日志中的 rea-mcp 行；常见原因是 Node 版本、npx 被拦截、或首次下载超时',
      toolCount: 0,
    };
  }

  return {
    id: 'mcp',
    label: 'REA MCP 服务',
    // The upstream catalogue is 207 tools. Fewer than half means a partial
    // connection or a different server answered, which warrants a warning even
    // though calls may still work.
    status: count >= 100 ? 'ok' : 'warn',
    value: `${count} 个工具`,
    detail: count >= 100
      ? null
      : `只注册了 ${count} 个工具，低于完整的 207 个；可能是部分工具被限制或版本不符`,
    fix: count >= 100 ? null : '重新加载 rea-mcp 行以重建工具目录',
    toolCount: count,
  };
}

/** Java is a hard prerequisite for JADX and apktool. */
function checkJava(java) {
  return {
    id: 'java',
    label: 'Java 运行时',
    status: java?.present ? 'ok' : 'warn',
    value: java?.present ? String(java.version ?? '已安装').slice(0, 40) : '缺失',
    detail: java?.present ? null : 'JADX 与 apktool 依赖 Java，缺失时 Android 分析不可用',
    fix: java?.present ? null : '安装 JDK 17+ 并确保 java 在 PATH 中',
  };
}

/**
 * Python runtime for the MobileRE layer.
 *
 * Missing packages are reported by name rather than as a single failure: the
 * thirteen standard-library scripts still work, so this is a partial capability
 * (warn), never a hard error.
 */
function checkPython(python) {
  if (!python) {
    return {
      id: 'python',
      label: 'Python 运行时',
      status: 'warn',
      value: '未探测',
      detail: 'MobileRE 的 21 个脚本需要 Python 3.9+',
      fix: '安装 Python 3 后刷新；插件会自动发现 %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Python',
    };
  }
  if (!python.present) {
    return {
      id: 'python',
      label: 'Python 运行时',
      status: 'warn',
      value: '缺失',
      detail: python.error ?? 'MobileRE 的 21 个脚本需要 Python 3.9+',
      fix: '安装 Python 3.11+，或用 config.pythonPath 指定解释器路径',
    };
  }

  const missing = python.missing ?? [];
  const core = missing.filter((name) => ['frida', 'capstone', 'elftools'].includes(name));
  const optional = missing.filter((name) => !core.includes(name));

  if (missing.length === 0) {
    return {
      id: 'python',
      label: 'Python 运行时',
      status: 'ok',
      value: python.version,
      detail: 'MobileRE 全部脚本可用',
      fix: null,
    };
  }

  const pip = missing
    .map((name) => (name === 'elftools' ? 'pyelftools' : (name === 'z3' ? 'z3-solver' : name)))
    .join(' ');

  return {
    id: 'python',
    label: 'Python 运行时',
    status: 'warn',
    value: `${python.version} · 缺 ${missing.length} 包`,
    detail: `未安装：${missing.join(', ')}。纯标准库脚本仍可用`,
    fix: `${python.command} -m pip install ${pip}`,
  };
}

/** Engine summary as one line. */
function checkEngines(providers, java) {
  const ready = providers.filter((provider) => provider.present);
  const required = providers.filter((provider) => !provider.advisory);

  // JADX without Java cannot decompile, so a present jar with no runtime is not
  // "ready" in any useful sense.
  const blockedByJava = !java?.present && ready.some((provider) => provider.id === 'jadx');
  const readyCount = ready.length;
  const totalCount = providers.length;

  const status = blockedByJava
    ? 'warn'
    : readyCount === totalCount
      ? 'ok'
      : readyCount === 0
        ? 'error'
        : 'warn';

  return {
    id: 'engines',
    label: '分析引擎',
    status,
    value: `${readyCount} / ${totalCount}`,
    detail: blockedByJava
      ? 'JADX 已安装但缺少 Java，无法反编译'
      : readyCount === totalCount
        ? null
        : `未安装：${providers.filter((provider) => !provider.present).map((provider) => provider.title).join(', ')}`,
    fix: readyCount === totalCount ? null : '在工作台下方的引擎卡片上点击「一键安装」',
    readyCount,
    totalCount,
  };
}

/** Where engines live, plus whether that path is writable. */
async function checkCache(cacheRoot) {
  try {
    const fs = await import('node:fs/promises');
    await fs.mkdir(cacheRoot, { recursive: true });
    const probe = `${cacheRoot}/.write-probe`;
    await fs.writeFile(probe, 'ok');
    await fs.rm(probe, { force: true });
    return {
      id: 'cache',
      label: '引擎目录',
      status: 'ok',
      value: cacheRoot,
      detail: null,
      fix: null,
    };
  } catch (error) {
    return {
      id: 'cache',
      label: '引擎目录',
      status: 'error',
      value: cacheRoot,
      detail: `目录不可写：${error.message}`,
      fix: '检查磁盘空间与目录权限，或把引擎装到其他位置后手动设置环境变量',
    };
  }
}

/**
 * Full service-health report.
 *
 * Returned as a list so the panel renders one row per check without knowing the
 * order or the set of checks in advance.
 */
export async function buildHealth({ tools, telemetry, python = null }) {
  const report = await probeAll();

  const checks = [
    checkNode(),
    checkMcpTools(tools),
    checkEngines(report.providers, report.java),
    checkJava(report.java),
    checkPython(python),
    await checkCache(CACHE_ROOT),
  ];

  const counts = telemetry?.counts ?? { total: 0, failed: 0, rea: 0, reaFailed: 0 };
  const recentFailureRate = counts.total > 0 ? counts.failed / counts.total : 0;

  checks.push({
    id: 'errors',
    label: '近期错误',
    // A high failure rate matters more than an absolute count: one failure among
    // three calls is far worse than five among two hundred.
    status: recentFailureRate > 0.25 ? 'error' : recentFailureRate > 0.05 ? 'warn' : 'ok',
    value: `${counts.failed} / ${counts.total}`,
    detail: counts.failed > 0
      ? `自启动以来 ${counts.total} 次调用中有 ${counts.failed} 次失败`
      : null,
    fix: counts.failed > 0 ? '展开下方「错误聚合」查看具体工具与原因' : null,
  });

  const worst = checks.some((check) => check.status === 'error')
    ? 'error'
    : checks.some((check) => check.status === 'warn')
      ? 'warn'
      : 'ok';

  return {
    ok: worst !== 'error',
    overall: worst,
    at: Date.now(),
    uptimeMs: Date.now() - (telemetry?.startedAt ?? Date.now()),
    checks,
    environment: providerEnvironment(),
    reaVersion: REA_AGENTS_VERSION,
    cacheRoot: CACHE_ROOT,
    platform: `${process.platform}/${process.arch}`,
  };
}

```

`lib/jdk.js`:

```js
/**
 * JDK provisioning.
 *
 * Ghidra 11.2+ requires Java 21, and the machine may have 17 (or nothing). Java
 * is a different install problem from the analysis engines:
 *
 *  - It ships as an `.msi`/`.pkg`/`.tar.gz`, not a zip we can unpack into
 *    `~/.dsh/rea-engines`, and on Windows the MSI wants administrator rights.
 *  - The system already has a Java that other tools use. Replacing `JAVA_HOME`
 *    globally would change every other program on the machine, which is not
 *    something a plugin should do without being asked.
 *
 * So this installs a *private* JDK into the plugin's own cache and exposes it
 * through `REA_JAVA_HOME`. Ghidra reads that first; everything else keeps the
 * system Java. Nothing global changes.
 */

import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import path from 'node:path';
import os from 'node:os';
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';

/** Where a private JDK lives. Sibling of the engine cache, so one delete cleans both. */
export const JDK_ROOT = path.join(os.homedir(), '.dsh', 'rea-jdk');

/** The major version Ghidra 11.x requires. */
export const REQUIRED_JAVA = 21;

/**
 * Download sources, tried in order until one is fast enough to finish.
 *
 * Measured on a Chinese network: `api.adoptium.net` served the 196 MB Windows
 * archive at 0.04 MB/s — 85 minutes, and long enough that the 60 s stall timer
 * aborted it every time. The Tsinghua mirror of the same Adoptium tree delivered
 * 1.9 MB/s, about 47× faster. So the mirror comes first and the official API is
 * the fallback for networks where the mirror is unreachable.
 *
 * The mirror path is resolved by reading its directory index rather than
 * hardcoding a build number: OpenJDK 21 receives updates, and a pinned filename
 * would 404 after the next one.
 */
const TUNA_ADOPTIUM = 'https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/Adoptium';

function platformSegments() {
  const arch = process.arch === 'arm64' ? 'aarch64' : 'x64';

  if (process.platform === 'win32') {
    return {
      adoptium: { os: 'windows', arch, kind: 'zip' },
      tuna: { os: 'windows', arch, kind: 'zip', pattern: /OpenJDK21U-jdk_x64_windows_hotspot.*\.zip$/ },
      archive: 'jdk.zip',
    };
  }
  if (process.platform === 'darwin') {
    return {
      adoptium: { os: 'mac', arch, kind: 'tar.gz' },
      tuna: { os: 'mac', arch, kind: 'tar.gz', pattern: /OpenJDK21U-jdk_aarch64_mac_hotspot.*\.tar\.gz$/ },
      archive: 'jdk.tar.gz',
    };
  }
  return {
    adoptium: { os: 'linux', arch, kind: 'tar.gz' },
    tuna: { os: 'linux', arch, kind: 'tar.gz', pattern: /OpenJDK21U-jdk_x64_linux_hotspot.*\.tar\.gz$/ },
    archive: 'jdk.tar.gz',
  };
}

/** Absolute mirror URL for the newest matching build, or null if unreachable. */
async function resolveMirrorUrl(spec) {
  const directory = `${TUNA_ADOPTIUM}/${REQUIRED_JAVA}/jdk/${spec.arch}/${spec.os}/`;
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`${directory}?mirrorlist`, {
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000),
    });
    if (!response.ok) return null;

    const html = await response.text();
    const names = [...html.matchAll(/href="([^"]+)"/g)]
      .map((match) => match[1])
      .filter((href) => spec.pattern.test(href));

    if (names.length === 0) return null;
    // Directory listings sort lexicographically; the last match is the newest.
    return directory + names[names.length - 1];
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/**
 * Candidate list for this platform, best first.
 *
 * Resolved lazily so an unreachable mirror costs one HEAD and not a failed
 * install.
 */
async function downloadCandidates() {
  const segments = platformSegments();
  const candidates = [];

  const mirror = await resolveMirrorUrl(segments.tuna);
  if (mirror) {
    candidates.push({ url: mirror, label: '清华镜像', kind: segments.tuna.kind });
  }

  candidates.push({
    url: `https://api.adoptium.net/v3/binary/latest/${REQUIRED_JAVA}/ga`
      + `/${segments.adoptium.os}/${segments.adoptium.arch}/jdk/hotspot/normal/eclipse`,
    label: 'Adoptium 官方',
    kind: segments.adoptium.kind,
  });

  return { candidates, archive: segments.archive };
}

/** Run a binary and capture its first stderr/stdout line. */
function run(command, args) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const child = spawn(command, args, { stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'], windowsHide: true });
    let out = '';
    child.stdout.setEncoding('utf8');
    child.stderr.setEncoding('utf8');
    child.stdout.on('data', (c) => { out += c; });
    child.stderr.on('data', (c) => { out += c; });
    child.on('error', () => resolve({ ok: false, text: '' }));
    child.on('exit', (code) => resolve({ ok: code === 0, text: out }));
  });
}

/** Parse the major version out of `java -version` output. */
export function parseJavaMajor(text) {
  // Java 8 prints `1.8.0_xxx`; 9+ prints `21.0.1` or `21`.
  const quoted = /version "(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?/.exec(text ?? '');
  if (quoted) {
    const major = Number(quoted[1]);
    return major === 1 ? Number(quoted[2] ?? 0) : major;
  }
  const bare = /(?:openjdk|java)\s+(\d+)/i.exec(text ?? '');
  return bare ? Number(bare[1]) : null;
}

/**
 * Find a JDK 21+ without downloading anything.
 *
 * Order: the private cache (our own install), then `REA_JAVA_HOME`, then
 * `JAVA_HOME`, then PATH. The private cache wins so a plugin install is stable
 * regardless of what the user later changes globally.
 */
export async function findJdk21() {
  const candidates = [];

  // 1. our own install
  if (existsSync(JDK_ROOT)) {
    const entries = await fs.readdir(JDK_ROOT).catch(() => []);
    for (const entry of entries) {
      const home = path.join(JDK_ROOT, entry);
      candidates.push({
        home,
        java: path.join(home, 'bin', process.platform === 'win32' ? 'java.exe' : 'java'),
        source: 'plugin',
      });
    }
  }

  // 2. operator-provided
  for (const [envName, source] of [['REA_JAVA_HOME', 'rea-java-home'], ['JAVA_HOME', 'java-home']]) {
    const home = process.env[envName];
    if (!home) continue;
    candidates.push({
      home,
      java: path.join(home, 'bin', process.platform === 'win32' ? 'java.exe' : 'java'),
      source,
    });
  }

  // 3. PATH
  candidates.push({
    home: null,
    java: 'java',
    source: 'path',
  });

  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    if (candidate.home && !existsSync(candidate.java)) continue;

    const result = await run(candidate.java, ['-version']);
    if (!result.ok || !result.text) continue;

    const major = parseJavaMajor(result.text);
    if (major === null) continue;

    return {
      present: major >= REQUIRED_JAVA,
      major,
      sufficient: major >= REQUIRED_JAVA,
      home: candidate.home,
      java: candidate.java,
      source: candidate.source,
      version: result.text.split('\n')[0].trim(),
      required: REQUIRED_JAVA,
    };
  }

  return {
    present: false,
    major: null,
    sufficient: false,
    home: null,
    java: null,
    source: null,
    version: null,
    required: REQUIRED_JAVA,
  };
}

/**
 * Download and unpack a private JDK 21.
 *
 * `onProgress` gets byte counts so the panel can show a bar; the archive is
 * ~180 MB and takes long enough that silence would look like a hang.
 */
export async function installJdk({ onProgress, signal } = {}) {
  const { candidates, archive } = await downloadCandidates();
  await fs.mkdir(JDK_ROOT, { recursive: true });

  const archivePath = path.join(JDK_ROOT, archive);

  // Download with Range support so a resumed job continues rather than restarting.
  const { download } = await import('./providers.js');

  let downloaded = null;
  const failures = [];

  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    if (signal?.aborted) throw new Error('已取消');
    onProgress?.({
      phase: 'download',
      percent: 0,
      received: 0,
      total: 0,
      source: candidate.label,
    });

    try {
      await download(candidate.url, archivePath, {
        maxBytes: 512 * 1024 * 1024,
        signal,
        // A 196 MB archive on a slow link needs more patience than the 60 s
        // default: the mirror moves 1.9 MB/s but can pause longer than that on
        // a congested link without the transfer being dead.
        stallMs: 180_000,
        onProgress: (progress) => onProgress?.({
          phase: 'download',
          received: progress.received,
          total: progress.total,
          percent: progress.percent,
          bytesPerSecond: progress.bytesPerSecond,
          source: candidate.label,
        }),
      });
      downloaded = candidate;
      break;
    } catch (error) {
      // A cancelled job is not a source failure; do not try the next URL.
      if (signal?.aborted) throw error;
      failures.push(`${candidate.label}: ${error?.message ?? error}`);
      onProgress?.({
        phase: 'download',
        percent: 0,
        received: 0,
        total: 0,
        source: `${candidate.label} 失败，换下一个源`,
      });
    }
  }

  if (!downloaded) {
    throw new Error(`所有下载源均失败：\n${failures.join('\n')}`);
  }

  onProgress?.({ phase: 'extract', percent: 100 });

  // Unpack into a staging directory, then move the single top-level folder in.
  const staging = path.join(JDK_ROOT, '.staging');
  await fs.rm(staging, { recursive: true, force: true });
  await fs.mkdir(staging, { recursive: true });

  await extractArchive(archivePath, staging, downloaded.kind, { signal });

  const entries = await fs.readdir(staging);
  const root = entries.length === 1 ? path.join(staging, entries[0]) : staging;

  // Give it a stable name so `findJdk21` cannot accumulate a second copy.
  const target = path.join(JDK_ROOT, `jdk-${REQUIRED_JAVA}`);
  await fs.rm(target, { recursive: true, force: true });
  await fs.rename(root, target);

  await fs.rm(staging, { recursive: true, force: true });
  await fs.rm(archivePath, { force: true });

  onProgress?.({ phase: 'done', percent: 100 });

  return { home: target, java: path.join(target, 'bin', process.platform === 'win32' ? 'java.exe' : 'java') };
}

/**
 * Extract a zip or tar.gz using the platform's own tools.
 *
 * Deliberately not a JS archiver: a JDK archive is ~300 MB unpacked with tens
 * of thousands of entries, and the OS tools are both faster and guaranteed to
 * preserve the executable bits on Unix.
 */
function extractArchive(archive, destination, kind, { signal } = {}) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    let command;
    let args;

    if (kind === 'zip') {
      if (process.platform === 'win32') {
        command = 'powershell.exe';
        args = ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-Command',
          `Expand-Archive -LiteralPath '${archive.replace(/'/g, "''")}' -DestinationPath '${destination.replace(/'/g, "''")}' -Force`];
      } else {
        command = 'unzip';
        args = ['-q', archive, '-d', destination];
      }
    } else {
      command = 'tar';
      args = ['-xzf', archive, '-C', destination];
    }

    const child = spawn(command, args, { stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'], windowsHide: true });
    let stderr = '';
    child.stderr.setEncoding('utf8');
    child.stderr.on('data', (c) => { stderr += c; });

    const onAbort = () => {
      try { child.kill(); } catch { /* already gone */ }
      reject(new Error('解压已取消'));
    };
    signal?.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true });

    child.on('error', (error) => {
      signal?.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort);
      reject(new Error(`解压失败：${error.message}`));
    });
    child.on('exit', (code) => {
      signal?.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort);
      if (code === 0) resolve();
      else reject(new Error(`解压失败（退出码 ${code}）${stderr ? `：${stderr.slice(-400)}` : ''}`));
    });
  });
}

/** Remove the private JDK and report what it freed. */
export async function uninstallJdk() {
  if (!existsSync(JDK_ROOT)) return { removed: false, freedBytes: 0 };

  let freedBytes = 0;
  const walk = async (dir) => {
    const entries = await fs.readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).catch(() => []);
    for (const entry of entries) {
      const full = path.join(dir, entry.name);
      if (entry.isDirectory()) await walk(full);
      else {
        const stat = await fs.stat(full).catch(() => null);
        if (stat) freedBytes += stat.size;
      }
    }
  };
  await walk(JDK_ROOT);

  await fs.rm(JDK_ROOT, { recursive: true, force: true });
  return { removed: true, freedBytes };
}

/** Size of the private JDK on disk, for the uninstall preview. */
export async function jdkDirectorySize() {
  if (!existsSync(JDK_ROOT)) return 0;
  let total = 0;
  const walk = async (dir) => {
    const entries = await fs.readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).catch(() => []);
    for (const entry of entries) {
      const full = path.join(dir, entry.name);
      if (entry.isDirectory()) await walk(full);
      else {
        const stat = await fs.stat(full).catch(() => null);
        if (stat) total += stat.size;
      }
    }
  };
  await walk(JDK_ROOT);
  return total;
}
```

`lib/mcp-bridge.js`:

```js
/**
 * Bridge an MCP server's tools into the Host's tool registry.
 *
 * The plugin owns this rather than relying on a profile row, because the row
 * depends on a package the profile may not have — and a missing package fails
 * silently, leaving the workbench showing "0 tools" with nothing to click.
 *
 * Names are prefixed `mcp__<server>__` to match the Host's own MCP client, so a
 * tool that arrives through this bridge and one that arrives through a profile
 * row are addressed identically in a conversation.
 */

import { McpClient, toHostParameters, flattenResult, trimDescription } from './mcp-client.js';

/** Tool descriptors that carry no useful schema still need the required keys. */
function describeTool(client, tool, shape) {
  const bare = tool.name.replace(/^mcp[_-]{1,2}/i, '');
  return {
    name: `mcp__${client.serverName}__${bare}`,
    description: shape.compact
      ? trimDescription(tool.description, shape.maxDescriptionChars)
      : (tool.description ?? ''),
    parameters: toHostParameters(tool, {
      maxDepth: shape.maxDepth,
      compact: shape.compact,
    }),
    output: {
      schema: { type: 'string' },
      render: (value) => (typeof value === 'string' ? value : JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)),
    },
  };
}

/**
 * Register every tool the server exposes, and keep the registry in step with
 * reconnects. Returns a controller the plugin uses for status and teardown.
 *
 * `shape` controls how much of each tool definition reaches the model:
 * `compact`, `maxDepth`, `maxDescriptionChars`. It is on by default because
 * the raw definitions cost about 215k tokens per request — see
 * `compactSchema` in mcp-client.js for the measurement behind that number.
 */
export function attachMcpBridge(ctx, client, { onState, shape } = {}) {
  /** toolName → disposer from ctx.tools.register */
  const registered = new Map();

  const shapeOpts = {
    compact: shape?.compact ?? true,
    // Clamped to at least 1: at depth 0 every parameter collapses to
    // `{type:'object'}`, which describes nothing and would make the tools
    // uncallable. A config typo should not do that.
    maxDepth: Math.max(1, Number(shape?.maxDepth ?? 3)),
    maxDescriptionChars: Number(shape?.maxDescriptionChars ?? 160),
  };

  function clearTools() {
    for (const dispose of registered.values()) {
      try {
        dispose();
      } catch {
        // A failed unregister must not block the remaining ones.
      }
    }
    registered.clear();
  }

  function registerTools(tools) {
    clearTools();

    for (const tool of tools) {
      const descriptor = describeTool(client, tool, shapeOpts);

      const dispose = ctx.tools.register({
        name: descriptor.name,
        description: descriptor.description,
        parameters: descriptor.parameters,
        output: descriptor.output,

        async execute(args) {
          // REA calls can take minutes (Ghidra analysis, firmware extraction).
          // The per-call timeout is generous on purpose; the Host's own
          // timeout is the outer bound.
          const result = await client.callTool(tool.name, args ?? {}, {
            timeoutMs: 600_000,
          });
          const flat = flattenResult(result);
          if (flat.isError) {
            // Throwing is how a tool reports failure to the Host, so the
            // telemetry layer records it as failed rather than successful.
            throw new Error(flat.text || `工具 ${tool.name} 返回错误`);
          }
          return flat.text;
        },

        // REA tools mutate nothing outside their own cache, and two analyses of
        // different artifacts are independent.
        isConcurrencySafe: true,
      });

      registered.set(descriptor.name, dispose);
    }
  }

  client.on('tools', ({ tools }) => {
    registerTools(tools);
    onState?.({ state: client.state, toolCount: registered.size, error: client.error });
  });

  client.on('state', ({ state, detail }) => {
    onState?.({
      state,
      detail,
      toolCount: registered.size,
      error: client.error,
      serverInfo: client.serverInfo,
    });
  });

  return {
    get toolCount() {
      return registered.size;
    },
    get state() {
      return client.state;
    },
    get error() {
      return client.error;
    },
    get serverInfo() {
      return client.serverInfo;
    },
    /** Tool names currently registered by this bridge. */
    listNames() {
      return [...registered.keys()];
    },
    /** Start (or restart) the server and register whatever it exposes. */
    async start() {
      const tools = await client.start();
      // `client.start()` already emitted `tools`, which registered them; this
      // guard covers a restart that resolved before the listener ran.
      if (registered.size === 0 && tools.length > 0) registerTools(tools);
      return registered.size;
    },
    async stop() {
      clearTools();
      await client.stop();
    },
  };
}

/** Build a client from the resolved plugin config. */
export function createMcpClient(config) {
  return new McpClient({
    name: 'rea',
    command: process.platform === 'win32' ? 'npx.cmd' : 'npx',
    args: ['-y', `rea-agents@${config.reaVersion ?? '6.7.0'}`, 'mcp'],
    env: config.providerEnv ?? {},
  });
}
```

`lib/mcp-client.js`:

```js
/**
 * A minimal MCP client, in-process.
 *
 * Why this exists: the workbench ships a `rea-mcp` row that expects
 * `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` to be installed in the profile. A profile that
 * does not have it (or has one whose nine exact-version peers disagree) starts
 * that row, fails, and — because `failOnStartupError` is false — reports
 * nothing. The panel then shows "0 tools" with no way to fix it from the UI.
 *
 * So the plugin speaks the protocol itself. The subset needed is small and
 * stable: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`,
 * `tools/list` and `tools/call`. Everything here is observable — a failure
 * produces a message the workbench can render, which is the actual point.
 *
 * Deliberately NOT implemented: prompts, resources, completions, sampling,
 * roots. REA exposes tools; the rest would be dead code.
 */

import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { EventEmitter } from 'node:events';

/** Protocol revision this client speaks. Servers negotiate down if needed. */
const PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2024-11-05';

/** How long a `initialize` + `tools/list` bootstrap may take. */
const BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;

/** Cap on one response line, so a runaway server cannot exhaust memory. */
const MAX_LINE_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024;

class McpError extends Error {
  constructor(message, { code = null, data = null } = {}) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'McpError';
    this.code = code;
    this.data = data;
  }
}

/**
 * One long-lived MCP server process.
 *
 * Events:
 *   'state'  { state, detail }   lifecycle transitions the UI can render
 *   'log'    { level, text }     stderr lines from the server
 *   'tools'  { tools }           the tool list after (re)connect
 */
export class McpClient extends EventEmitter {
  constructor({ command, args = [], env = {}, cwd, name = 'rea' }) {
    super();
    this.command = command;
    this.args = args;
    this.env = env;
    this.cwd = cwd;
    this.serverName = name;

    this.child = null;
    this.nextId = 1;
    this.pending = new Map();
    this.buffer = '';
    this.tools = [];

    /** idle | starting | ready | error | stopped */
    this.state = 'idle';
    this.error = null;
    this.serverInfo = null;

    this.stderrTail = [];
    this.restarts = 0;

    /**
     * Backoff schedule in milliseconds: five attempts over about 52 s.
     *
     * A cold `npx rea-agents` download on a slow link can take 30 s; a machine
     * that is briefly offline recovers in seconds. This covers both without
     * keeping a genuinely broken install spinning forever.
     */
    this.retryDelaysMs = [2000, 5000, 10000, 15000, 20000];
    // A deliberate stop must not be reported as an unexpected exit.
    this.stopping = false;
  }

  #setState(state, detail = null) {
    this.state = state;
    if (state === 'error') this.error = detail;
    this.emit('state', { state, detail, serverInfo: this.serverInfo });
  }

  /**
   * Spawn, handshake, and pull the tool list. Resolves once ready.
   *
   * Retries on its own: the first run downloads rea-agents through npx, and a
   * cold registry hit fails for reasons that resolve themselves. A terminal
   * error — no interpreter, a spawn failure that cannot change — stops early
   * instead of burning forty-five seconds on retries that cannot succeed.
   */
  async start() {
    if (this.state === 'starting' || this.state === 'ready') return this.tools;

    const delays = this.retryDelaysMs;
    let lastError = null;

    for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= delays.length; attempt += 1) {
      const label = attempt === 0 ? '首次连接' : `第 ${attempt + 1} 次尝试`;
      this.#setState('starting', `${label}：正在启动 rea-agents`);

      try {
        await this.#spawn();
        await this.#handshake();
        this.tools = await this.#listTools();
        this.restarts = attempt;
        this.#setState('ready');
        this.emit('tools', { tools: this.tools });
        return this.tools;
      } catch (error) {
        lastError = error instanceof McpError
          ? error
          : new McpError(error?.message ?? String(error));
        this.#kill();

        // A spawn failure with no interpreter will not fix itself.
        if (lastError.code === 'spawn') break;
        if (attempt >= delays.length) break;

        const wait = delays[attempt];
        // A sub-second backoff would round to "0 秒", which reads as a bug.
        const waitLabel = wait < 1000 ? `${wait} 毫秒` : `${Math.round(wait / 1000)} 秒`;
        this.#setState(
          'starting',
          `${label}失败，${waitLabel}后自动重试（${lastError.message.slice(0, 80)}）`,
        );
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, wait));
      }
    }

    const message = lastError?.message ?? '未知错误';
    this.#setState('error', message);
    throw lastError ?? new McpError(message);
  }

  #spawn() {
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      let child;
      try {
        child = spawn(this.command, this.args, {
          cwd: this.cwd,
          env: { ...process.env, ...this.env },
          stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
          // `npx` is a .cmd shim on Windows; without a shell it ENOENTs.
          shell: process.platform === 'win32',
          windowsHide: true,
        });
      } catch (error) {
        reject(new McpError(
          `无法启动 MCP 进程（${this.command}）：${error.message}`, { code: 'spawn' },
        ));
        return;
      }

      this.child = child;

      const failEarly = (error) => {
        reject(new McpError(
          `MCP 进程启动失败：${error.message}`, { code: 'spawn' },
        ));
      };
      child.once('error', failEarly);

      child.once('spawn', () => {
        child.off('error', failEarly);
        child.on('error', (error) => {
          this.emit('log', { level: 'error', text: error.message });
        });
        resolve();
      });

      child.stdout.setEncoding('utf8');
      child.stdout.on('data', (chunk) => this.#onStdout(chunk));

      child.stderr.setEncoding('utf8');
      child.stderr.on('data', (chunk) => this.#onStderr(chunk));

      child.on('exit', (code, signal) => {
        const wasReady = this.state === 'ready';
        // Reject anything still waiting: its answer will never arrive.
        for (const [, entry] of this.pending) {
          entry.reject(new McpError(
            `MCP 进程已退出（code=${code ?? 'null'}, signal=${signal ?? 'none'}）`,
            { code: 'exit' },
          ));
        }
        this.pending.clear();
        this.child = null;

        if (this.stopping) return;
        if (this.state !== 'error') {
          this.#setState(
            'stopped',
            wasReady
              ? `进程已退出（code=${code ?? 'null'}）`
              : `进程启动后立即退出（code=${code ?? 'null'}），请检查 Node 与 npx 是否可用`,
          );
        }
      });
    });
  }

  #onStdout(chunk) {
    this.buffer += chunk;
    if (this.buffer.length > MAX_LINE_BYTES) {
      this.buffer = '';
      this.emit('log', { level: 'error', text: '响应超出缓冲上限，已丢弃' });
      return;
    }

    // MCP stdio framing is newline-delimited JSON. A partial line stays buffered.
    let index;
    while ((index = this.buffer.indexOf('\n')) >= 0) {
      const line = this.buffer.slice(0, index).trim();
      this.buffer = this.buffer.slice(index + 1);
      if (!line) continue;

      let message;
      try {
        message = JSON.parse(line);
      } catch {
        // A server that prints banners to stdout is not speaking the protocol;
        // surface it rather than failing silently.
        this.emit('log', { level: 'warn', text: line.slice(0, 400) });
        continue;
      }
      this.#onMessage(message);
    }
  }

  #onStderr(chunk) {
    for (const line of String(chunk).split(/\r?\n/)) {
      const text = line.trim();
      if (!text) continue;
      this.stderrTail.push(text);
      if (this.stderrTail.length > 40) this.stderrTail.shift();
      this.emit('log', { level: 'info', text: text.slice(0, 400) });
    }
  }

  #onMessage(message) {
    // A server-initiated request would need its own handler; none is used here.
    if (message.id === undefined) return;

    const entry = this.pending.get(message.id);
    if (!entry) return;
    this.pending.delete(message.id);

    if (message.error) {
      entry.reject(new McpError(
        message.error.message ?? 'MCP 请求失败',
        { code: message.error.code ?? null, data: message.error.data ?? null },
      ));
      return;
    }
    entry.resolve(message.result);
  }

  #request(method, params = {}, timeoutMs = 60_000) {
    if (!this.child) {
      return Promise.reject(new McpError(
        'MCP 进程未运行', { code: 'not-running' },
      ));
    }
    const id = this.nextId++;
    const payload = { jsonrpc: '2.0', id, method, params };

    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const timer = setTimeout(() => {
        this.pending.delete(id);
        reject(new McpError(`MCP 请求超时：${method}`, { code: 'timeout' }));
      }, timeoutMs);

      this.pending.set(id, {
        resolve: (value) => { clearTimeout(timer); resolve(value); },
        reject: (error) => { clearTimeout(timer); reject(error); },
      });

      try {
        this.child.stdin.write(`${JSON.stringify(payload)}\n`);
      } catch (error) {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        this.pending.delete(id);
        reject(new McpError(`MCP 写入失败：${error.message}`, { code: 'write' }));
      }
    });
  }

  #notify(method, params = {}) {
    if (!this.child) return;
    try {
      this.child.stdin.write(`${JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', method, params })}\n`);
    } catch {
      // A dead pipe is reported by the exit handler.
    }
  }

  async #handshake() {
    const result = await this.#request('initialize', {
      protocolVersion: PROTOCOL_VERSION,
      capabilities: {},
      clientInfo: { name: 'dsh-plugin-rea', version: '2.1.0' },
    }, BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT_MS);

    this.serverInfo = result?.serverInfo ?? null;
    this.#notify('notifications/initialized');
    return result;
  }

  async #listTools() {
    const collected = [];
    let cursor;

    // The spec allows pagination; REA returns everything in one page, but a
    // loop costs nothing and a truncated list would be a silent data loss.
    for (let page = 0; page < 20; page += 1) {
      const result = await this.#request(
        'tools/list',
        cursor ? { cursor } : {},
        BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT_MS,
      );
      for (const tool of result?.tools ?? []) collected.push(tool);
      cursor = result?.nextCursor;
      if (!cursor) break;
    }
    return collected;
  }

  /** Call one tool. `args` must already match the tool's schema. */
  async callTool(name, args = {}, { timeoutMs = 600_000 } = {}) {
    if (this.state !== 'ready') {
      throw new McpError(
        this.state === 'error'
          ? `MCP 未就绪：${this.error}`
          : 'MCP 正在启动，请稍后重试',
        { code: 'not-ready' },
      );
    }
    const result = await this.#request('tools/call', { name, arguments: args }, timeoutMs);
    return result;
  }

  #kill() {
    const child = this.child;
    this.child = null;
    if (!child) return;
    try {
      child.kill();
    } catch {
      // Already gone.
    }
  }

  /** Stop the server and reject anything in flight. */
  async stop() {
    this.stopping = true;
    this.#kill();
    for (const [, entry] of this.pending) {
      entry.reject(new McpError('MCP 客户端已关闭', { code: 'closed' }));
    }
    this.pending.clear();
    this.#setState('stopped', '已停止');
  }
}

/**
 * Cut a tool description down to its first sentence.
 *
 * Every tool description here is injected into the system prompt on every
 * request, and REA's run long: a paragraph of provenance, a paragraph of
 * caveats, then the actual contract. The first sentence is the part that says
 * what the tool does; the rest is reference material the model can ask for by
 * reading the offline docs instead of paying for it on every turn.
 */
export function trimDescription(text, maxChars = 160) {
  const raw = typeof text === 'string' ? text.trim() : '';
  if (!raw) return '';
  // 0 or a negative value means "keep the whole description" — that is what
  // someone writing `toolDescriptionChars: 0` intends, and it is cheaper to
  // honour that here than to make the config option mean two things.
  if (!(maxChars > 0)) return raw;
  // Split after a sentence end followed by whitespace, or after a CJK period.
  const first = raw.split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+|(?<=。)/)[0] ?? raw;
  const chosen = first.length <= maxChars ? first : first.slice(0, maxChars).trimEnd() + '…';
  return chosen;
}

/**
 * Cap how deep a JSON Schema is allowed to nest.
 *
 * The reason this exists: `compare_web_captures` inlines an entire HAR-shaped
 * capture structure into its `inputSchema` — 433 properties, 226 `anyOf`
 * branches, 238 descriptions — for one tool. Measured, that single tool is
 * 166 KB of the 773 KB total across 207 tools, and it lands in the system
 * prompt on every single request.
 *
 * Past `maxDepth` a value collapses to its shape alone. That is enough for the
 * model to know something goes there; the exact fields are discoverable from
 * the tool's own error message or the offline docs, and paying 46k tokens on
 * every turn to avoid one round-trip is a bad trade.
 *
 * The recursion treats `properties` as a map of *named* child schemas rather
 * than as one more level of nesting, so `maxDepth: 3` means "three levels of
 * actual parameters", not "two levels plus a map of property names". Getting
 * that wrong is what made an earlier version of this function leave
 * `compare_web_captures` almost untouched: the depth counter ran out exactly on
 * the property-name map, where every key looks like a schema keyword, so the
 * whole subtree was copied verbatim.
 *
 * `required` survives only where `properties` survives, because a required list
 * naming fields that are no longer declared would fail validation.
 */
export function compactSchema(node, maxDepth = 3, depth = 0) {
  if (node === null || typeof node !== 'object') return node;
  if (Array.isArray(node)) return node.map((item) => compactSchema(item, maxDepth, depth));

  // At the limit, keep only what identifies the value's type. Anything else is
  // interior detail that belongs in the docs, not in every request.
  if (depth >= maxDepth) {
    const minimal = {};
    for (const key of ['type', 'format', 'enum', 'const']) {
      if (key in node) minimal[key] = node[key];
    }
    if (minimal.type === undefined && minimal.enum === undefined && minimal.const === undefined) {
      minimal.type = 'object';
    }
    return minimal;
  }

  const out = {};

  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(node)) {
    // `$schema` is a draft identifier, not information about the parameters.
    if (key === '$schema') continue;
    // Nested descriptions are the bulk of the payload and the least load-bearing.
    if (key === 'description' && depth > 1) continue;

    // A map of named child schemas: each name is a parameter, not a keyword.
    if (key === 'properties' && value && typeof value === 'object') {
      const props = {};
      for (const [propName, propSchema] of Object.entries(value)) {
        props[propName] = compactSchema(propSchema, maxDepth, depth + 1);
      }
      out.properties = props;
      continue;
    }

    // Branching keywords hold an array of schemas, not an object.
    if ((key === 'oneOf' || key === 'anyOf' || key === 'allOf') && Array.isArray(value)) {
      out[key] = value.map((branch) => compactSchema(branch, maxDepth, depth + 1));
      continue;
    }

    if (key === 'items' || key === 'additionalProperties') {
      out[key] = compactSchema(value, maxDepth, depth + 1);
      continue;
    }

    out[key] = compactSchema(value, maxDepth, depth + 1);
  }

  return out;
}

/**
 * Turn an MCP tool schema into a JSON-Schema object the Host's `tools`
 * service accepts.
 *
 * MCP uses `inputSchema`, which is already JSON Schema; the Host takes
 * `parameters`. The copy is shallow-normalised because some servers omit
 * `type: object`, and a Host that validates strictly would reject it.
 *
 * `compact` applies `compactSchema` at `maxDepth`. It defaults to on, because
 * the uncompressed set costs about 215k tokens per request; see the comment on
 * `compactSchema` for the measurement.
 */
export function toHostParameters(tool, { maxDepth = 3, compact = true } = {}) {
  const schema = tool?.inputSchema;
  if (!schema || typeof schema !== 'object') {
    return { type: 'object', properties: {}, additionalProperties: true };
  }
  const shaped = compact ? compactSchema(schema, maxDepth) : schema;
  return {
    type: 'object',
    ...shaped,
    properties: shaped.properties ?? {},
  };
}

/**
 * Flatten an MCP tool result into the text the Host renders.
 *
 * REA returns a `content` array of text/image blocks plus `isError`. The panel
 * and the model both need the text; images are reported by name because the
 * Host's tool channel is text.
 */
export function flattenResult(result) {
  const blocks = Array.isArray(result?.content) ? result.content : [];
  const parts = [];

  for (const block of blocks) {
    if (block?.type === 'text' && typeof block.text === 'string') {
      parts.push(block.text);
    } else if (block?.type === 'image') {
      parts.push(`[image ${block.mimeType ?? 'unknown'}${block.name ? ` ${block.name}` : ''}]`);
    } else if (block?.type === 'resource') {
      parts.push(`[resource ${block.resource?.uri ?? 'unknown'}]`);
    }
  }

  if (parts.length === 0 && result?.structuredContent !== undefined) {
    try {
      parts.push(JSON.stringify(result.structuredContent, null, 2));
    } catch {
      parts.push(String(result.structuredContent));
    }
  }

  return {
    text: parts.join('\n\n'),
    isError: result?.isError === true,
  };
}
```

`lib/pip-mirrors.js`:

```js
/**
 * Mirror selection by measurement, not by assumption.
 *
 * The problem this solves: "use the Tsinghua mirror" is folklore, not evidence.
 * Measured on one machine, a 4 MB wheel came down fastest from the official
 * index (592 ms) and slowest from Aliyun (7 s); a 58 MB wheel from the official
 * index stalled outright and had to be cancelled twice. Neither source is
 * reliably faster — it depends on the package, the time of day and the route.
 *
 * So the installer measures. Each candidate mirror is timed on a small, stable
 * file, the fastest is tried first, and a failure falls through to the next.
 * The result is cached for the process, because probing costs real time and the
 * ranking rarely changes within one install.
 */

import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';

/**
 * Mirrors, ordered as a tie-break fallback rather than as a preference.
 *
 * The comment on each one records what was actually observed, so the next
 * person can tell a measurement from a guess.
 */
export const MIRRORS = [
  {
    id: 'official',
    url: 'https://pypi.org/simple',
    label: 'PyPI 官方',
    note: '4 MB 时实测 592 ms（最快）；58 MB 时曾卡死',
  },
  {
    id: 'tsinghua',
    url: 'https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple',
    label: '清华 TUNA',
    note: '4 MB 时 936 ms；58 MB 时曾跑到 72 MB/s',
  },
  {
    id: 'ustc',
    url: 'https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/pypi/simple',
    label: '中科大',
    note: '4 MB 时 1.7 s',
  },
  {
    id: 'tencent',
    url: 'https://mirrors.cloud.tencent.com/pypi/simple',
    label: '腾讯云',
    note: '索引页 308 ms，未测大文件',
  },
  {
    id: 'aliyun',
    url: 'https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple',
    label: '阿里云',
    note: '4 MB 时 7 s（最慢）',
  },
];

/**
 * Probe each mirror's actual throughput.
 *
 * `pip download` is used rather than a raw HTTP fetch so the measurement covers
 * the same path an install takes: index resolution, redirects, and the CDN the
 * wheel is actually served from. Tiny package on purpose — this is a probe, not
 * a benchmark, and it must fit inside a settings page's patience.
 *
 * Results are ordered fastest first. A mirror that errors or times out is
 * dropped rather than ranked last, because "slow" and "broken" need different
 * handling.
 */
export async function rankMirrors(python, { packageName = 'pyelftools', timeoutMs = 25_000 } = {}) {
  if (!python) return { ranked: MIRRORS, failed: [], measured: false };

  const results = await Promise.all(
    MIRRORS.map(async (mirror) => {
      const began = Date.now();
      try {
        const ok = await downloadProbe(python, packageName, mirror.url, timeoutMs);
        if (!ok) return { mirror, ms: null, ok: false };
        return { mirror, ms: Date.now() - began, ok: true };
      } catch {
        return { mirror, ms: null, ok: false };
      }
    }),
  );

  const ranked = results
    .filter((entry) => entry.ok)
    .sort((a, b) => a.ms - b.ms)
    .map((entry) => ({ ...entry.mirror, measuredMs: entry.ms }));

  const failed = results.filter((entry) => !entry.ok).map((entry) => entry.mirror);

  // A machine with no reachable mirror is not a reason to refuse: the caller
  // falls back to the default order and lets pip report the real error.
  return {
    ranked: ranked.length > 0 ? ranked : MIRRORS,
    failed,
    measured: ranked.length > 0,
  };
}

/** One `pip download` into a throwaway directory, with a hard timeout. */
function downloadProbe(python, packageName, indexUrl, timeoutMs) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const child = spawn(
      python,
      [
        '-m', 'pip', 'download', packageName,
        '--no-deps', '--no-cache-dir',
        '-d', probeDir(),
        '-i', indexUrl,
        '--quiet',
        '--disable-pip-version-check',
      ],
      {
        env: { ...process.env, PYTHONIOENCODING: 'utf-8', PYTHONUTF8: '1' },
        stdio: 'ignore',
        windowsHide: true,
      },
    );

    let settled = false;
    const finish = (value) => {
      if (settled) return;
      settled = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      try { child.kill(); } catch { /* already gone */ }
      resolve(value);
    };

    const timer = setTimeout(() => finish(false), timeoutMs);
    child.on('error', () => finish(false));
    child.on('exit', (code) => finish(code === 0));
  });
}

/** A per-probe temp directory; pip cleans the wheels itself after each run. */
let probeCounter = 0;
function probeDir() {
  probeCounter += 1;
  const base = process.env.TEMP ?? process.env.TMPDIR ?? '/tmp';
  return `${base}/rea-mirror-probe-${process.pid}-${probeCounter}`;
}
```

`lib/providers.js`:

```js
/**
 * Analysis-engine bootstrap for the REA bundle.
 *
 * One user action — pressing Install — does everything: resolve the release,
 * download with resume, extract, verify, and report the environment variables
 * REA needs. Nothing is bundled: engines land in a per-user directory at
 * `~/.dsh/rea-engines/<engine>/`, which survives plugin reinstalls and can be
 * deleted to reclaim disk.
 *
 * Three constraints shaped the implementation:
 *
 *  - **Progress is observable.** A 543 MiB Ghidra download is minutes long, so
 *    bytes received, phase, and percent are pushed to listeners rather than
 *    inferred from a spinner.
 *  - **Resumable.** A partial file survives interruption and the next attempt
 *    continues from that offset. Switching mirrors mid-transfer would corrupt a
 *    prefix, so the downloader refuses to do that.
 *  - **Verification, not exit codes.** An engine counts as ready only when a
 *    probe finds its launcher and, for JADX, an archive containing REA's exact
 *    bridge classes. A download that "succeeded" but cannot be used is a
 *    failure.
 */

import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { execFile } from 'node:child_process';
import { accessSync, readdirSync, existsSync, promises as fs } from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { promisify } from 'node:util';

const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile);

/**
 * A transfer stopped by the caller (pause or cancel), as opposed to one that
 * failed on its own.
 *
 * The distinction matters at every layer above: the downloader keeps the partial
 * file, the installer records `cancelled` rather than `failed`, and the job
 * reports `paused` rather than `error`. A plain Error would collapse all three
 * into "something broke".
 */
class DownloadAborted extends Error {
  constructor(detail = '传输已暂停') {
    super(detail);
    this.name = 'DownloadAborted';
    this.aborted = true;
  }
}

/** Version pin shared with cordis.patch.yml. */
export const REA_AGENTS_VERSION = '6.7.0';

/** Where engines are installed. Survives plugin reinstalls. */
export const CACHE_ROOT = path.join(os.homedir(), '.dsh', 'rea-engines');

/**
 * Download sources in preference order.
 *
 * Upstream GitHub is tried first because it is authoritative. Public mirrors
 * follow, because on some networks the release CDN accepts a connection and then
 * sends nothing — measured at a 24-second hard failure versus 1.2-1.8 second
 * mirror responses. A mirror relays bytes already published upstream, so the
 * source of truth does not change.
 *
 * `REA_DOWNLOAD_MIRRORS` prepends caller entries as `<prefix>=<base-url>`;
 * `REA_DOWNLOAD_MIRRORS=off` disables every mirror.
 */
const DEFAULT_GITHUB_MIRRORS = [
  'https://ghfast.top/https://github.com',
  'https://gh-proxy.com/https://github.com',
  'https://ghproxy.net/https://github.com',
];

function candidateUrls(url) {
  const override = process.env.REA_DOWNLOAD_MIRRORS ?? '';
  if (override.trim().toLowerCase() === 'off') return [url];

  const callerRules = override
    .split(/[\s,]+/)
    .map((entry) => entry.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .map((entry) => {
      const index = entry.indexOf('=');
      return index > 0 ? { prefix: entry.slice(0, index), base: entry.slice(index + 1) } : null;
    })
    .filter(Boolean);

  const builtIn = DEFAULT_GITHUB_MIRRORS.map((base) => ({ prefix: 'https://github.com', base }));
  const candidates = [];

  for (const rule of [...callerRules, ...builtIn]) {
    if (url.includes(rule.prefix)) candidates.push(url.replace(rule.prefix, rule.base));
  }
  candidates.push(url);

  const seen = new Set();
  return candidates.filter((candidate) => {
    if (seen.has(candidate)) return false;
    seen.add(candidate);
    return true;
  });
}

async function run(command, args, options = {}) {
  try {
    const { stdout, stderr } = await execFileAsync(command, args, {
      timeout: options.timeoutMs ?? 60_000,
      maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024,
      windowsHide: true,
      ...(options.signal ? { signal: options.signal } : {}),
    });
    return { ok: true, stdout: stdout ?? '', stderr: stderr ?? '' };
  } catch (error) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      stdout: error.stdout ?? '',
      stderr: error.stderr ?? '',
      code: error.code ?? null,
      message: error.message,
    };
  }
}

/**
 * Run a shell script (.cmd / .bat). `shell: true` lets the platform quote the
 * path, which is the only portable way to run a batch file whose path contains
 * spaces such as `C:\Program Files\...`.
 */
async function runShell(command, args, options = {}) {
  const quoted = command.includes(' ') ? `"${command}"` : command;
  const line = [quoted, ...args].join(' ');
  try {
    const { stdout, stderr } = await execFileAsync(line, [], {
      shell: true,
      timeout: options.timeoutMs ?? 300_000,
      maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024,
      windowsHide: true,
      ...(options.signal ? { signal: options.signal } : {}),
    });
    return { ok: true, stdout: stdout ?? '', stderr: stderr ?? '' };
  } catch (error) {
    return { ok: false, stdout: error.stdout ?? '', stderr: error.stderr ?? '', message: error.message };
  }
}

async function exists(target) {
  try {
    await fs.access(target);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

async function isDirectory(target) {
  try {
    return (await fs.stat(target)).isDirectory();
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

function firstLine(text) {
  return String(text).split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => line.trim()).find(Boolean) ?? '';
}

/**
 * Resolve an executable to a runnable absolute path.
 *
 * A GUI-launched Host has no login shell PATH, so bare `which npm` is
 * unreliable. On Windows the runnable sibling of an extensionless `where` hit is
 * the `.cmd`, which is probed beside the running node binary first.
 */
async function which(command) {
  if (process.platform === 'win32') {
    const nodeDirectory = path.dirname(process.execPath);
    for (const name of [`${command}.cmd`, `${command}.bat`, `${command}.exe`]) {
      const candidate = path.join(nodeDirectory, name);
      if (await exists(candidate)) return candidate;
    }
    const probe = await run('where', [command]);
    if (probe.ok) {
      const lines = String(probe.stdout).split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => line.trim()).filter(Boolean);
      const runnable = lines.find((line) => /\.(cmd|bat|exe)$/i.test(line));
      if (runnable) return runnable;
      if (lines.length > 0) return `${lines[0]}.cmd`;
    }
    return null;
  }
  const probe = await run('which', [command]);
  if (!probe.ok) return null;
  return String(probe.stdout).split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => line.trim()).find(Boolean) ?? null;
}

async function findFile(root, predicate, { maxDepth = 6 } = {}) {
  const queue = [{ directory: root, depth: 0 }];
  while (queue.length > 0) {
    const { directory, depth } = queue.shift();
    let entries;
    try {
      entries = await fs.readdir(directory, { withFileTypes: true });
    } catch {
      continue;
    }
    for (const entry of entries) {
      const full = path.join(directory, entry.name);
      if (entry.isFile() && predicate(entry.name, full)) return full;
      if (entry.isDirectory() && depth < maxDepth) queue.push({ directory: full, depth: depth + 1 });
    }
  }
  return null;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Download with progress, resume and mirror fallback
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Move a finished download into place, surviving Windows handle lag.
 *
 * `fs.rename` is atomic and instant on POSIX, but on Windows it fails with
 * `EPERM` while any handle to either path is still open — and an antivirus
 * scanner or a just-closed stream can hold one for a few hundred milliseconds
 * after the bytes are on disk. Retrying briefly covers the common case; copying
 * and deleting covers a lock that outlives the retries, at the cost of one extra
 * pass over the file.
 */
async function renameWithRetry(from, to, attempts = 6) {
  let lastError = null;

  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < attempts; attempt += 1) {
    try {
      await fs.rename(from, to);
      return;
    } catch (error) {
      lastError = error;
      // ENOENT means someone else moved it; nothing to retry.
      if (error?.code === 'ENOENT') throw error;
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 120 * (attempt + 1)));
    }
  }

  // A lock that survives ~2.5 s of retries: copy instead, then drop the source.
  try {
    await fs.copyFile(from, to);
    await fs.rm(from, { force: true });
    return;
  } catch {
    throw lastError;
  }
}

/**
 * Download one URL to a file.
 *
 * @param onProgress called with `{ received, total, percent, bytesPerSecond }`
 *                   whenever enough bytes have arrived to be worth a repaint.
 */
export async function download(url, destination, { maxBytes, signal, onProgress, stallMs = 60_000 } = {}) {
  const temporary = `${destination}.partial`;
  await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(destination), { recursive: true });

  // A caller that aborted before the transfer starts must not open a socket,
  // and must surface the abort rather than reporting an empty download.
  if (signal?.aborted) {
    throw new DownloadAborted();
  }

  // Resume from a previous interruption.
  let resumeFrom = 0;
  try {
    resumeFrom = (await fs.stat(temporary)).size;
  } catch {
    resumeFrom = 0;
  }

  const controller = new AbortController();
  let abortedByCaller = false;
  const abort = () => {
    abortedByCaller = true;
    controller.abort();
  };
  signal?.addEventListener('abort', abort, { once: true });

  /**
   * Set only when the stall timer is what aborted the transfer, so the catch
   * block can tell a dead connection from a deliberate cancel.
   */
  let stalled = false;

  // A stall timer reset on every chunk: a slow-but-progressing transfer
  // survives, a genuinely stuck one fails in a minute.
  let stallTimer;
  const armStall = () => {
    clearTimeout(stallTimer);
    stallTimer = setTimeout(() => {
      stalled = true;
      controller.abort();
    }, stallMs);
  };

  const startedAt = Date.now();
  const startBytes = resumeFrom;

  try {
    armStall();
    const headers = resumeFrom > 0 ? { range: `bytes=${resumeFrom}-` } : {};
    const response = await fetch(url, { redirect: 'follow', signal: controller.signal, headers });

    if (response.status === 416) {
      await renameWithRetry(temporary, destination);
      return { bytes: resumeFrom, resumed: true, note: 'partial file already complete' };
    }
    if (!response.ok && response.status !== 206) {
      throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
    }

    // A server that ignores Range returns the whole body, so the partial prefix
    // must be discarded rather than appended.
    const appending = response.status === 206 && resumeFrom > 0;
    if (!appending) resumeFrom = 0;

    const declared = Number(response.headers.get('content-length') ?? 0);
    const total = appending && declared ? resumeFrom + declared : declared;
    if (maxBytes && total > maxBytes) {
      throw new Error(`download is ${Math.round(total / 1048576)} MiB, over the ${Math.round(maxBytes / 1048576)} MiB cap`);
    }

    const handle = await fs.open(temporary, appending ? 'a' : 'w');
    const hash = createHash('sha256');
    let received = resumeFrom;
    let lastReport = 0;

    try {
      const reader = response.body.getReader();
      for (;;) {
        armStall();
        const { done, value } = await reader.read();
        if (done) break;
        received += value.byteLength;
        if (maxBytes && received > maxBytes) {
          throw new Error(`download exceeded the ${Math.round(maxBytes / 1048576)} MiB cap at ${received} bytes`);
        }
        hash.update(value);
        await handle.write(value);

        // Throttle to ~4 reports/second: enough for a smooth bar, far below the
        // chunk rate of a fast connection.
        const now = Date.now();
        if (onProgress && (now - lastReport > 250 || received === total)) {
          lastReport = now;
          const elapsed = Math.max(1, (now - startedAt) / 1000);
          onProgress({
            received,
            total: total || null,
            percent: total ? Math.min(100, (received / total) * 100) : null,
            bytesPerSecond: (received - startBytes) / elapsed,
          });
        }
      }
    } finally {
      await handle.close();
      clearTimeout(stallTimer);
    }

    if (received === 0) {
      await fs.rm(temporary, { force: true });
      throw new Error('download produced 0 bytes');
    }
    if (total && received < total) {
      // Keep the partial file so a re-run resumes instead of restarting.
      throw new Error(`truncated at ${received} of ${total} bytes; re-run to resume`);
    }

    // Windows refuses a rename while any handle to either path is open, and a
    // finished fetch body can keep one until it is cancelled. Releasing it here
    // is what stops a perfectly complete download from failing with
    // `EPERM: operation not permitted, rename`.
    await renameWithRetry(temporary, destination);
    return { bytes: received, resumed: appending, sha256: appending ? null : hash.digest('hex') };
  } catch (error) {
    // Three different things arrive here as AbortError, and conflating them was
    // a real bug: a stall timeout surfaced as "This operation was aborted",
    // which reads as the user cancelling and names no cause at all.
    //
    //   caller     -> DownloadAborted, partial file kept as the resume point
    //   stall      -> a named timeout naming the stall, partial file kept
    //   otherwise  -> the real error, unchanged
    if (abortedByCaller || (error?.name === 'AbortError' && signal?.aborted)) {
      throw new DownloadAborted();
    }
    if (stalled) {
      throw new Error(
        `下载中断：${Math.round(stallMs / 1000)} 秒没有收到数据`
        + `（已收 ${Math.round(startBytes / 1048576)} MB）。`
        + '已保留部分文件，重试会从断点继续。',
      );
    }
    throw error;
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(stallTimer);
    signal?.removeEventListener('abort', abort);
  }
}

/**
 * Try every candidate URL in order.
 *
 * A truncated transfer stops the loop: its partial file is the resume point, and
 * continuing against a different mirror would append a different source's bytes
 * onto that prefix.
 */
async function downloadFirst(url, destination, options = {}) {
  const attempts = [];
  for (const candidate of candidateUrls(url)) {
    try {
      const result = await download(candidate, destination, options);
      return { ...result, url: candidate, attempts };
    } catch (error) {
      // A pause or cancel must stop the whole chain, not fall through to the
      // next mirror: retrying at a different URL would resume a different
      // source's bytes onto the same partial prefix.
      if (error?.aborted || options.signal?.aborted) throw error;

      if (/truncated/.test(error.message)) {
        let kept = 0;
        try {
          kept = (await fs.stat(`${destination}.partial`)).size;
        } catch {
          kept = 0;
        }
        throw new Error(
          `${error.message}. ${Math.round(kept / 1048576)} MiB 已保留，重新点击安装会从断点继续。`,
        );
      }
      attempts.push({ url: candidate, error: error.message });
    }
  }
  throw new Error(
    `所有下载源都失败：${attempts.map((attempt) => `${attempt.url} → ${attempt.error}`).join('；')}。`
    + ' 可设置 REA_DOWNLOAD_MIRRORS 指向可达镜像。',
  );
}

/**
 * Extract an archive using a tool that ships with the OS. Windows 10+ has
 * bsdtar (which reads zip), with PowerShell Expand-Archive as a fallback for
 * archives bsdtar has choked on.
 */
async function extractArchive(archive, destination, { signal, onProgress } = {}) {
  await fs.mkdir(destination, { recursive: true });
  const lower = archive.toLowerCase();
  onProgress?.({ phase: 'extract' });

  if (process.platform === 'win32') {
    const tar = path.join(process.env.SystemRoot ?? 'C:\\Windows', 'System32', 'tar.exe');
    const useTar = (await exists(tar)) ? tar : 'tar';
    const viaTar = await run(useTar, ['-xf', archive, '-C', destination], { signal, timeoutMs: 1_800_000 });
    if (viaTar.ok) return;

    if (lower.endsWith('.zip')) {
      const viaPowerShell = await run('powershell.exe', [
        '-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-Command',
        `Expand-Archive -LiteralPath '${archive.replace(/'/g, "''")}' -DestinationPath '${destination.replace(/'/g, "''")}' -Force`,
      ], { signal, timeoutMs: 1_800_000 });
      if (viaPowerShell.ok) return;
      throw new Error(
        `解压失败：tar (${firstLine(viaTar.stderr || viaTar.message)}) / `
        + `Expand-Archive (${firstLine(viaPowerShell.stderr || viaPowerShell.message)})`,
      );
    }
    throw new Error(`解压失败：${firstLine(viaTar.stderr || viaTar.message)}`);
  }

  if (lower.endsWith('.zip')) {
    const result = await run('unzip', ['-q', '-o', archive, '-d', destination], { signal, timeoutMs: 1_800_000 });
    if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`解压失败：${firstLine(result.stderr || result.message)}`);
    return;
  }
  const result = await run('tar', ['-xf', archive, '-C', destination], { signal, timeoutMs: 1_800_000 });
  if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`解压失败：${firstLine(result.stderr || result.message)}`);
}

/**
 * Collapse a single top-level directory from the staging area into the final
 * location, so the layout is `.../ghidra/` rather than a version-named folder
 * that changes with every release.
 */
async function normalizeExtraction(staging, finalDirectory) {
  const entries = await fs.readdir(staging, { withFileTypes: true });
  const directories = entries.filter((entry) => entry.isDirectory());

  await fs.rm(finalDirectory, { recursive: true, force: true });
  await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(finalDirectory), { recursive: true });

  if (directories.length === 1 && entries.length === 1) {
    await fs.rename(path.join(staging, directories[0].name), finalDirectory);
    await fs.rm(staging, { recursive: true, force: true });
    return finalDirectory;
  }

  await fs.rename(staging, finalDirectory);
  return finalDirectory;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// JAR inspection
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function jarEntryNames(jarPath) {
  const handle = await fs.open(jarPath, 'r');
  try {
    const { size } = await handle.stat();
    const tailLength = Math.min(size, 65557);
    const tail = Buffer.alloc(tailLength);
    await handle.read(tail, 0, tailLength, size - tailLength);

    let eocd = -1;
    for (let index = tail.length - 22; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
      if (tail.readUInt32LE(index) === 0x06054b50) {
        eocd = index;
        break;
      }
    }
    if (eocd < 0) return null;

    const entryCount = tail.readUInt16LE(eocd + 10);
    let cursor = tail.readUInt32LE(eocd + 16);

    const header = Buffer.alloc(46);
    const names = [];
    for (let index = 0; index < entryCount; index += 1) {
      await handle.read(header, 0, 46, cursor);
      if (header.readUInt32LE(0) !== 0x02014b50) break;
      const nameLength = header.readUInt16LE(28);
      const extraLength = header.readUInt16LE(30);
      const commentLength = header.readUInt16LE(32);
      const nameBuffer = Buffer.alloc(nameLength);
      await handle.read(nameBuffer, 0, nameLength, cursor + 46);
      names.push(nameBuffer.toString('utf8'));
      cursor += 46 + nameLength + extraLength + commentLength;
    }
    return names;
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
}

const JADX_BRIDGE_CLASSES = [
  'com/atxx/jhmcp/JadxSession.class',
  'com/atxx/jhmcp/SessionHolder.class',
  'jadx/api/JadxDecompiler.class',
  'com/google/gson/Gson.class',
  'io/modelcontextprotocol/kotlin/sdk/server/Server.class',
];

async function jarHasReaBridgeClasses(jarPath) {
  let names;
  try {
    names = await jarEntryNames(jarPath);
  } catch (error) {
    return { ok: false, reason: `jar 无法读取：${error.message}` };
  }
  if (!names) return { ok: false, reason: '文件不是可读的 JAR' };

  const set = new Set(names);
  const missing = JADX_BRIDGE_CLASSES.filter((name) => !set.has(name));
  if (missing.length > 0) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      reason: `jar 缺少 REA 桥接类（${missing.slice(0, 2).join(', ')}`
        + `${missing.length > 2 ? ` 等 ${missing.length} 个` : ''}），`
        + ' 这是 jadx-ai-mcp 而不是 jadx-headless-mcp 0.7.1',
    };
  }
  return { ok: true };
}

export async function probeJava() {
  const found = await which('java');
  if (!found) return { present: false, remediation: '安装 JDK 17+ 并把 java 放进 PATH' };
  const version = await run(found, ['-version']);
  return { present: true, path: found, version: firstLine(version.stderr || version.stdout) };
}
```
