```js
const ghidra = {
  id: 'ghidra',
  title: 'Ghidra',
  directory: 'ghidra',
  envVar: 'GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR',
  sizeMb: 543,
  pagesUrl: 'https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/releases',

  async probe() {
    const candidates = [
      process.env.GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR,
      path.join(CACHE_ROOT, 'ghidra'),
      path.join(os.homedir(), 'ghidra'),
      path.join(os.homedir(), 'tools', 'ghidra'),
      '/opt/ghidra',
      '/usr/local/ghidra',
      '/Applications/ghidra',
    ].filter((candidate) => typeof candidate === 'string' && candidate.length > 0);

    for (const candidate of candidates) {
      if (!(await isDirectory(candidate))) continue;
      const launcher = await findFile(candidate, (name) =>
        name === 'ghidraRun' || name === 'ghidraRun.bat'
        || name === 'analyzeHeadless' || name === 'analyzeHeadless.bat');
      if (!launcher) continue;
      return {
        present: true,
        root: candidate,
        launcher,
        source: candidate === process.env.GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR ? 'env' : 'discovered',
      };
    }
    return { present: false };
  },

  /** Ghidra ships one `*_PUBLIC*.zip` per release that covers every platform. */
  async resolve({ signal } = {}) {
    const response = await fetch('https://api.github.com/repos/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/releases?per_page=30', {
      signal,
      headers: { accept: 'application/vnd.github+json', 'user-agent': 'dsh-plugin-rea' },
    });
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`GitHub API 返回 HTTP ${response.status}`);

    const releases = await response.json();
    const release = releases.find((candidate) => String(candidate.tag_name ?? '').startsWith('Ghidra_12.1'));
    if (!release) throw new Error('未找到 Ghidra 12.1.x 发布');

    const asset = (release.assets ?? []).find((candidate) => {
      const name = String(candidate.name ?? '').toLowerCase();
      return name.includes('_public') && name.endsWith('.zip');
    });
    if (!asset) throw new Error(`${release.tag_name} 没有 *_PUBLIC*.zip 资源`);

    return { url: asset.browser_download_url, filename: asset.name, version: release.tag_name, sizeBytes: asset.size };
  },

  async install({ asset, signal, maxBytes, onProgress }) {
    const archive = path.join(CACHE_ROOT, '.downloads', asset.filename);
    if (!(await exists(archive))) {
      await downloadFirst(asset.url, archive, {
        maxBytes,
        signal,
        onProgress: (progress) => onProgress?.({ phase: 'download', ...progress }),
      });
    }
    const staging = path.join(CACHE_ROOT, '.staging', 'ghidra');
    await fs.rm(staging, { recursive: true, force: true });
    await extractArchive(archive, staging, { signal, onProgress });
    return normalizeExtraction(staging, path.join(CACHE_ROOT, 'ghidra'));
  },
};

const jadx = {
  id: 'jadx',
  title: 'JADX',
  directory: 'jadx',
  envVar: 'REA_JADX_MCP_JAR',
  sizeMb: 110,
  pagesUrl: 'https://github.com/1013503897/jadx-headless-mcp/releases/tag/v0.7.1',

  async probe() {
    const configured = process.env.REA_JADX_MCP_JAR;
    if (configured && (await exists(configured))) {
      const valid = await jarHasReaBridgeClasses(configured);
      if (valid.ok) return { present: true, root: configured, source: 'env' };
      return { present: false, note: `REA_JADX_MCP_JAR 无效：${valid.reason}` };
    }

    const directory = path.join(CACHE_ROOT, 'jadx');
    const jar = path.join(directory, 'jadx-headless-mcp.jar');
    if (!(await exists(jar))) return { present: false };

    const valid = await jarHasReaBridgeClasses(jar);
    if (!valid.ok) return { present: false, root: jar, note: valid.reason };

    const cli = await jadxCliLauncher(path.join(directory, 'cli'));
    if (!cli) return { present: false, root: jar, note: '缺少 jadx CLI 启动脚本' };
    return { present: true, root: jar, cli, source: 'cache' };
  },

  /**
   * Two assets: the jadx CLI (the decompiler) and the MCP bridge REA requires at
   * exactly 0.7.1. Both are needed; either alone leaves decompilation broken.
   */
  async resolve({ signal } = {}) {
    const headers = { accept: 'application/vnd.github+json', 'user-agent': 'dsh-plugin-rea' };

    const cliResponse = await fetch('https://api.github.com/repos/skylot/jadx/releases/latest', { signal, headers });
    if (!cliResponse.ok) throw new Error(`GitHub API 返回 HTTP ${cliResponse.status}（skylot/jadx）`);
    const cliRelease = await cliResponse.json();
    const cliAsset = (cliRelease.assets ?? []).find((candidate) => /^jadx-[\d.]+\.zip$/.test(String(candidate.name ?? '')));
    if (!cliAsset) throw new Error('jadx 没有 CLI zip 资源');

    const mcpResponse = await fetch(
      'https://api.github.com/repos/1013503897/jadx-headless-mcp/releases/tags/v0.7.1',
      { signal, headers },
    );
    if (!mcpResponse.ok) throw new Error(`GitHub API 返回 HTTP ${mcpResponse.status}（jadx-headless-mcp）`);
    const mcpRelease = await mcpResponse.json();
    const mcpAsset = (mcpRelease.assets ?? []).find((candidate) => String(candidate.name ?? '').endsWith('-all.jar'))
      ?? (mcpRelease.assets ?? []).find((candidate) => String(candidate.name ?? '').endsWith('.jar'));

    return {
      cli: { url: cliAsset.browser_download_url, filename: cliAsset.name, sizeBytes: cliAsset.size },
      mcp: mcpAsset ? { url: mcpAsset.browser_download_url, filename: mcpAsset.name, sizeBytes: mcpAsset.size } : null,
      filename: cliAsset.name,
      version: `${cliRelease.tag_name}${mcpRelease.tag_name ? ` + ${mcpRelease.tag_name}` : ''}`,
      sizeBytes: cliAsset.size + (mcpAsset?.size ?? 0),
    };
  },

  async install({ asset, signal, maxBytes, onProgress }) {
    const directory = path.join(CACHE_ROOT, 'jadx');
    const cliDirectory = path.join(directory, 'cli');

    if (asset.cli) {
      const archive = path.join(CACHE_ROOT, '.downloads', asset.cli.filename);
      if (!(await exists(archive))) {
        await downloadFirst(asset.cli.url, archive, {
          maxBytes,
          signal,
          onProgress: (progress) => onProgress?.({ phase: 'download', file: 'jadx-cli', ...progress }),
        });
      }
      const staging = path.join(CACHE_ROOT, '.staging', 'jadx-cli');
      await fs.rm(staging, { recursive: true, force: true });
      await extractArchive(archive, staging, { signal, onProgress });
      await normalizeExtraction(staging, cliDirectory);
    }

    if (asset.mcp) {
      const target = path.join(directory, 'jadx-headless-mcp.jar');
      await downloadFirst(asset.mcp.url, target, {
        maxBytes,
        signal,
        onProgress: (progress) => onProgress?.({ phase: 'download', file: 'jadx-mcp', ...progress }),
      });
    }

    const cli = await jadxCliLauncher(cliDirectory);
    return cli ?? path.join(directory, 'jadx-headless-mcp.jar');
  },
};

async function jadxCliLauncher(root) {
  if (!(await isDirectory(root))) return null;
  const preferred = process.platform === 'win32' ? ['jadx.bat', 'jadx.cmd'] : ['jadx'];
  for (const name of preferred) {
    const found = await findFile(root, (candidate) => candidate === name, { maxDepth: 5 });
    if (found) return found;
  }
  return findFile(root, (candidate) => candidate === 'jadx' || candidate === 'jadx.bat', { maxDepth: 5 });
}

const apktool = {
  id: 'apktool',
  title: 'apktool',
  directory: 'apktool',
  envVar: 'REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND',
  sizeMb: 4,
  pagesUrl: 'https://github.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool/releases',

  async probe() {
    const configured = process.env.REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND;
    if (configured && (await exists(configured))) {
      return { present: true, root: configured, source: 'env' };
    }
    const onPath = await which('apktool');
    if (onPath) return { present: true, root: onPath, source: 'path' };

    const wrapper = path.join(
      CACHE_ROOT,
      'apktool',
      process.platform === 'win32' ? 'apktool.bat' : 'apktool',
    );
    if (await exists(wrapper)) return { present: true, root: wrapper, source: 'cache' };
    return { present: false };
  },

  async resolve() {
    // Bitbucket answers HEAD with 403 and cannot be mirrored, so the release is
    // resolved through GitHub, which also serves the asset itself.
    try {
      const response = await fetch('https://api.github.com/repos/iBotPeaches/Apktool/releases/latest', {
        headers: { accept: 'application/vnd.github+json', 'user-agent': 'dsh-plugin-rea' },
      });
      if (response.ok) {
        const release = await response.json();
        const asset = (release.assets ?? []).find((candidate) => String(candidate.name ?? '').endsWith('.jar'));
        if (asset) {
          return { url: asset.browser_download_url, filename: asset.name, version: release.tag_name, sizeBytes: asset.size };
        }
      }
    } catch {
      // Fall through to the pinned URL; the download stage reports real errors.
    }
    return {
      url: 'https://github.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool/releases/download/v2.11.1/apktool_2.11.1.jar',
      filename: 'apktool_2.11.1.jar',
      version: '2.11.1',
      sizeBytes: null,
    };
  },

  async install({ asset, signal, maxBytes, onProgress }) {
    const directory = path.join(CACHE_ROOT, 'apktool');
    const jar = path.join(directory, asset.filename);
    await downloadFirst(asset.url, jar, {
      maxBytes,
      signal,
      onProgress: (progress) => onProgress?.({ phase: 'download', ...progress }),
    });

    // A wrapper gives REA one stable launch path per platform.
    if (process.platform === 'win32') {
      const wrapper = path.join(directory, 'apktool.bat');
      await fs.writeFile(wrapper, `@echo off\r\njava -jar "${jar}" %*\r\n`, 'utf8');
      return wrapper;
    }
    const wrapper = path.join(directory, 'apktool');
    await fs.writeFile(wrapper, `#!/bin/sh\nexec java -jar "${jar}" "$@"\n`, 'utf8');
    await fs.chmod(wrapper, 0o755);
    return wrapper;
  },
};

const frida = {
  id: 'frida',
  title: 'Frida',
  directory: 'frida',
  envVar: null,
  advisory: true,
  sizeMb: null,
  pagesUrl: 'https://frida.re/docs/installation/',

  async probe() {
    const resolved = await which('frida');
    if (resolved) return { present: true, root: resolved, source: 'path', version: null };

    const packageRoots = [
      path.join(process.env.APPDATA ?? '', 'npm', 'node_modules', 'frida'),
      path.join(os.homedir(), '.npm-global', 'lib', 'node_modules', 'frida'),
      '/usr/local/lib/node_modules/frida',
      '/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/frida',
    ].filter((candidate) => candidate.length > 0);

    for (const root of packageRoots) {
      const manifest = path.join(root, 'package.json');
      if (!(await exists(manifest))) continue;
      try {
        const { version } = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(manifest, 'utf8'));
        return { present: true, root, version: version ?? null, source: 'npm-package' };
      } catch {
        // Unreadable manifest is not proof of a usable install.
      }
    }
    return { present: false, advisory: true };
  },

  async resolve() {
    return { packageSpec: 'frida@17.23.2', version: '17.23.2' };
  },

  async install({ signal, onProgress }) {
    onProgress?.({ phase: 'install', message: 'npm install -g frida' });

    const npmCli = path.join(path.dirname(process.execPath), 'node_modules', 'npm', 'bin', 'npm-cli.js');
    const args = ['install', '-g', 'frida@17.23.2'];

    // The npm CLI is a Node script, so run it through the current node binary:
    // no shell, no quoting, no EINVAL from spawning a .cmd.
    const result = (await exists(npmCli))
      ? await run(process.execPath, [npmCli, ...args], { signal, timeoutMs: 600_000 })
      : await runShell((await which('npm')) ?? 'npm', args, { signal, timeoutMs: 600_000 });

    if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`npm 安装失败：${firstLine(result.stderr || result.message)}`);
    return 'global npm prefix';
  },
};

export const PROVIDERS = [ghidra, jadx, apktool, frida];

export async function probeAll() {
  const [java, ...results] = await Promise.all([
    probeJava(),
    ...PROVIDERS.map(async (provider) => {
      try {
        return {
          id: provider.id,
          title: provider.title,
          sizeMb: provider.sizeMb,
          pagesUrl: provider.pagesUrl,
          ...(await provider.probe()),
        };
      } catch (error) {
        return {
          id: provider.id,
          title: provider.title,
          sizeMb: provider.sizeMb,
          pagesUrl: provider.pagesUrl,
          present: false,
          error: error.message,
        };
      }
    }),
  ]);
  return { java, providers: results, cacheRoot: CACHE_ROOT };
}

/**
 * Install every engine that is missing.
 *
 * `onProgress` receives `{ id, phase, percent, received, total, bytesPerSecond }`
 * for each engine in turn. The return value lists one outcome per engine, so a
 * partial success is reported honestly rather than as a single pass/fail.
 */
export async function installEngines({
  only,
  maxProviderDownloadMb = 2048,
  signal,
  onProgress,
} = {}) {
  const selected = only?.length ? PROVIDERS.filter((provider) => only.includes(provider.id)) : PROVIDERS;
  const maxBytes = maxProviderDownloadMb > 0 ? maxProviderDownloadMb * 1048576 : undefined;
  const outcomes = [];

  for (const provider of selected) {
    if (signal?.aborted) {
      outcomes.push({ id: provider.id, title: provider.title, status: 'cancelled' });
      continue;
    }

    let current;
    try {
      current = await provider.probe();
    } catch (error) {
      outcomes.push({ id: provider.id, title: provider.title, status: 'failed', detail: error.message });
      continue;
    }

    if (current.present) {
      outcomes.push({
        id: provider.id,
        title: provider.title,
        status: 'already-present',
        location: current.root,
        source: current.source,
      });
      continue;
    }

    onProgress?.({ id: provider.id, phase: 'resolve', percent: 0 });
    try {
      const asset = await provider.resolve({ signal });
      const location = await provider.install({
        asset,
        signal,
        maxBytes,
        onProgress: (progress) => onProgress?.({ id: provider.id, ...progress }),
      });

      // Verify rather than trust the install call: an engine that cannot be
      // found afterwards is a failure, whatever the download reported.
      const verification = await provider.probe();
      if (!verification.present) {
        outcomes.push({
          id: provider.id,
          title: provider.title,
          status: provider.advisory ? 'advisory-incomplete' : 'failed',
          detail: `已写入 ${location}，但复检仍未发现可用安装`,
        });
        continue;
      }

      outcomes.push({
        id: provider.id,
        title: provider.title,
        status: 'installed',
        location: verification.root ?? location,
        version: asset.version ?? null,
        envVar: provider.envVar,
      });
      onProgress?.({ id: provider.id, phase: 'done', percent: 100 });
    } catch (error) {
      // A pause or cancel is a user decision, not a failure. Reporting it as
      // `failed` would make the panel render an error for a deliberate stop.
      if (error?.aborted || signal?.aborted) {
        outcomes.push({ id: provider.id, title: provider.title, status: 'cancelled' });
        onProgress?.({ id: provider.id, phase: 'paused' });
        continue;
      }
      outcomes.push({
        id: provider.id,
        title: provider.title,
        status: provider.advisory ? 'advisory-incomplete' : 'failed',
        detail: error.message,
      });
      onProgress?.({ id: provider.id, phase: 'failed' });
    }
  }

  return { outcomes, environment: providerEnvironment() };
}

/**
 * Disk usage of one engine directory, or 0 when absent.
 *
 * Reported before an uninstall so the user sees what they reclaim, and after a
 * partially failed install so a broken half-download is visible.
 */
async function directorySize(root) {
  let total = 0;
  const queue = [root];
  while (queue.length > 0) {
    const current = queue.pop();
    let entries;
    try {
      entries = await fs.readdir(current, { withFileTypes: true });
    } catch {
      continue;
    }
    for (const entry of entries) {
      const full = path.join(current, entry.name);
      if (entry.isDirectory()) {
        queue.push(full);
      } else if (entry.isFile()) {
        try {
          total += (await fs.stat(full)).size;
        } catch {
          // A file that vanished mid-walk contributes nothing.
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return total;
}

/** Engines that can be removed safely, with the paths each one owns. */
const UNINSTALLABLE = {
  ghidra: {
    // Only the directory this plugin manages. A Ghidra the user installed
    // elsewhere is never touched: removing a shared tool would break work the
    // plugin knows nothing about.
    paths: () => [path.join(CACHE_ROOT, 'ghidra')],
    // Downloaded archives live here and are safe to drop with the engine.
    cleanup: () => [path.join(CACHE_ROOT, '.downloads'), path.join(CACHE_ROOT, '.staging')],
  },
  jadx: {
    paths: () => [path.join(CACHE_ROOT, 'jadx')],
    cleanup: () => [path.join(CACHE_ROOT, '.downloads'), path.join(CACHE_ROOT, '.staging')],
  },
  apktool: {
    paths: () => [path.join(CACHE_ROOT, 'apktool')],
    cleanup: () => [path.join(CACHE_ROOT, '.downloads'), path.join(CACHE_ROOT, '.staging')],
  },
  frida: {
    // Frida is a global npm package, not a directory this plugin owns. Only
    // report how to remove it; uninstalling another project's dependency would
    // be a destructive surprise.
    npm: 'frida',
    paths: () => [],
    cleanup: () => [],
  },
};

/**
 * Report what an uninstall would remove, without removing anything. The panel
 * calls this first so the confirmation shows a real byte count.
 */
export async function inspectUninstall(only) {
  const ids = only?.length ? only : Object.keys(UNINSTALLABLE);
  const entries = [];

  for (const id of ids) {
    const spec = UNINSTALLABLE[id];
    const provider = PROVIDERS.find((candidate) => candidate.id === id);
    if (!spec || !provider) {
      entries.push({ id, removable: false, reason: '未知引擎' });
      continue;
    }

    const probe = await provider.probe().catch(() => ({ present: false }));
    const owned = spec.paths();
    let bytes = 0;
    for (const target of owned) bytes += await directorySize(target);

    entries.push({
      id,
      title: provider.title,
      // `present` covers both a managed copy and one found elsewhere; `owned`
      // distinguishes what this plugin can actually delete.
      present: probe.present === true,
      managedByPlugin: owned.length > 0,
      location: probe.root ?? owned[0] ?? null,
      bytes,
      npmCommand: spec.npm ? `npm uninstall -g ${spec.npm}` : null,
      removable: spec.paths().length > 0,
      reason: spec.npm
        ? `Frida 是全局 npm 包，请手动执行 npm uninstall -g ${spec.npm} 卸载`
        : null,
    });
  }

  return {
    ok: true,
    entries,
    reclaimableBytes: entries.reduce((sum, entry) => sum + (entry.bytes ?? 0), 0),
  };
}

/**
 * Remove the engine directories this plugin installed.
 *
 * Only paths under `CACHE_ROOT` are touched. An engine found at an external
 * location (an operator-exported `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR`, a system install) is
 * reported but never deleted, because deleting a tool shared with other work
 * would be unrecoverable.
 */
export async function uninstallEngines({ only, signal } = {}) {
  const ids = only?.length ? only : Object.keys(UNINSTALLABLE);
  const outcomes = [];

  for (const id of ids) {
    const spec = UNINSTALLABLE[id];
    const provider = PROVIDERS.find((candidate) => candidate.id === id);

    if (!spec || !provider) {
      outcomes.push({ id, status: 'failed', detail: '未知引擎' });
      continue;
    }

    if (spec.npm) {
      outcomes.push({
        id,
        title: provider.title,
        status: 'external',
        detail: `Frida 是全局 npm 包，请在终端执行 ${spec.npm ? `npm uninstall -g ${spec.npm}` : 'npm uninstall -g frida'}`,
      });
      continue;
    }

    if (signal?.aborted) {
      outcomes.push({ id, title: provider.title, status: 'cancelled' });
      continue;
    }

    const owned = spec.paths();
    let freed = 0;
    const removed = [];

    for (const target of owned) {
      // Defensive: every path must resolve inside the managed cache root.
      const resolved = path.resolve(target);
      if (!resolved.startsWith(path.resolve(CACHE_ROOT) + path.sep)) {
        outcomes.push({
          id,
          title: provider.title,
          status: 'refused',
          detail: `拒绝删除缓存目录之外的路径：${resolved}`,
        });
        continue;
      }
      const size = await directorySize(resolved);
      await fs.rm(resolved, { recursive: true, force: true });
      freed += size;
      removed.push(resolved);
    }

    // Downloaded archives are shared across engines; drop them only when the
    // engine's own directory was actually removed.
    if (removed.length > 0) {
      for (const temp of spec.cleanup()) {
        const resolved = path.resolve(temp);
        if (!resolved.startsWith(path.resolve(CACHE_ROOT) + path.sep)) continue;
        await fs.rm(resolved, { recursive: true, force: true }).catch(() => {});
      }
    }

    const verification = await provider.probe().catch(() => ({ present: false }));

    outcomes.push({
      id,
      title: provider.title,
      status: verification.present ? 'still-present' : 'removed',
      removed,
      freedBytes: freed,
      // A copy found outside the cache survives by design; naming it prevents
      // "I uninstalled it but it still shows READY".
      surviving: verification.present ? (verification.root ?? null) : null,
      detail: verification.present
        ? `插件管理的副本已删除，但在 ${verification.root ?? '其他位置'} 仍有安装，未被改动`
        : null,
    });
  }

  return { outcomes, environment: providerEnvironment() };
}

/** Environment variables the MCP launch needs. Only paths that exist are
 * returned, so a stale value cannot make REA report a configured-but-broken
 * engine.
 */
/**
 * Locate a JDK this plugin installed itself.
 *
 * Synchronous on purpose: providerEnvironment() runs during activation and its
 * result is merged into a plain object, so it cannot await. A missing private
 * JDK simply leaves the system Java in effect.
 */
function findPrivateJdkHome() {
  const root = path.join(os.homedir(), '.dsh', 'rea-jdk');
  try {
    for (const entry of readdirSync(root)) {
      const home = path.join(root, entry);
      const java = path.join(home, 'bin', process.platform === 'win32' ? 'java.exe' : 'java');
      if (existsSync(java)) return home;
    }
  } catch {
    // No private JDK.
  }
  return null;
}

export function providerEnvironment() {
  const env = {};

  /**
   * A private JDK 21 wins over the system Java for the processes this plugin
   * launches. Ghidra 11.2+ refuses to start on 17, and changing JAVA_HOME
   * globally would change every other program on the machine — so the JDK the
   * panel installs is published here, scoped to the child processes we spawn.
   */
  const privateJdk = findPrivateJdkHome();
  if (privateJdk) {
    env.JAVA_HOME = privateJdk;
    env.REA_JAVA_HOME = privateJdk;
  }

  const ghidraRoot = path.join(CACHE_ROOT, 'ghidra');
  for (const launcher of ['ghidraRun', 'ghidraRun.bat', 'support/analyzeHeadless', 'support/analyzeHeadless.bat']) {
    try {
      accessSync(path.join(ghidraRoot, launcher));
      env.GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR = ghidraRoot;
      break;
    } catch {
      // Try the next launcher layout.
    }
  }

  const jar = path.join(CACHE_ROOT, 'jadx', 'jadx-headless-mcp.jar');
  try {
    accessSync(jar);
    env.REA_JADX_MCP_JAR = jar;
  } catch {
    // Not installed yet.
  }

  const apktoolLauncher = path.join(CACHE_ROOT, 'apktool', process.platform === 'win32' ? 'apktool.bat' : 'apktool');
  try {
    accessSync(apktoolLauncher);
    env.REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND = apktoolLauncher;
  } catch {
    // Not installed yet.
  }

  return env;
}

/** Only keys REA consumes, so a config typo is dropped rather than silently dead. */
export function readConfiguredProviderEnv(providerEnv) {
  const allowed = new Set([
    'GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR',
    'REA_JADX_MCP_JAR',
    'REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND',
    'REA_IDA_MCP_CONFIG',
    'REA_KUNA_COMMAND',
    'REA_TSHARK_COMMAND',
    'REA_CAPINFOS_COMMAND',
    'REA_SIGROK_COMMAND',
    'REA_WABT_BIN_DIRECTORY',
    'REA_ADB_PATH',
    'REA_APKTOOL_JAVA',
  ]);
  const env = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(providerEnv ?? {})) {
    if (!allowed.has(key)) continue;
    if (typeof value !== 'string' || value.trim().length === 0) continue;
    env[key] = value;
  }
  return env;
}

export function describeOutcome(outcome) {
  const prefix = `${outcome.id}: ${outcome.status}`;
  if (outcome.location) return `${prefix} (${outcome.location})`;
  if (outcome.detail) return `${prefix} — ${outcome.detail}`;
  return prefix;
}

```

`lib/provision.js`:

```js
/**
 * First-run provisioning.
 *
 * The plugin is useless until three things exist: the MCP server (npx), the
 * analysis engines, and — for the mobile layer — Python packages. Asking the
 * user to press three buttons after `npm install` is asking them to finish the
 * installation themselves.
 *
 * So activation runs this once. Four rules keep it from being intrusive:
 *
 *  - **Order matters.** The MCP server is what makes tools exist at all, so it
 *    goes first and everything else continues in parallel behind it. JDK comes
 *    before Ghidra because Ghidra refuses to start on Java 17.
 *  - **Only what is missing.** Each step probes first; a satisfied machine does
 *    no work and no downloads.
 *  - **Big and optional by default.** Ghidra is 543 MB and only some users need
 *    native analysis, so it is *not* fetched automatically. It is reported as
 *    available with one click. Everything small enough to be unremarkable —
 *    apktool, JADX, Frida, the seven Python packages — is.
 *  - **Never blocks activation.** `apply()` must return so the Host and the GUI
 *    come up; provisioning runs detached and every failure lands in the health
 *    panel with a reason.
 *
 * The report is kept so `/status` can answer "what did the installer actually
 * do", which is the difference between a silent background task and a
 * diagnosable one.
 */

import { installEngines, probeAll, CACHE_ROOT } from './providers.js';
import { probePython } from './tools-mobile.js';
import { PipRunner } from './python-install.js';
import { findJdk21, installJdk } from './jdk.js';

/**
 * Engines fetched without asking.
 *
 * Ghidra is absent because 543 MB is a decision. Frida is absent because its
 * install writes to the global npm prefix — a machine-wide side effect, and it
 * conflicts with any Frida the user already manages. Both stay one-click.
 *
 * What remains here is small, self-contained inside the plugin cache, and
 * required for the Android path to work at all.
 */
const AUTO_ENGINES = ['apktool', 'jadx'];

/** Hard per-step ceilings, in milliseconds. */
const STEP_TIMEOUT_MS = {
  engines: 15 * 60_000,
  jdk: 15 * 60_000,
  python: 10 * 60_000,
};

/**
 * Run an async step with a deadline.
 *
 * The inner work is given an AbortSignal so a download can cancel cleanly rather
 * than being abandoned mid-write; the timeout reports a distinct reason so the
 * panel can say "timed out" instead of a bare failure.
 */
async function withDeadline(item, run) {
  const limit = STEP_TIMEOUT_MS[item] ?? 10 * 60_000;
  const controller = new AbortController();

  let timer;
  const deadline = new Promise((_, reject) => {
    timer = setTimeout(() => {
      controller.abort();
      reject(new Error(`${item} 超时（${Math.round(limit / 1000)}s）`));
    }, limit);
  });

  try {
    return await Promise.race([run(controller.signal), deadline]);
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

/**
 * Steps run in this order; each records its own outcome rather than aborting the
 * chain, because a failed JADX install should not stop the Python packages.
 */
export async function provision({ signal, onStep } = {}) {
  const report = {
    startedAt: Date.now(),
    finishedAt: null,
    steps: [],
    skipped: [],
  };

  const record = (step) => {
    report.steps.push(step);
    onStep?.(step);
    return step;
  };

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  // 1. Engines (small ones only)
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  try {
    const before = await probeAll();
    const missing = AUTO_ENGINES.filter(
      (id) => !before.providers.find((provider) => provider.id === id)?.present,
    );

    if (missing.length === 0) {
      report.skipped.push({ item: 'engines', reason: '全部已安装' });
    } else {
      record({ item: 'engines', status: 'running', detail: `安装 ${missing.join(', ')}` });

      const outcome = await installEngines({
        only: missing,
        maxProviderDownloadMb: 2048,
        signal,
      });

      const failed = (outcome.outcomes ?? []).filter((entry) => entry.status !== 'installed');
      record({
        item: 'engines',
        status: failed.length > 0 ? 'partial' : 'done',
        detail: failed.length > 0
          ? `失败：${failed.map((entry) => `${entry.id}(${entry.reason ?? entry.status})`).join(', ')}`
          : `已装 ${missing.join(', ')}`,
      });
    }
  } catch (error) {
    record({ item: 'engines', status: 'error', detail: error?.message ?? String(error) });
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  // 2. JDK 21 (only when Ghidra is wanted and the system Java is too old)
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  try {
    const jdk = await findJdk21();
    if (jdk.sufficient) {
      report.skipped.push({
        item: 'jdk',
        reason: `已有 Java ${jdk.major}（${jdk.source}）`,
      });
    } else if (!jdk.present) {
      // No Java at all: JADX and apktool also need one, so this is worth doing.
      record({ item: 'jdk', status: 'running', detail: '安装私有 JDK 21' });
      await installJdk({ signal });
      record({ item: 'jdk', status: 'done', detail: '已安装私有 JDK 21' });
    } else {
      // Java exists but is older than 21. Installing a second JDK only matters
      // once Ghidra is wanted, so leave the choice to the user.
      report.skipped.push({
        item: 'jdk',
        reason: `系统 Java ${jdk.major} < 21；装 Ghidra 时需要，可在面板一键安装`,
      });
    }
  } catch (error) {
    record({ item: 'jdk', status: 'error', detail: error?.message ?? String(error) });
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  // 3. Python packages for the MobileRE layer
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  try {
    const python = await probePython();
    if (!python.present) {
      report.skipped.push({ item: 'python', reason: '未找到 Python 3' });
    } else if ((python.missing ?? []).length === 0) {
      report.skipped.push({ item: 'python', reason: '7 个依赖已齐全' });
    } else {
      // probePython already reports import names, which is exactly what the
      // installer accepts; it translates to pip names itself.
      const missingPip = python.missing ?? [];
      record({
        item: 'python',
        status: 'running',
        detail: `安装 ${missingPip.length} 个包`,
      });

      const installer = new PipRunner({
        python: python.command,
        packages: missingPip.map((name) => (name === 'elftools' ? 'pyelftools' : (name === 'z3' ? 'z3-solver' : name))),
      });
      const result = await installer.install({ signal });

      record({
        item: 'python',
        status: 'done',
        detail: `已装 ${result.mirror?.label ?? '镜像'}`,
      });
    }
  } catch (error) {
    record({ item: 'python', status: 'error', detail: error?.message ?? String(error) });
  }

  report.finishedAt = Date.now();
  return report;
}

/**
 * Ghidra is reported, never auto-installed.
 *
 * 543 MB is a decision, not a default. The panel shows it as "可安装" with its
 * size, and `rea_provider_install` can fetch it when asked.
 */
export function ghidraStatus(report) {
  const outcome = report.steps.find((step) => step.item === 'engines');
  return {
    autoInstalled: false,
    sizeMb: 543,
    reason: '需要 543 MB 下载和 JDK 21；桌面面板可一键安装',
    enginesDir: CACHE_ROOT,
    engineStep: outcome ?? null,
  };
}

/** One-line summary for the activation log. */
export function summarize(report) {
  const done = report.steps.filter((step) => step.status === 'done').length;
  const failed = report.steps.filter((step) => step.status !== 'done' && step.status !== 'running').length;
  const skipped = report.skipped.length;
  const ms = (report.finishedAt ?? Date.now()) - report.startedAt;
  return `已装 ${done} 项，跳过 ${skipped} 项，失败 ${failed} 项，耗时 ${(ms / 1000).toFixed(1)}s`;
}

```

`lib/python-install.js`:

```js
/**
 * Per-package Python dependency management.
 *
 * The earlier design offered one "install all 7" button, which answered the
 * wrong question: when a single package breaks (a wheel that will not build, a
 * version conflict), the user needs to see WHICH one, install it alone, and
 * remove it again to retest. So each package is its own row with its own state.
 *
 * `importName` vs `pipName` matters: Python imports `pyelftools` and `z3`, while
 * pip installs `pyelftools` and `z3-solver`. That mismatch is itself a common
 * reason a script still reports "missing" after an apparently successful
 * install, so the table records both.
 */

import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { EventEmitter } from 'node:events';
import { rankMirrors } from './pip-mirrors.js';

/** The packages the vendored MobileRE scripts import. */
export const PYTHON_PACKAGES = [
  {
    // The PyPI package is 'pyelftools' but the module it installs is
    // 'elftools'. Probing the pip name reports it missing after a successful
    // install, which reads as a broken package.
    importName: 'elftools',
    pipName: 'pyelftools',
    label: 'pyelftools',
    sizeMb: 1,
    usedBy: ['so.py'],
    purpose: 'ELF 段/节解析，SO 分析基础',
  },
  {
    importName: 'capstone',
    pipName: 'capstone',
    label: 'capstone',
    sizeMb: 2,
    usedBy: ['so.py', 'emu_run.py'],
    purpose: 'ARM64/x86 反汇编引擎',
  },
  {
    importName: 'keystone',
    pipName: 'keystone-engine',
    label: 'keystone-engine',
    sizeMb: 2,
    usedBy: ['emu_run.py'],
    purpose: '汇编器，模拟执行时修补指令',
  },
  {
    importName: 'lief',
    pipName: 'lief',
    label: 'lief',
    sizeMb: 14,
    usedBy: ['unpack.py', 'so.py'],
    purpose: 'ELF/PE/DEX 读写与重打包',
  },
  {
    importName: 'z3',
    pipName: 'z3-solver',
    label: 'z3-solver',
    sizeMb: 32,
    usedBy: ['cipher_lab.py'],
    purpose: 'SMT 求解器，白盒密码逆向',
  },
  {
    importName: 'unicorn',
    pipName: 'unicorn',
    label: 'unicorn',
    sizeMb: 58,
    usedBy: ['emu_run.py', 'uniharness.py'],
    purpose: 'CPU 指令级模拟执行',
  },
  {
    importName: 'frida',
    pipName: 'frida',
    label: 'frida',
    sizeMb: 152,
    usedBy: ['frida_run.py', 'unpack.py'],
    purpose: '运行时插桩，动态 hook',
  },
];

/** Resolve the pip name for an import name. */
export function pipNameOf(importName) {
  return PYTHON_PACKAGES.find((p) => p.importName === importName)?.pipName ?? importName;
}

/** Resolve the catalogue entry for an import name. */
export function packageInfo(importName) {
  return PYTHON_PACKAGES.find((p) => p.importName === importName) ?? null;
}

/**
 * Where each package lives on disk, how big it is, and its version.
 *
 * One `python -c` for all of them: spawning Python costs ~100 ms on Windows and
 * a per-package probe would make the settings page feel broken.
 */
export async function packageInventory(python) {
  if (!python) return {};

  const names = PYTHON_PACKAGES.map((p) => p.importName);
  const script = `
import json, importlib, os, sys

out = {}
for name in ${JSON.stringify(names)}:
    try:
        m = importlib.import_module(name)
        path = getattr(m, '__file__', None)
        if path and os.path.basename(path).startswith('__init__'):
            path = os.path.dirname(path)
        size = 0
        if path:
            if os.path.isdir(path):
                for root, _dirs, files in os.walk(path):
                    for f in files:
                        try:
                            size += os.path.getsize(os.path.join(root, f))
                        except OSError:
                            pass
            else:
                try:
                    size = os.path.getsize(path)
                except OSError:
                    pass
        ver = getattr(m, '__version__', None)
        out[name] = {
            'version': str(ver) if ver is not None else None,
            'path': path,
            'sizeMb': round(size / 1048576, 1),
        }
    except Exception as exc:
        out[name] = None
print(json.dumps(out))
`;

  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const child = spawn(python, ['-c', script], {
      env: { ...process.env, PYTHONIOENCODING: 'utf-8', PYTHONUTF8: '1' },
      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
      windowsHide: true,
    });
    let out = '';
    child.stdout.setEncoding('utf8');
    child.stdout.on('data', (chunk) => { out += chunk; });
    child.on('error', () => resolve({}));
    child.on('exit', () => {
      try { resolve(JSON.parse(out.trim())); } catch { resolve({}); }
    });
  });
}

/** A paused or cancelled operation must be distinguishable from a failure. */
export class InstallAborted extends Error {
  constructor(reason = 'cancelled') {
    super(reason === 'pause' ? '已暂停' : '已取消');
    this.name = 'InstallAborted';
    this.reason = reason;
  }
}

/**
 * One pip operation, observable.
 *
 * Events:
 *   'progress' { phase, package, done, total, percent }
 *   'log'      { level, text }
 */
export class PipRunner extends EventEmitter {
  constructor({ python, mirror = null }) {
    super();
    this.python = python;
    this.mirror = mirror;
    this.child = null;
    this.aborted = false;
    this.abortReason = null;
  }

  /**
   * Install pip package names.
   *
   * Mirrors are chosen by measurement unless one is pinned: probing showed the
   * official index can be fastest on one package and stall on the next, so a
   * hardcoded preference is wrong roughly half the time.
   */
  async install(packages, { signal } = {}) {
    if (!this.python) throw new Error('未找到 Python 解释器');
    if (!packages?.length) return { installed: [], mirror: null };

    let candidates;
    if (this.mirror) {
      candidates = [{ url: this.mirror, label: this.mirror }];
    } else {
      this.emit('progress', {
        phase: 'probing', package: null, done: 0, total: packages.length, percent: 0,
      });
      const ranking = await rankMirrors(this.python);
      candidates = ranking.ranked;
      this.emit('log', {
        level: 'info',
        text: `镜像测速：${ranking.ranked.map((m) => `${m.label}(${m.measuredMs ?? '?'}ms)`).join(' → ')}`,
      });
    }

    const attempts = [];
    for (const candidate of candidates) {
      if (signal?.aborted) throw new InstallAborted(this.abortReason ?? 'cancelled');
      try {
        const result = await this.#run(
          ['-m', 'pip', 'install', '--progress-bar', 'off', '--disable-pip-version-check',
            ...packages, ...(candidate.url ? ['-i', candidate.url] : [])],
          packages,
          signal,
        );
        return { ...result, mirror: candidate };
      } catch (error) {
        if (error instanceof InstallAborted) throw error;
        attempts.push({ mirror: candidate, error });
        this.emit('log', {
          level: 'warn',
          text: `${candidate.label ?? candidate.url} 失败，换下一个源：${(error?.message ?? '').slice(0, 120)}`,
        });
      }
    }

    const detail = attempts
      .map((a) => `${a.mirror.label ?? a.mirror.url}: ${a.error.message.split('\n')[0]}`)
      .join('；');
    throw new Error(`所有镜像均失败（${attempts.length} 个）：${detail}`);
  }

  /** Remove packages by pip name. */
  async uninstall(packages, { signal } = {}) {
    if (!this.python) throw new Error('未找到 Python 解释器');
    if (!packages?.length) return { removed: [] };
    return this.#run(
      ['-m', 'pip', 'uninstall', '-y', '--disable-pip-version-check', ...packages],
      packages,
      signal,
    );
  }

  /** One pip process, parsed into progress events. */
  #run(args, packages, signal) {
    const total = packages.length;
    let done = 0;

    this.emit('progress', {
      phase: 'starting', package: null, done: 0, total, percent: 0,
    });

    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const child = spawn(this.python, args, {
        env: {
          ...process.env,
          PYTHONIOENCODING: 'utf-8',
          PYTHONUTF8: '1',
          PYTHONUNBUFFERED: '1',
        },
        stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
        windowsHide: true,
      });

      this.child = child;
      let tail = '';
      const stderrTail = [];

      const onAbort = () => {
        this.aborted = true;
        try { child.kill('SIGTERM'); } catch { /* already gone */ }
      };
      signal?.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true });

      const handle = (raw) => {
        const line = raw.trim();
        if (!line) return;

        const downloading = /^Downloading\s+(\S+?)-[\d.]/i.exec(line);
        if (downloading) {
          this.emit('progress', {
            phase: 'download', package: downloading[1], done, total,
            percent: Math.round((done / total) * 100),
          });
        }

        if (/^Installing collected packages:/i.test(line) || /^Uninstalling /i.test(line)) {
          this.emit('progress', {
            phase: 'extract', package: null, done, total,
            percent: Math.round((done / total) * 100),
          });
        }

        if (/^Successfully installed|^Successfully uninstalled/i.test(line)) {
          done = total;
          this.emit('progress', {
            phase: 'verify', package: null, done, total, percent: 100,
          });
        }

        this.emit('log', { level: 'info', text: line.slice(0, 300) });
      };

      child.stdout.setEncoding('utf8');
      child.stdout.on('data', (chunk) => {
        tail += chunk;
        let index;
        while ((index = tail.indexOf('\n')) >= 0) {
          handle(tail.slice(0, index));
          tail = tail.slice(index + 1);
        }
      });

      child.stderr.setEncoding('utf8');
      child.stderr.on('data', (chunk) => {
        for (const line of String(chunk).split(/\r?\n/)) {
          const text = line.trim();
          if (!text) continue;
          stderrTail.push(text);
          if (stderrTail.length > 60) stderrTail.shift();
          this.emit('log', {
            level: /error/i.test(text) ? 'error' : 'warn',
            text: text.slice(0, 300),
          });
        }
      });

      child.on('error', (error) => {
        signal?.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort);
        reject(new Error(`无法启动 pip：${error.message}`));
      });

      child.on('exit', (code) => {
        signal?.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort);
        this.child = null;

        if (this.aborted) {
          reject(new InstallAborted(this.abortReason ?? 'cancelled'));
          return;
        }
        if (code === 0) {
          this.emit('progress', {
            phase: 'done', package: null, done: total, total, percent: 100,
          });
          resolve({ done: packages });
          return;
        }
        const detail = stderrTail.slice(-6).join('\n');
        reject(new Error(`pip 退出码 ${code}${detail ? `：${detail}` : ''}`));
      });
    });
  }

  abort(reason = 'cancelled') {
    this.abortReason = reason;
    if (this.child) {
      try { this.child.kill('SIGTERM'); } catch { /* already gone */ }
    }
  }
}
```

`lib/self-update.js`:

```js
/**
 * Pull the plugin's own repository forward.
 *
 * The plugin cannot replace its loaded modules, so this deliberately stops at
 * "the files on disk are now the new version, restart DSH to load them". It is
 * an updater, not a hot-swapper — claiming otherwise would be a lie the user
 * discovers when nothing changes.
 *
 * What it will not do:
 *
 *   - `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, or anything that discards work. If the
 *     working tree is dirty the update refuses and says which files are in the
 *     way, because the person most likely to run this from a checkout is the
 *     person with uncommitted edits.
 *   - `git pull` on a detached HEAD. There is no upstream to merge, and a pull
 *     there either fails confusingly or creates a merge commit nobody asked for.
 *   - Reinstall dependencies. This package declares none (`dependencies: {}`),
 *     so a pull is the whole update. If that ever changes, `needsInstall` below
 *     is the hook.
 *
 * Progress is a single global state object rather than a job map: two
 * concurrent `git pull`s in one working tree would corrupt the index, so the
 * second caller gets the running state instead of a second process.
 */

import { execFile } from 'node:child_process';
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
/** Package root — `lib/` sits one level down. */
const ROOT = path.resolve(HERE, '..');

/** A `git pull` that has not finished in this long is not going to. */
const GIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;

/** Step identifiers, in execution order. The panel renders these as a list. */
export const UPDATE_STEPS = [
  { id: 'inspect', label: '检查仓库状态' },
  { id: 'fetch', label: '查询上游' },
  { id: 'pull', label: '拉取更新' },
  { id: 'verify', label: '确认新版本' },
];

/** The one update in flight, or the last one that ran. */
let state = {
  phase: 'idle', // idle | running | done | failed | skipped
  steps: [],
  startedAt: null,
  finishedAt: null,
  fromVersion: null,
  toVersion: null,
  behind: 0,
  restartRequired: false,
  error: null,
};

function snapshot() {
  return { ...state, steps: state.steps.map((step) => ({ ...step })) };
}

/** Current or last update state. */
export function selfUpdateStatus() {
  return snapshot();
}

/**
 * Run one git command in the package root.
 *
 * `execFile` with an argument array rather than a shell string: the paths here
 * are known, but keeping the shell out of it means no quoting bug can turn a
 * pull into something else.
 */
function git(args, { timeout = GIT_TIMEOUT_MS } = {}) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    execFile('git', args, {
      cwd: ROOT,
      timeout,
      windowsHide: true,
      maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024,
      encoding: 'utf8',
    }, (error, stdout, stderr) => {
      resolve({
        ok: !error,
        code: error?.code ?? 0,
        stdout: (stdout ?? '').trim(),
        stderr: (stderr ?? '').trim(),
        message: error?.message ?? null,
      });
    });
  });
}

function readVersion() {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'package.json'), 'utf8')).version ?? null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function setStep(id, patch) {
  const index = state.steps.findIndex((step) => step.id === id);
  if (index === -1) {
    state.steps.push({ id, status: 'pending', detail: null, at: Date.now(), ...patch });
    return;
  }
  state.steps[index] = { ...state.steps[index], ...patch, at: Date.now() };
}

function finish(phase, patch = {}) {
  state = {
    ...state,
    ...patch,
    phase,
    finishedAt: Date.now(),
  };
  return snapshot();
}

/**
 * Pull the repository forward.
 *
 * Returns the final state. Every failure path returns a `phase` and a readable
 * `error` rather than throwing: the caller is an HTTP route whose job is to
 * report, not to crash.
 */
export async function runSelfUpdate({ force = false } = {}) {
  if (state.phase === 'running') return snapshot();

  state = {
    phase: 'running',
    steps: UPDATE_STEPS.map((step) => ({ ...step, status: 'pending', detail: null, at: null })),
    startedAt: Date.now(),
    finishedAt: null,
    fromVersion: readVersion(),
    toVersion: null,
    behind: 0,
    restartRequired: false,
    error: null,
  };

  // ── 1. inspect ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  setStep('inspect', { status: 'running' });

  if (!existsSync(path.join(ROOT, '.git'))) {
    setStep('inspect', { status: 'failed', detail: '不是 git 检出' });
    return finish('failed', { error: '插件目录不是 git 仓库，无法自动更新。请用插件管理器重装。' });
  }

  const branch = await git(['rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD']);
  if (!branch.ok || branch.stdout === 'HEAD') {
    setStep('inspect', { status: 'failed', detail: '游离 HEAD' });
    return finish('failed', { error: '当前处于游离 HEAD 状态，没有上游分支可拉取。' });
  }

  const dirty = await git(['status', '--porcelain']);
  if (dirty.ok && dirty.stdout) {
    const files = dirty.stdout.split('\n').slice(0, 5).map((line) => line.trim()).join('、');
    setStep('inspect', { status: 'failed', detail: '有未提交的改动' });
    return finish('failed', {
      error: `工作区有未提交的改动（${files}），已停止以免覆盖。`
        + '先提交或撤销这些改动再更新。',
    });
  }

  setStep('inspect', { status: 'done', detail: `分支 ${branch.stdout}` });

  // ── 2. fetch ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  setStep('fetch', { status: 'running' });

  const fetched = await git(['fetch', '--prune', 'origin']);
  if (!fetched.ok) {
    setStep('fetch', { status: 'failed', detail: fetched.stderr || fetched.message });
    return finish('failed', {
      error: `拉取上游失败：${fetched.stderr || fetched.message || '未知错误'}`,
    });
  }

  const behind = await git(['rev-list', '--count', 'HEAD..@{u}']);
  const behindCount = behind.ok ? Number(behind.stdout) || 0 : 0;
  state.behind = behindCount;

  if (behindCount === 0 && !force) {
    setStep('fetch', { status: 'done', detail: '已是最新' });
    setStep('pull', { status: 'skipped', detail: '无需拉取' });
    setStep('verify', { status: 'done', detail: `当前 ${state.fromVersion}` });
    return finish('skipped', {
      toVersion: state.fromVersion,
      error: null,
    });
  }

  setStep('fetch', { status: 'done', detail: `落后 ${behindCount} 个提交` });

  // ── 3. pull ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  setStep('pull', { status: 'running' });

  // `--ff-only`: if the histories diverged, stop and report rather than
  // producing a merge commit in someone's plugin directory.
  const pulled = await git(['pull', '--ff-only']);
  if (!pulled.ok) {
    setStep('pull', { status: 'failed', detail: pulled.stderr || pulled.message });
    return finish('failed', {
      error: `拉取失败：${pulled.stderr || pulled.message || '未知错误'}`
        + '（本地与上游可能已分叉，需要手动处理）',
    });
  }

  setStep('pull', { status: 'done', detail: pulled.stdout.split('\n')[0] || '已更新' });

  // ── 4. verify ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  setStep('verify', { status: 'running' });

  const toVersion = readVersion();
  state.toVersion = toVersion;

  const changed = toVersion !== state.fromVersion;
  setStep('verify', {
    status: 'done',
    detail: changed ? `${state.fromVersion} → ${toVersion}` : `仍为 ${toVersion}`,
  });

  /*
   * Always ask for a restart, even when the version string did not change: the
   * files on disk are what the next process loads, and a commit that only
   * touched code still needs one. Reporting "no restart needed" because the
   * version was not bumped would leave the user running old modules while
   * believing they had updated.
   */
  return finish('done', { restartRequired: true, error: null });
}

/**
 * Whether the update needs a dependency install afterwards.
 *
 * False today — this package declares no dependencies, so `git pull` is the
 * whole update. Kept as a named export so the day that changes, the caller has
 * one place to look rather than a hardcoded assumption in the route.
 */
export function needsInstall() {
  try {
    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'package.json'), 'utf8'));
    const deps = { ...(pkg.dependencies ?? {}) };
    return Object.keys(deps).length > 0;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

```

`lib/skills-install.js`:

```js
/**
 * Install this plugin's skills where DSH actually looks for them.
 *
 * Why this exists: a plugin's `skills/*.md` inside its own package is inert. DSH
 * discovers skills from `<projectRoot>/.dsh/skills` and `<projectRoot>/.agents/skills`
 * (see `dsh-skill-filesystem`), and nothing scans a plugin's own directory. So
 * shipping skills in the package without installing them produced a plugin whose
 * four skills never appeared in the catalogue — they were only ever reachable if
 * someone copied them by hand.
 *
 * The install is additive and namespaced: files land under `.dsh/skills/rea/`,
 * a manifest records exactly what was written and its content hash, so:
 *   - a second start with unchanged content writes nothing;
 *   - an upgraded plugin replaces only its own files;
 *   - uninstalling removes only files it can prove it wrote.
 *
 * A file the user edited is left alone and reported, because silently
 * overwriting someone's notes is worse than a stale skill.
 */

import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import path from 'node:path';
import os from 'node:os';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const SKILLS_SRC = path.join(HERE, '..', 'skills');

/** Directory name inside `.dsh/skills`. Keeps our files separable from others'. */
const NAMESPACE = 'rea';

/** Manifest file, so uninstall knows exactly what it may delete. */
const MANIFEST = '.manifest.json';

function sha256(text) {
  return createHash('sha256').update(text, 'utf8').digest('hex');
}

/**
 * Locate the project root the way DSH does: walk up from cwd looking for a
 * `.dsh` or `.agents` marker. Falls back to the home directory, which is where a
 * project-less session puts its skills.
 */
function findProjectRoot() {
  let dir = process.cwd();
  const { root } = path.parse(dir);

  for (;;) {
    if (existsSync(path.join(dir, '.dsh')) || existsSync(path.join(dir, '.agents'))) {
      return dir;
    }
    if (dir === root) break;
    const parent = path.dirname(dir);
    if (parent === dir) break;
    dir = parent;
  }

  return os.homedir();
}

/**
 * Every skills root DSH reads, most authoritative first.
 *
 * Two roots exist, and writing only one was a real gap:
 *   <project>/.dsh/skills     source project-dsh, higher rank
 *   <project>/.agents/skills  source project-agents, lower rank
 *
 * The agents tree is the convention the upstream REA project uses for every
 * client it supports, so a skill installed only under .dsh would be invisible to
 * tooling that reads .agents. Writing both keeps the higher-ranked copy
 * authoritative on a name collision while staying discoverable everywhere.
 */
function findSkillsRoots() {
  const project = findProjectRoot();

  return [
    path.join(project, '.dsh', 'skills'),
    path.join(project, '.agents', 'skills'),
  ];
}

/** Read every `.md` in the package's skills directory. */
async function readSources() {
  const sources = [];
  let entries = [];

  try {
    entries = await fs.readdir(SKILLS_SRC);
  } catch {
    return sources;
  }

  for (const name of entries) {
    if (!name.endsWith('.md')) continue;
    const text = await fs.readFile(path.join(SKILLS_SRC, name), 'utf8');
    sources.push({ name, text, hash: sha256(text) });
  }

  return sources;
}

/**
 * Install or refresh skills in every root DSH reads.
 *
 * Returns a report rather than throwing: a read-only filesystem should degrade
 * to "skills unavailable" with the reason, not stop the plugin from loading. A
 * root that cannot be written is reported per root, and the others still get the
 * files — a locked `.agents` tree must not cost the `.dsh` copy.
 */
export async function installSkills() {
  const sources = await readSources();
  if (sources.length === 0) {
    return { ok: false, reason: '包内没有 skills/ 目录', written: [], skipped: [], roots: [] };
  }

  const written = [];
  const skipped = [];
  const roots = [];

  for (const root of findSkillsRoots()) {
    const target = path.join(root, NAMESPACE);
    const manifestPath = path.join(target, MANIFEST);

    let previous = { files: {} };
    try {
      previous = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(manifestPath, 'utf8'));
    } catch {
      // First install here, or a manifest we cannot read: treat as empty.
    }

    try {
      await fs.mkdir(target, { recursive: true });
    } catch (error) {
      roots.push({ dir: target, ok: false, reason: error.message });
      continue;
    }

    let wroteHere = 0;

    for (const source of sources) {
      const dest = path.join(target, source.name);
      const previousHash = previous.files?.[source.name];

      // Already ours and unchanged: nothing to do.
      if (previousHash === source.hash && existsSync(dest)) {
        skipped.push({ name: source.name, root: target, reason: 'unchanged' });
        continue;
      }

      // Present but not recorded by us, or recorded with a different hash: the
      // user may have edited it. Report instead of overwriting.
      if (existsSync(dest)) {
        const current = await fs.readFile(dest, 'utf8');
        if (sha256(current) !== source.hash && previousHash !== undefined) {
          skipped.push({ name: source.name, root: target, reason: '本地已修改，保留用户版本' });
          continue;
        }
        if (previousHash === undefined) {
          skipped.push({ name: source.name, root: target, reason: '同名文件不是本插件写入的，跳过' });
          continue;
        }
      }

      try {
        await fs.writeFile(dest, source.text, 'utf8');
        written.push(source.name);
        wroteHere += 1;
      } catch (error) {
        skipped.push({ name: source.name, root: target, reason: error.message });
      }
    }

    // Record what we own here, so a later uninstall can be surgical.
    const files = {};
    for (const source of sources) files[source.name] = source.hash;
    try {
      await fs.writeFile(
        manifestPath,
        `${JSON.stringify({ installedAt: new Date().toISOString(), files }, null, 2)}\n`,
        'utf8',
      );
    } catch {
      // A manifest we cannot write means a later uninstall asks rather than deletes.
    }

    roots.push({ dir: target, ok: true, written: wroteHere });
  }

  const anyOk = roots.some((root) => root.ok);
  return {
    ok: anyOk,
    reason: anyOk ? undefined : roots.map((root) => `${root.dir}: ${root.reason}`).join('; '),
    // Kept for callers that expect one directory; the first writable root.
    dir: roots.find((root) => root.ok)?.dir ?? null,
    written,
    skipped,
    roots,
  };
}

/**
 * Remove only the files this plugin wrote, from every root it wrote to.
 *
 * A file whose hash no longer matches the manifest was edited after install and
 * is kept, because deleting a user's revision is data loss.
 */
export async function uninstallSkills() {
  const removed = [];
  const kept = [];
  const roots = [];

  for (const root of findSkillsRoots()) {
    const target = path.join(root, NAMESPACE);
    const manifestPath = path.join(target, MANIFEST);

    let manifest;
    try {
      manifest = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(manifestPath, 'utf8'));
    } catch {
      // This root was never installed into.
      continue;
    }

    let removedHere = 0;

    for (const [name, hash] of Object.entries(manifest.files ?? {})) {
      const file = path.join(target, name);
      try {
        const current = await fs.readFile(file, 'utf8');
        if (sha256(current) !== hash) {
          kept.push({ name, root: target, reason: '安装后被修改过，保留' });
          continue;
        }
        await fs.unlink(file);
        removed.push(name);
        removedHere += 1;
      } catch {
        // Already gone.
      }
    }

    try {
      await fs.unlink(manifestPath);
      const rest = await fs.readdir(target);
      if (rest.length === 0) await fs.rmdir(target);
    } catch {
      // Directory not empty because the user added files; leave it.
    }

    roots.push({ dir: target, removed: removedHere });
  }

  return {
    ok: removed.length > 0 || roots.length > 0,
    reason: roots.length === 0 ? '没有安装清单，可能从未安装' : undefined,
    removed,
    kept,
    roots,
  };
}
```

`lib/telemetry.js`:

```js
/**
 * Runtime telemetry for the REA workbench.
 *
 * What this records and why:
 *
 *   - **Every tool call** the agent makes, REA or otherwise, with name, duration,
 *     outcome, and error message. That answers "where did it break", which no
 *     amount of engine-status display can.
 *   - **MCP health** as observed from outside the client: whether the `rea`
 *     server's tools are registered in this process and how many.
 *   - **A bounded ring buffer**. An agent can issue hundreds of calls in one
 *     turn; keeping all of them would grow without limit. The buffer keeps the
 *     most recent N and counts what it dropped, so the panel never claims to
 *     show "everything".
 *
 * Design constraints:
 *
 *  - Recording must never break a tool call. Every hook is wrapped so a throw in
 *    telemetry is swallowed and the real tool result survives.
 *  - Errors are aggregated by a normalized key (tool + error shape), so 40
 *    identical failures read as one row with a count instead of 40 lines.
 *  - Nothing here is persisted. This is live operational state, cleared when the
 *    Host restarts, which is the honest scope of "what is happening now".
 */

import { EventEmitter } from 'node:events';
import { explainError, toolLabel } from './error-explain.js';

/** Rows kept for the message stream. Older rows are dropped and counted. */
const MAX_ENTRIES = 500;

/** Distinct error groups tracked at once. */
const MAX_ERROR_GROUPS = 100;

/** Per-tool rolling statistics. */
const MAX_TOOL_STATS = 200;

/**
 * Normalize an error message into a grouping key.
 *
 * Variable data is stripped so two failures of the same kind group together:
 * a port number, a path, a byte offset, a GUID, an address. Without this every
 * occurrence of one bug looks like a different bug.
 */
export function normalizeErrorKey(message) {
  let text = String(message ?? '');

  // Addresses and identifiers first: they would otherwise look like numbers to
  // the later rules.
  text = text.replace(/0x[0-9a-f]+/gi, '0x#');
  text = text.replace(/[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}/gi, '<uuid>');

  /**
   * Windows paths may contain spaces (`C:\Program Files\...`), so a single
   * whitespace-delimited token stops at `Program`. The rule is: a drive letter,
   * then everything up to a quoted boundary, a line break, or a trailing
   * all-caps error code — that code is the diagnostic and must survive.
   */
  text = text.replace(/[A-Za-z]:\\[^\r\n"'`|]*?(?=\s+[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{2,}\b|["'`\r\n|]|$)/g, '<path>');
  // A path with no trailing error word, ending at whitespace.
  text = text.replace(/[A-Za-z]:\\[^\s"'`|]*/g, '<path>');

  // POSIX paths need at least one separator, so a lone `/` is left alone.
  text = text.replace(/\/(?:[^\s'"`]+\/?)+/g, '<path>');

  // Remaining long numbers are offsets, ports and ids, never diagnostic.
  text = text.replace(/\b\d{4,}\b/g, '#');

  // A tool error is often a JSON payload; 200 characters cut it mid-word and
  // hid the actual cause. The panel wraps and clamps instead.
  return text.slice(0, 600);
}

/** Shorten a value for display without destroying its meaning. */
function truncate(text, max = 400) {
  const value = String(text ?? '');
  return value.length <= max ? value : `${value.slice(0, max)}…`;
}

/**
 * Extract a readable error from whatever a failed tool returned.
 *
 * Tool failures arrive as a materialized result with content blocks, so the text
 * is buried in there rather than being an Error instance.
 */
function extractFailure(result) {
  if (!result || typeof result !== 'object') return null;

  const isError = result.isError === true;
  if (!isError) return null;

  // Prefer the structured failure reason over a rendered block.
  const reason = result.error?.message ?? result.error?.info?.reason;
  if (typeof reason === 'string' && reason.length > 0) {
    return { message: reason, code: result.error?.info?.code ?? null };
  }

  const blocks = Array.isArray(result.content) ? result.content : [];
  const text = blocks
    .filter((block) => block?.type === 'text' && typeof block.text === 'string')
    .map((block) => block.text)
    .join('\n')
    .trim();

  if (text.length > 0) return { message: truncate(text, 2000), code: null };
  return { message: '工具返回错误，但没有错误文本', code: null };
}

export class ReaTelemetry extends EventEmitter {
  constructor({ maxEntries = MAX_ENTRIES } = {}) {
    super();
    // Many panels may subscribe; the default of 10 would warn past that.
    this.setMaxListeners(50);

    this.maxEntries = maxEntries;
    /** Newest first. */
    this.entries = [];
    /** How many rows fell off the end of the buffer. */
    this.dropped = 0;
    /** Monotonic id so a client can tell new rows from old. */
    this.nextSeq = 1;

    /** Aggregated error groups keyed by `tool::normalizedMessage`. */
    this.errorGroups = new Map();
    /** Per-tool counters. */
    this.toolStats = new Map();

    this.startedAt = Date.now();
    this.counts = {
      total: 0,
      failed: 0,
      rea: 0,
      reaFailed: 0,
      other: 0,
      otherFailed: 0,
    };
    /**
     * Response time is tracked per group, because the two have nothing in
     * common: a REA analysis runs for seconds and a `read` for milliseconds.
     * Averaging them produced a meaningless "680 ms".
     */
    this.ms = {
      rea: { total: 0, calls: 0 },
      other: { total: 0, calls: 0 },
    };
    this.totalMs = 0;
    this.timedCalls = 0;
  }

  /** True when a tool name belongs to the REA server. */
  static isReaTool(name) {
    return typeof name === 'string' && name.startsWith('mcp__rea__');
  }

  /**
   * Record one completed tool call.
   *
   * `failure` is the extracted failure or null; `durationMs` may be null when
   * the start timestamp was unavailable, which is reported rather than guessed.
   */
  record({ name, durationMs, failure, meta }) {
    const seq = this.nextSeq;
    this.nextSeq += 1;

    const isRea = ReaTelemetry.isReaTool(name);
    const failed = failure !== null;

    this.counts.total += 1;
    if (failed) this.counts.failed += 1;

    if (isRea) {
      this.counts.rea += 1;
      if (failed) this.counts.reaFailed += 1;
    } else {
      this.counts.other += 1;
      if (failed) this.counts.otherFailed += 1;
    }

    /**
     * Per-group timing sums. Kept as running accumulators rather than derived
     * from the ring buffer: the buffer drops old entries and its average would
     * drift away from the true figure.
     */
    const bucket = isRea ? this.ms.rea : this.ms.other;
    if (typeof durationMs === 'number' && Number.isFinite(durationMs)) {
      bucket.total += durationMs;
      bucket.calls += 1;
      this.totalMs += durationMs;
      this.timedCalls += 1;
    }

    const entry = {
      seq,
      at: Date.now(),
      tool: name,
      rea: isRea,
      durationMs: typeof durationMs === 'number' && Number.isFinite(durationMs) ? Math.round(durationMs) : null,
      ok: !failed,
      error: failure ? truncate(failure.message, 600) : null,
      errorCode: failure?.code ?? null,
      meta: meta ?? null,
    };

    this.entries.unshift(entry);
    if (this.entries.length > this.maxEntries) {
      const removed = this.entries.length - this.maxEntries;
      this.entries.length = this.maxEntries;
      this.dropped += removed;
    }

    this.#updateToolStats(name, entry);
    if (failed) this.#updateErrorGroups(name, failure);

    // Live subscribers get the row immediately; the buffer is the replay source
    // for a panel that opens later.
    this.emit('entry', entry);
    return entry;
  }

  #updateToolStats(name, entry) {
    const current = this.toolStats.get(name) ?? {
      tool: name,
      rea: entry.rea,
      calls: 0,
      failures: 0,
      totalMs: 0,
      maxMs: 0,
      lastAt: 0,
      lastError: null,
    };

    current.calls += 1;
    if (!entry.ok) {
      current.failures += 1;
      current.lastError = entry.error;
    }
    if (entry.durationMs !== null) {
      current.totalMs += entry.durationMs;
      current.maxMs = Math.max(current.maxMs, entry.durationMs);
    }
    current.lastAt = entry.at;
    this.toolStats.set(name, current);

    // Bound the map: an unusual process could see thousands of dynamic names.
    if (this.toolStats.size > MAX_TOOL_STATS) {
      const oldest = [...this.toolStats.values()].sort((a, b) => a.lastAt - b.lastAt)[0];
      if (oldest) this.toolStats.delete(oldest.tool);
    }
  }

  #updateErrorGroups(name, failure) {
    const key = `${name}::${normalizeErrorKey(failure.message)}`;

    /**
     * The panel rendered the raw English message, which is the one thing a
     * non-programmer cannot act on. The explanation is attached here rather
     * than only in the client so the same Chinese reading is available to every
     * consumer of `/metrics`, including an agent reading the API.
     *
     * `null` when no rule matches: an unknown error keeps its original text
     * rather than being forced into a wrong category.
     */
    const current = this.errorGroups.get(key) ?? {
      key,
      tool: name,
      toolLabel: toolLabel(name),
      message: truncate(failure.message, 300),
      explanation: explainError(failure.message),
      count: 0,
      firstAt: Date.now(),
      lastAt: 0,
    };
    current.count += 1;
    current.lastAt = Date.now();
    this.errorGroups.set(key, current);

    if (this.errorGroups.size > MAX_ERROR_GROUPS) {
      const oldest = [...this.errorGroups.values()].sort((a, b) => a.lastAt - b.lastAt)[0];
      if (oldest) this.errorGroups.delete(oldest.key);
    }
  }

  /** Rows after `sinceSeq`, newest first, for an incremental panel sync. */
  since(sinceSeq = 0) {
    return this.entries.filter((entry) => entry.seq > sinceSeq);
  }

  /**
   * Aggregate view for the panel's summary cards.
   *
   * Slowest and most-failing tools are ranked so a performance or reliability
   * problem is visible without reading the stream.
   */
  snapshot({ entryLimit = 200 } = {}) {
    const tools = [...this.toolStats.values()].map((stat) => ({
      ...stat,
      avgMs: stat.calls > 0 ? Math.round(stat.totalMs / stat.calls) : null,
      failureRate: stat.calls > 0 ? stat.failures / stat.calls : 0,
    }));

    return {
      startedAt: this.startedAt,
      uptimeMs: Date.now() - this.startedAt,
      counts: {
        ...this.counts,
        // Two rates and two averages, never one blended figure: a REA call and
        // an \`edit\` have different success shapes and durations, and combining
        // them produced a number that described neither.
        reaRate: this.counts.rea > 0
          ? (this.counts.rea - this.counts.reaFailed) / this.counts.rea
          : null,
        otherRate: this.counts.other > 0
          ? (this.counts.other - this.counts.otherFailed) / this.counts.other
          : null,
        reaAvgMs: this.ms.rea.calls > 0
          ? Math.round(this.ms.rea.total / this.ms.rea.calls)
          : null,
        otherAvgMs: this.ms.other.calls > 0
          ? Math.round(this.ms.other.total / this.ms.other.calls)
          : null,
        avgMs: this.timedCalls > 0 ? Math.round(this.totalMs / this.timedCalls) : null,
      },
      buffered: this.entries.length,
      dropped: this.dropped,
      maxEntries: this.maxEntries,
      entries: this.entries.slice(0, entryLimit),
      errors: [...this.errorGroups.values()].sort((a, b) => b.lastAt - a.lastAt),
      slowest: [...tools]
        .filter((tool) => tool.avgMs !== null && tool.calls >= 1)
        .sort((a, b) => b.avgMs - a.avgMs)
        .slice(0, 8),
      failing: [...tools]
        .filter((tool) => tool.failures > 0)
        .sort((a, b) => b.failures - a.failures)
        .slice(0, 8),
      reaTools: tools.filter((tool) => tool.rea).length,
    };
  }

  /** Clear counters. The stream keeps its rows unless `clearEntries` is set. */
  reset({ clearEntries = true } = {}) {
    if (clearEntries) {
      this.entries = [];
      this.dropped = 0;
    }
    this.errorGroups.clear();
    this.toolStats.clear();
    this.counts = { total: 0, failed: 0, rea: 0, reaFailed: 0 };
    this.totalMs = 0;
    this.timedCalls = 0;
    this.startedAt = Date.now();
  }
}

/**
 * Attach telemetry to the Host event bus.
 *
 * `tools/execute` is a waterfall that wraps every dispatch, so it supplies the
 * start time; `tools/result` is the frozen final outcome, so it supplies the
 * verdict. Pairing them by call id is what yields a duration.
 *
 * Every callback is guarded: a telemetry bug must never turn a working tool call
 * into a failure.
 */
export function attachTelemetry(ctx, telemetry) {
  const started = new Map();

  const disposeStart = ctx.on('tools/execute', (exec, next) => {
    try {
      const id = String(exec?.callId ?? '');
      if (id) started.set(id, Date.now());
    } catch {
      // Never let bookkeeping break the dispatch.
    }
    return next();
  });

  const disposeResult = ctx.on('tools/result', (exec, result) => {
    try {
      const id = String(exec?.callId ?? '');
      const beganAt = id ? started.get(id) : undefined;
      if (id) started.delete(id);

      telemetry.record({
        name: String(exec?.name ?? 'unknown'),
        durationMs: beganAt ? Date.now() - beganAt : null,
        failure: extractFailure(result),
      });
    } catch {
      // As above: telemetry is observational only.
    }
  });

  // Restrict the start map so an unpaired dispatch cannot leak forever.
  const sweep = setInterval(() => {
    if (started.size > 2000) {
      const keep = [...started.entries()].slice(-1000);
      started.clear();
      for (const [key, value] of keep) started.set(key, value);
    }
  }, 60_000);
  if (typeof sweep.unref === 'function') sweep.unref();

  return () => {
    clearInterval(sweep);
    disposeStart();
    disposeResult();
  };
}
```
