`lib/tool-cli.js`:

```js
/**
 * The `rea` CLI, wrapped as one Host tool.
 *
 * Why a CLI tool at all when the MCP bridge already exposes 207 tools: cost.
 * Every MCP tool ships its full JSON Schema into the prompt, and a single
 * `tools/list` result is tens of thousands of tokens. The CLI is a thin command
 * surface over the same engine with two properties an agent wants:
 *
 *   --format json       machine-readable output instead of prose
 *   --filter-output     project only the keys that matter, so a 40 KB Evidence
 *                       bundle becomes the 400 bytes the question needed
 *
 * So this is a *budget* tool, not a replacement: the MCP path stays for
 * interactive multi-step work, and this one is for a single question answered
 * cheaply. It is also the only path that can read `--llms`, the manifest REA
 * publishes specifically for models.
 */

import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';

/** How long a CLI call may run. Ghidra analysis is the slow end. */
const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 600_000;

/**
 * Commands safe to expose as a free-form string.
 *
 * A whitelist rather than "anything the CLI accepts": the argument becomes part
 * of a command line, and a typo should fail here rather than inside a spawned
 * process with unexpected flags.
 */
const SAFE_COMMAND = /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/;

/** Strip anything that could break out of the argv array. */
function assertCommand(command) {
  if (!SAFE_COMMAND.test(command)) {
    throw new Error(`非法的 rea 子命令：${command}（只允许小写字母、数字和连字符）`);
  }
  return command;
}

/**
 * Run `rea <args>` and return stdout.
 *
 * Arguments are passed as an argv array with no shell, so a path containing
 * spaces or quotes is a value, never a second command.
 */
function runRea(args, { timeoutMs = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, cwd, signal } = {}) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const command = process.platform === 'win32' ? 'npx.cmd' : 'npx';
    const fullArgs = ['-y', `rea-agents@${runRea.version ?? '6.7.0'}`, ...args];

    const child = spawn(command, fullArgs, {
      cwd,
      env: { ...process.env, PYTHONIOENCODING: 'utf-8', PYTHONUTF8: '1' },
      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
      windowsHide: true,
      // npx is a .cmd shim on Windows and needs a shell to resolve.
      shell: process.platform === 'win32',
    });

    let stdout = '';
    let stderr = '';
    let killed = false;

    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      killed = true;
      try { child.kill(); } catch { /* already gone */ }
    }, timeoutMs);

    const onAbort = () => {
      killed = true;
      try { child.kill(); } catch { /* already gone */ }
    };
    signal?.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true });

    child.stdout.setEncoding('utf8');
    child.stderr.setEncoding('utf8');
    child.stdout.on('data', (chunk) => { stdout += chunk; });
    child.stderr.on('data', (chunk) => { stderr += chunk; });

    child.on('error', (error) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      signal?.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort);
      reject(new Error(`无法启动 rea CLI：${error.message}`));
    });

    child.on('exit', (code) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      signal?.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort);
      if (killed) {
        reject(new Error(`rea ${args[0] ?? ''} 超时（${Math.round(timeoutMs / 1000)}s）已终止`));
        return;
      }
      resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout, stderr });
    });
  });
}

/**
 * Build the CLI tool.
 *
 * One tool with a `command` argument rather than 155 separate tools: the CLI is
 * discoverable through `--llms`, and 155 schemas in the prompt would cost more
 * than the MCP bridge it is meant to save.
 */
export function buildCliTool(config = {}) {
  const defaultTimeout = Number(config.cliTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS);

  return {
    name: 'rea_cli',
    description:
      'Run the rea CLI directly. Cheaper than the MCP tools for a single question: '
      + 'use --format json for machine output and --filter-output to keep only the keys you need. '
      + 'Discover commands with action=commands, and read the full agent manifest with action=manifest. '
      + 'Every command from the MCP surface is available here; prefer this when the answer is one call '
      + 'deep and the full Evidence envelope is not needed.',
    parameters: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        action: {
          type: 'string',
          enum: ['run', 'commands', 'manifest', 'schema'],
          description:
            'run=执行子命令；commands=列出全部命令（轻量）；'
            + 'manifest=打印完整 LLM 清单（--llms，含每个命令的参数）；'
            + 'schema=查某个命令的 JSON Schema',
        },
        command: {
          type: 'string',
          description: 'action=run 时要执行的 rea 子命令，如 analyze、inspect_native_load_image',
        },
        args: {
          type: 'array',
          items: { type: 'string' },
          description:
            '子命令的参数数组，按 CLI 顺序原样传递。'
            + '例：["E:/sample.exe", "--format", "json"]',
        },
        format: {
          type: 'string',
          enum: ['json', 'toon', 'yaml', 'md', 'jsonl'],
          description: '输出格式（默认由 CLI 决定；json 最省 token 且易解析）',
        },
        filter: {
          type: 'string',
          description:
            '只保留指定键路径，逗号分隔。例："identity,pseudocode"，'
            + '可大幅减少输出体积',
        },
        tokenLimit: {
          type: 'number',
          description: '限制输出 token 数（CLI 的 --token-limit）',
        },
        timeoutMs: {
          type: 'number',
          description: '超时毫秒数，缺省 600000（10 分钟，Ghidra 分析可能很慢）',
        },
      },
      required: ['action'],
    },
    async execute(input = {}) {
      const action = String(input.action ?? 'run');

      if (action === 'commands') {
        const result = await runRea(['--help'], { timeoutMs: 60_000 });
        const commands = [...result.stdout.matchAll(/^ {2}([a-z][a-z0-9-]+)\s{2,}/gm)]
          .map((m) => m[1]);
        return `${commands.length} 个命令：\n\n${commands.join('\n')}`;
      }

      if (action === 'manifest') {
        const result = await runRea(['--llms'], { timeoutMs: 60_000 });
        if (result.code !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr || 'rea --llms 失败');
        return result.stdout;
      }

      if (action === 'schema') {
        const target = String(input.command ?? '');
        if (!target) throw new Error('action=schema 需要 command 参数');
        const result = await runRea([assertCommand(target), '--schema'], { timeoutMs: 60_000 });
        if (result.code !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr || `rea ${target} --schema 失败`);
        return result.stdout;
      }

      // action === 'run'
      const target = String(input.command ?? '');
      if (!target) throw new Error('action=run 需要 command 参数');

      const argv = [assertCommand(target)];

      // Spread caller args verbatim; they are values, not shell words.
      if (Array.isArray(input.args)) {
        for (const value of input.args) argv.push(String(value));
      }

      if (input.format) argv.push('--format', String(input.format));
      if (input.filter) argv.push('--filter-output', String(input.filter));
      if (input.tokenLimit) argv.push('--token-limit', String(input.tokenLimit));

      const timeoutMs = Number(input.timeoutMs ?? defaultTimeout);
      const result = await runRea(argv, { timeoutMs });

      if (result.code !== 0) {
        const detail = (result.stderr || result.stdout || '').trim();
        throw new Error(`rea ${target} 退出码 ${result.code}${detail ? `：\n${detail.slice(0, 1500)}` : ''}`);
      }

      return result.stdout.trim() || '(命令无输出)';
    },
  };
}

/** Let the factory pin the upstream version without a second config path. */
export function setCliVersion(version) {
  runRea.version = version;
}
```

`lib/tool-docs.js`:

```js
/**
 * Documentation index for the REA project.
 *
 * 72 documents totalling 1.23 MB. Putting them in the prompt is not an option,
 * and neither is putting all 72 titles: the point is that a model should read
 * the *one* document that answers its question, which means it needs a map
 * cheap enough to always be affordable.
 *
 * So this module ships a compact index — topic, one-line summary, and the exact
 * keys a caller would search for — and fetches document bodies on demand from a
 * pinned commit. Nothing is downloaded until asked for.
 *
 * The index is generated, not hand-maintained: `scripts/gen-doc-index.mjs`
 * reads the project's `docs/` directory at a pinned ref and writes
 * `vendor/rea-docs/index.json`. Re-running it is how the index follows an
 * upstream release.
 */

import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import path from 'node:path';
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const INDEX_PATH = path.join(HERE, '..', 'vendor', 'rea-docs', 'index.json');
const DOCS_PATH = path.join(HERE, '..', 'vendor', 'rea-docs', 'docs');


/** Whether the documentation bodies are packaged (offline-ready). */
export function docsAreVendored() {
  return existsSync(path.join(HERE, '..', 'vendor', 'rea-docs', 'VENDORED'));
}

/** Load the generated index. Returns null when the vendor tree is absent. */
export async function loadDocIndex() {
  try {
    const raw = await fs.readFile(INDEX_PATH, 'utf8');
    return JSON.parse(raw);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/**
 * Search the index.
 *
 * Substring matching over name + summary + keywords, ranked by where the match
 * lands: a name hit beats a keyword hit, which beats a summary hit. Deliberately
 * not fuzzy — a near-miss would hand the model the wrong document, and reading
 * the wrong 40 KB document costs more than the search saved.
 */
export function searchIndex(index, query, { limit = 8 } = {}) {
  if (!index?.docs?.length) return [];
  const needle = String(query ?? '').trim().toLowerCase();
  if (!needle) {
    return index.docs.slice(0, limit).map((doc) => ({ ...doc, score: 0 }));
  }

  const terms = needle.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);

  return index.docs
    .map((doc) => {
      const name = doc.name.toLowerCase();
      const summary = (doc.summary ?? '').toLowerCase();
      const keywords = (doc.keywords ?? []).join(' ').toLowerCase();

      let score = 0;
      for (const term of terms) {
        if (name.includes(term)) score += 10;
        if (keywords.includes(term)) score += 5;
        if (summary.includes(term)) score += 2;
      }
      return { ...doc, score };
    })
    .filter((doc) => doc.score > 0)
    .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)
    .slice(0, limit);
}

/**
 * Read one document.
 *
 * Prefers the vendored copy (offline, pinned) and falls back to the network at
 * the indexed ref so a fresh checkout of the plugin still works before the
 * vendor script has run. A `section` argument returns only the matching heading
 * block, which is how a 70 KB document gets used without paying for all of it.
 */
export async function readDoc(index, name, { section = null } = {}) {
  const entry = index?.docs?.find((doc) => doc.name === name || doc.slug === name);
  if (!entry) {
    const available = (index?.docs ?? []).map((doc) => doc.name).join(', ');
    throw new Error(`没有这篇文档：${name}。可用：${available || '(索引为空)'}`);
  }

  // Bodies ship with the plugin: a distributed install must work offline, and a
  // firewall must not turn the documentation into an error message.
  const localPath = path.join(DOCS_PATH, entry.slug);
  if (!existsSync(localPath)) {
    throw new Error(
      `文档正文未随插件分发：${entry.slug}。`
      + '这是打包问题，运行 scripts/vendor-docs.mjs 重新拉取。',
    );
  }
  const text = await fs.readFile(localPath, 'utf8');

  if (!section) return text;

  // Return one heading block: from the matching `## ` heading to the next one.
  const lines = text.split('\n');
  const target = String(section).toLowerCase();
  const start = lines.findIndex((line) => /^#{1,3}\s/.test(line) && line.toLowerCase().includes(target));

  if (start < 0) {
    const headings = lines.filter((line) => /^#{1,3}\s/.test(line)).map((line) => line.trim());
    throw new Error(
      `「${section}」不在 ${entry.slug} 里。可用小节：\n${headings.slice(0, 40).join('\n')}`,
    );
  }

  const level = (lines[start].match(/^#+/) ?? ['#'])[0].length;
  let end = lines.length;
  for (let i = start + 1; i < lines.length; i += 1) {
    const match = lines[i].match(/^(#+)\s/);
    if (match && match[1].length <= level) {
      end = i;
      break;
    }
  }

  return lines.slice(start, end).join('\n');
}

/**
 * Build the documentation tool.
 *
 * `action=index` is the cheap map, `action=search` finds a document, and
 * `action=read` returns one document or one section of it.
 */
export function buildDocsTool() {
  return {
    name: 'rea_docs',
    description:
      'REA 官方文档（72 篇，1.2 MB）。先 search 找文档，再 read 读全文或某一节——'
      + '不要一次读全文，用 section 参数只取需要的小节。'
      + '安装、CLI 用法、各引擎（Ghidra/IDA/JEB/Kuna）配置、Android/iOS/固件/'
      + '浏览器/(Electron)/.NET 分析流程、Evidence 与比较契约都在这里。',
    parameters: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        action: {
          type: 'string',
          enum: ['index', 'search', 'read'],
          description: 'index=列出全部文档标题；search=按关键词找；read=读文档',
        },
        query: {
          type: 'string',
          description: 'action=search 的关键词，如 "ghidra"、"android"、"evidence"',
        },
        name: {
          type: 'string',
          description: 'action=read 的文档名（不含 .md），如 "cli"、"native-investigation"',
        },
        section: {
          type: 'string',
          description: '只取指定小节（标题关键词），如 "Windows"、"Provider"、"示例"',
        },
      },
      required: ['action'],
    },
    async execute(input = {}) {
      const index = await loadDocIndex();
      if (!index) {
        throw new Error('文档索引缺失（vendor/rea-docs/index.json）。运行 scripts/gen-doc-index.mjs 生成。');
      }

      const action = String(input.action ?? 'index');

      if (action === 'index') {
        const lines = index.docs.map((doc) => `${doc.name.padEnd(40)} ${doc.summary}`);
        return `${index.docs.length} 篇文档（ref ${index.ref ?? '未知'}）：\n\n${lines.join('\n')}`;
      }

      if (action === 'search') {
        const results = searchIndex(index, input.query, { limit: 8 });
        if (results.length === 0) {
          return `没有匹配「${input.query}」的文档。用 action=index 看全部 ${index.docs.length} 篇。`;
        }
        return results
          .map((doc) => `${doc.name}\n  ${doc.summary}`)
          .join('\n\n');
      }

      if (action === 'read') {
        const name = String(input.name ?? '');
        if (!name) throw new Error('action=read 需要 name 参数');
        return readDoc(index, name, { section: input.section ?? null });
      }

      throw new Error(`未知 action：${action}`);
    },
  };
}

```

`lib/tools-mobile.js`:

```js
/**
 * MobileRE tools — the mobile reverse-engineering layer.
 *
 * REA's Android surface is static: it reads classes, methods and resources out
 * of an APK. It cannot show you what an app does while it runs. MobileRE is the
 * other half — Frida hooks, unpacking, anti-injection probes, DEX recovery, SO
 * analysis, Unicorn emulation — and its scripts are Python, so they arrive here
 * as subprocesses rather than MCP tools.
 *
 * Design notes:
 *
 *  - **Grouped, not 1:1.** Twenty-one scripts would be twenty-one tools the
 *    model has to choose between. Each tool here is one job, and the script
 *    that does it is an implementation detail.
 *  - **The interpreter is discovered, not assumed.** `python` on Windows is
 *    often the Microsoft Store stub, which exits 49 and prints a help link. The
 *    probe skips that and reports the real reason.
 *  - **UTF-8 is forced.** Every script prints Chinese; the Windows console
 *    default is GBK, and mis-decoded output is worse than no output because it
 *    reads as data corruption.
 *  - **Missing dependencies are named.** A script that needs `frida` says so
 *    before it runs, instead of failing with an ImportError traceback.
 */

import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const VENDOR = path.join(HERE, '..', 'vendor', 'mobilere');
const TOOLS = path.join(VENDOR, 'tools');
const REFERENCES = path.join(VENDOR, 'references');

/** Seconds a tool may run before it is killed. Frida sessions need minutes. */
const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000;

/**
 * Script → Python packages it imports beyond the standard library.
 *
 * Kept here rather than parsed at runtime: a missing module is the single most
 * common failure, and an explicit table lets the tool say which package to
 * install instead of surfacing an ImportError from inside the script.
 */
const SCRIPT_REQUIREMENTS = {
  'frida_run.py': ['frida'],
  'unpack.py': ['frida'],
  'so.py': ['capstone', 'elftools'],
  'emu_run.py': ['unicorn', 'capstone'],
  'uniharness.py': ['unicorn', 'capstone'],
};

/** pip name for an import name, where they differ. */
const PIP_NAMES = {
  elftools: 'pyelftools',
  z3: 'z3-solver',
};

/**
 * Find a usable Python 3.
 *
 * Order matters: an explicitly configured path wins, then PATH, then the
 * per-user install location Windows uses when the Store stub owns `python`.
 * The Store stub is rejected because it exits 49 with a help link rather than
 * running anything — treating it as Python produces a confusing failure.
 */
export function findPython(configured = null) {
  const candidates = [];
  if (configured) candidates.push(configured);

  if (process.platform === 'win32') {
    candidates.push('python.exe', 'python3.exe', 'py.exe');
  } else {
    candidates.push('python3', 'python');
  }

  const home = process.env.USERPROFILE ?? process.env.HOME ?? '';
  if (process.platform === 'win32' && home) {
    for (const version of ['Python313', 'Python312', 'Python311', 'Python310']) {
      candidates.push(path.join(home, 'AppData', 'Local', 'Programs', 'Python', version, 'python.exe'));
    }
  }

  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    if (path.isAbsolute(candidate)) {
      if (existsSync(candidate)) return candidate;
      continue;
    }
    // On Windows a bare name resolves to the Microsoft Store stub, which exits
    // 49 and prints a help link. Only the per-user install path is trustworthy,
    // so bare names are skipped there and the absolute candidates above win.
    if (process.platform === 'win32') continue;
    return candidate;
  }
  return null;
}

let cachedPython = null;

/** Run the version probe once per process and memoise the result. */
function resolvePython(configured) {
  if (cachedPython) return cachedPython;

  const candidate = findPython(configured);
  if (!candidate) {
    cachedPython = { ok: false, error: '未找到 Python 3（已检查 PATH 与 %LOCALAPPDATA%\\Programs\\Python）' };
    return cachedPython;
  }
  cachedPython = { ok: true, command: candidate };
  return cachedPython;
}

/** Reset the memoised interpreter, so a settings change takes effect. */
export function resetPythonCache() {
  cachedPython = null;
}

/**
 * Probe the interpreter and the packages the vendored scripts need.
 *
 * One `python -c` invocation reports everything, because spawning Python is
 * ~100 ms on Windows and a per-module probe would make the settings page slow.
 */
export async function probePython(configured = null) {
  resetPythonCache();
  const resolved = resolvePython(configured);
  if (!resolved.ok) {
    return { present: false, version: null, missing: [], command: null, error: resolved.error };
  }

  const modules = [
    'frida', 'capstone', 'unicorn', 'lief', 'elftools', 'keystone', 'z3',
  ];

  const script = `
import sys, json
mods = ${JSON.stringify(modules)}
out = {}
for m in mods:
    try:
        __import__(m)
        out[m] = True
    except Exception:
        out[m] = False
print(json.dumps({"version": sys.version.split()[0], "modules": out}))
`;

  const result = await run(resolved.command, ['-c', script], { timeoutMs: 20_000 });
  if (result.code !== 0) {
    return {
      present: false,
      version: null,
      missing: [],
      command: resolved.command,
      error: (result.stderr || result.stdout || 'version probe failed').trim().slice(0, 300),
    };
  }

  let parsed;
  try {
    parsed = JSON.parse(result.stdout.trim().split('\n').pop());
  } catch {
    return {
      present: false,
      version: null,
      missing: [],
      command: resolved.command,
      error: '无法解析 Python 版本探测输出',
    };
  }

  const missing = Object.entries(parsed.modules).filter(([, ok]) => !ok).map(([name]) => name);

  return {
    present: true,
    version: parsed.version,
    modules: parsed.modules,
    missing,
    command: resolved.command,
  };
}

/**
 * Spawn a process and collect stdout/stderr.
 *
 * Not `exec`: the tool output is the payload, and a shell would rewrite it.
 * On Windows a `.py` file needs the interpreter as argv[0], which the caller
 * supplies; only the `.bat` helper needs a shell.
 */
function run(command, args, { cwd = TOOLS, timeoutMs = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, env = {} } = {}) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const child = spawn(command, args, {
      cwd,
      env: { ...process.env, PYTHONIOENCODING: 'utf-8', PYTHONUTF8: '1', ...env },
      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
      windowsHide: true,
      shell: command.endsWith('.bat'),
    });

    let stdout = '';
    let stderr = '';
    let killed = false;

    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      killed = true;
      try { child.kill(); } catch { /* already gone */ }
    }, timeoutMs);

    child.stdout.setEncoding('utf8');
    child.stderr.setEncoding('utf8');
    child.stdout.on('data', (chunk) => { stdout += chunk; });
    child.stderr.on('data', (chunk) => { stderr += chunk; });

    child.on('error', (error) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve({ code: -1, stdout, stderr: `${stderr}\n${error.message}`, killed });
    });

    child.on('exit', (code) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve({ code: code ?? -1, stdout, stderr, killed });
    });
  });
}

/**
 * Run one vendored script and flatten the result for the Host tool channel.
 *
 * A non-zero exit is an error, but its stderr is the interesting part: these
 * scripts report "device not found", "no frida server", "invalid ELF" there.
 */
async function runScript(scriptName, args, { timeoutMs, python } = {}) {
  const scriptPath = path.join(TOOLS, scriptName);
  if (!existsSync(scriptPath)) {
    throw new Error(`MobileRE 脚本缺失：${scriptName}（vendor/mobilere/tools 不完整）`);
  }

  const resolved = resolvePython(python);
  if (!resolved.ok) throw new Error(resolved.error);

  const required = SCRIPT_REQUIREMENTS[scriptName] ?? [];
  if (required.length > 0) {
    const probe = await probePython(python);
    const absent = required.filter((name) => probe.modules?.[name] === false);
    if (absent.length > 0) {
      const pipNames = absent.map((name) => PIP_NAMES[name] ?? name);
      throw new Error(
        `缺少 Python 依赖：${absent.join(', ')}。`
        + `安装命令：${probe.command} -m pip install ${pipNames.join(' ')}`,
      );
    }
  }

  const result = await run(resolved.command, [scriptPath, ...args], { timeoutMs });

  if (result.killed) {
    throw new Error(`${scriptName} 超时（${Math.round((timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS) / 1000)}s）已终止`);
  }

  const text = [result.stdout.trim(), result.stderr.trim()].filter(Boolean).join('\n\n');

  if (result.code !== 0) {
    throw new Error(`${scriptName} 退出码 ${result.code}：\n${text || '(无输出)'}`);
  }

  return text || '(脚本无输出)';
}

/** A read-only reference doc, so the model can pull the method behind a tool. */
function readReference(name) {
  const file = path.join(REFERENCES, name);
  if (!existsSync(file)) return null;
  return readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
}

/**
 * Build the MobileRE tools.
 *
 * Five tools, grouped by job. `python` comes from plugin config so an operator
 * with a specific interpreter can point at it.

export function buildMobileTools(config = {}) {
  const python = config.pythonPath ?? null;
  const baseTimeout = Number(config.mobileToolTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS);

  return [
    {
      name: 'mobile_unpack',
      description:
        'Android 脱壳：从 APK 或运行中的进程提取 DEX，去重并重建。'
        + '支持壳检测、内存 dump、DEX 合并。用于处理加固/加壳的 Android 应用。',
      parameters: {

        properties: {

            type: 'string',

        if (args.serial) argv.push('--serial', String(args.serial));

      },

    {
      name: 'mobile_frida',
      description:
        'Frida 动态插桩：在 Android/iOS 应用运行时执行 hook 脚本、绕过反调试、'

          duration: {
            type: 'number',

          },

      async execute(args = {}) {
        const action = String(args.action ?? 'run');
        const argv = [action];
        if (args.script) argv.push('--script', String(args.script));
        if (args.target) argv.push('--target', String(args.target));
        if (args.serial) argv.push('--serial', String(args.serial));
        if (args.duration) argv.push('--duration', String(args.duration));
        return runScript('frida_run.py', argv, { timeoutMs: baseTimeout, python });
      },

      name: 'mobile_check',

    {
      name: 'mobile_emulate',

      parameters: {

            type: 'string',

          },

            type: 'string',
            description: '要模拟的函数名（与 offset 二选一）',
          },
          offset: {
            type: 'string',
            description: '函数偏移或虚拟地址（与 symbol 二选一，如 0x1a20）',
          },
          args: {
            type: 'string',
            description: '传参，逗号分隔（十六进制或十进制，字符串用 \'文本\'）',
          },
          jni: {
            type: 'boolean',
            description: '启用 JNI 环境桩，模拟 JNIEnv 调用',
          },
          trace: {
            type: 'boolean',
            description: '输出指令级执行追踪',
          },
          read: {
            type: 'string',
            description: '执行后读取内存（格式：地址:长度，如 0x4000:64）',
          },
          poke: {
            type: 'string',
            description: '执行前写入内存（格式：地址=十六进制字节，如 0x4000=deadbeef）',

            type: 'number',
            description: '模拟超时秒数，缺省 30',

      async execute(args = {}) {

        if (!args.symbol && !args.offset) {
          throw new Error('必须提供 symbol 或 offset 之一来指定入口');
        }

        // emu_run.py takes the SO path first, then flags; there is no action
        // subcommand, so the mode is inferred from the flags supplied.
        const argv = [target];
        if (args.symbol) argv.push('--sym', String(args.symbol));
        if (args.offset) argv.push('--off', String(args.offset));
        if (args.args) argv.push('--args', String(args.args));
        if (args.jni) argv.push('--jni');
        if (args.trace) argv.push('--trace');
        if (args.read) argv.push('--read', String(args.read));
        if (args.poke) argv.push('--poke', String(args.poke));
        if (args.timeout) argv.push('--timeout', String(args.timeout));

        return runScript('emu_run.py', argv, { timeoutMs: baseTimeout, python });
      },
    },

    {
      name: 'mobile_reference',
      description:
        '读取 MobileRE 实战手册：反检测、脱壳、加密 hook、行为分析、'
        + 'native 分析、静态分析、排错指南、Frida API 参考。',
      parameters: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          topic: {
            type: 'string',
            enum: [
              'index', 'anti-detection', 'unpacking', 'crypto-hook',
              'behavior-analysis', 'static-analysis', 'native-analysis',
              'troubleshooting', 'api-reference',
            ],
            description: 'index 是总索引，会告诉你该读哪一篇',
          },
        },
        required: ['topic'],
      },
      async execute(args = {}) {
        const topic = String(args.topic ?? 'index');
        const file = topic === 'index' ? '_index.md' : `${topic}.md`;
        const text = readReference(file);
        if (text === null) {
          throw new Error(`手册不存在：${topic}。可用：见 mobile_reference 的 topic 枚举`);
        }
        return text;
      },
    },
  ];
}

/** Exposed for the health check: how many scripts and docs are actually present. */
export function vendorInventory() {
  const tools = existsSync(TOOLS) ? readDirSafe(TOOLS) : [];
  const docs = existsSync(REFERENCES) ? readDirSafe(REFERENCES) : [];
  return {
    root: VENDOR,
    toolCount: tools.filter((name) => name.endsWith('.py') || name.endsWith('.jar') || name.endsWith('.bat')).length,
    docCount: docs.filter((name) => name.endsWith('.md')).length,
    present: tools.length > 0,
  };
}

function readDirSafe(dir) {
  try {
    return readdirSync(dir);
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
}
```

`lib/tools.js`:

```js
/**
 * Tool registration for the REA bundle.
 *
 * These are DSH-native tools, not MCP tools. They sit beside the 207
 * `mcp__rea__*` tools that the `rea-mcp` row contributes, and they cover the
 * three things those MCP tools structurally cannot do:
 *
 *   1. report and repair analysis-engine readiness — REA refuses to download
 *      engines, so nobody else was going to do it;
 *   2. run the multi-step unpack pipeline that REA has no operation for;
 *   3. describe what this host can actually do, so an agent routes to a
 *      supported path instead of discovering a missing provider mid-analysis.
 *
 * Every tool returns plain JSON matching its declared schema. Errors are
 * returned as data with `ok: false` rather than thrown, because an agent
 * needs the remediation text and a thrown error loses the structured fields.
 */

import { installEngines, probeAll, describeOutcome, providerEnvironment, CACHE_ROOT, REA_AGENTS_VERSION } from './providers.js';
import { unpackTarget, describeUnpackCaps } from './unpack.js';

/**
 * Minimal JSON Schema helpers. DSH validates `parameters` as JSON Schema, so
 * these keep the declarations readable without pulling in a schema library.
 */
const stringProperty = (description, extra = {}) => ({ type: 'string', description, ...extra });
const numberProperty = (description, extra = {}) => ({ type: 'number', description, ...extra });
const booleanProperty = (description, extra = {}) => ({ type: 'boolean', description, ...extra });
const arrayProperty = (description, items, extra = {}) => ({ type: 'array', description, items, ...extra });

/** Wrap a handler so it always resolves to a schema-shaped object. */
function safeExecute(name, handler) {
  return async (args, exec) => {
    try {
      return await handler(args ?? {}, exec);
    } catch (error) {
      return {
        ok: false,
        tool: name,
        error: error?.message ?? String(error),
        hint: 'Re-run rea_provider_status to see current engine readiness before retrying.',
      };
    }
  };
}

/**

          lines: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },

      const targets = [
        {
```

`lib/unpack.js`:

```js
/**
 * Unpack pipeline — the capability REA has no operation for.
 *
 * REA is a static/runtime *observer*. Unpacking is a multi-stage process with
 * a decision at every step, so upstream leaves it to the agent. This module
 * encodes that decision tree so the agent gets one tool instead of twelve
 * shell commands it has to order correctly.
 *
 * Honesty rules this file follows, because unpacking is where tools most often
 * lie to their users:
 *
 *  - Detection is not unpacking. If only the detect stage ran, the result says
 *    so and `ok` reflects that the requested work did not complete.
 *  - A stage that cannot run on this host is `unsupported`, never silently
 *    skipped and never reported as success.
 *  - `strip` only claims success when the output re-reads as a valid artefact.
 *  - Dex dumping needs a device, root, and a running process. Every one of
 *    those is checked and named in the failure text.
 */

import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { promises as fs } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { promisify } from 'node:util';
import { execFile } from 'node:child_process';

const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile);

/**
 * Packer signatures. Entropy is the fallback: a section above ~7.0 bits per
 * byte is either compressed or encrypted, which means the static view is not
 * the real code.
 *
 * `strip` names the strategy this pipeline can actually run. Anything marked
 * `manual` is detected and then handed back with concrete next steps rather
 * than a vague "packed, unknown".
 */
export const PACKER_SIGNATURES = [
  {
    name: 'UPX',
    family: 'compressor',
    sectionPatterns: [/^UPX0$/i, /^UPX1$/i, /^UPX!$/i, /\.UPX$/i],
    markers: ['UPX!', 'UPX0', 'UPX1'],
    strip: 'upx',
    note: 'Self-extracting compressor with a documented stub; strip restores the original image.',
  },
  {
    name: 'ASPack',
    family: 'compressor',
    sectionPatterns: [/^\.aspack$/i, /^\.adata$/i],
    markers: ['.aspack', '.adata'],
    strip: 'manual',
    note: 'No offline stripper here; dump the image at OEP and rebuild the import table.',
  },
  {
    name: 'MPRESS',

    sectionPatterns: [/^\.MPRESS1$/i, /^\.MPRESS2$/i],
    markers: ['.MPRESS1'],
    strip: 'manual',
    note: 'Two-stage stub; needs a runtime dump at the second stage entry.',
  },
  {
    name: 'Themida',
    family: 'protector',
    sectionPatterns: [/^\.themida$/i, /^\.winlice$/i, /^\.vmp0$/i],
    markers: ['.themida', '.winlice'],
    strip: 'manual',
    note: 'Virtualised protector; static stripping is not achievable. Requires dynamic dumping plus import reconstruction at OEP.',

  {
    name: 'VMProtect',
    family: 'protector',

    markers: ['.vmp0', '.vmp1'],
    strip: 'manual',
    note: 'Code is translated to a VM; only the VM handler can be recovered, not original code.',
  },

    markers: ['.enigma1', '.enigma2'],

    strip: 'manual',
    note: 'Legacy protector; needs OEP location through stack/heap tricks.',
  },
  {

    apkMarkers: ['libjiagu', 'libjiagu_art', 'libjiagu_ls'],
    strip: 'manual',
    note: 'Android shell with anti-dump checks; needs a Frida-based dump, not a plain ptrace dump.',
  },
  {
    name: 'Bangcle',
    family: 'android-packer',
    apkMarkers: ['libsecexe', 'libsecmain', 'libsecshell'],
    strip: 'manual',
    note: 'Android shell; runtime dump required.',
  },
  {
    name: 'Yidun / Netease',
    family: 'android-packer',
    apkMarkers: ['libnesec', 'libyidun'],
    strip: 'manual',
    note: 'Android shell; runtime dump required.',
  },
  {
    name: 'Alibaba / Ali',
    family: 'android-packer',
    apkMarkers: ['libmobisec', 'libsgmain', 'libsgsecuritybody'],
    strip: 'manual',
    note: 'Android shell; runtime dump required.',

/** Entropy above this suggests compressed or encrypted content. */
const ENTROPY_THRESHOLD = 7.0;

/**
 * shannon entropy over a buffer, in bits per byte.
 * Kept local so this module has no dependency on a binary-parsing library.
 */
export function shannonEntropy(buffer) {
  if (buffer.length === 0) return 0;
  const counts = new Uint32Array(256);
  for (let index = 0; index < buffer.length; index += 1) {
    counts[buffer[index]] += 1;
  }
  let entropy = 0;
  for (const count of counts) {
    if (count === 0) continue;
    const probability = count / buffer.length;
    entropy -= probability * Math.log2(probability);
  }
  return entropy;
}

async function run(command, args, options = {}) {
  try {
    const { stdout, stderr } = await execFileAsync(command, args, {
      timeout: options.timeoutMs ?? 300_000,
      maxBuffer: 32 * 1024 * 1024,
      windowsHide: true,
      ...options,
    });
    return { ok: true, stdout: stdout ?? '', stderr: stderr ?? '' };
  } catch (error) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      stdout: error.stdout ?? '',
      stderr: error.stderr ?? '',
      code: error.code ?? null,
      message: error.message,
    };
  }
}

async function which(command) {
  const probe = await run(process.platform === 'win32' ? 'where' : 'which', [command]);
  return probe.ok ? String(probe.stdout).split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => line.trim()).find(Boolean) ?? null : null;
}

async function exists(target) {
  try {
    await fs.access(target);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * Minimal ZIP central-directory walker. Needed to read an APK's entry names
 * without extracting it, and to find `lib/` entries that identify an Android
 * packer. Deliberately small: only the fields this module reads.
 */
async function listZipEntries(zipPath) {
  const handle = await fs.open(zipPath, 'r');
  try {
    const { size } = await handle.stat();
    // The end-of-central-directory record is within the last 64 KiB.
    const tailLength = Math.min(size, 65557);
    const tail = Buffer.alloc(tailLength);
    await handle.read(tail, 0, tailLength, size - tailLength);

    let eocd = -1;
    for (let index = tail.length - 22; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
      if (tail.readUInt32LE(index) === 0x06054b50) {
        eocd = index;
        break;
      }
    }
    if (eocd < 0) throw new Error('not a ZIP archive: no end-of-central-directory record found');

    const entryCount = tail.readUInt16LE(eocd + 10);
    const directoryOffset = tail.readUInt32LE(eocd + 16);

    const header = Buffer.alloc(46);
    const names = [];
    let cursor = directoryOffset;
    for (let index = 0; index < entryCount; index += 1) {
      await handle.read(header, 0, 46, cursor);
      if (header.readUInt32LE(0) !== 0x02014b50) break;
      const nameLength = header.readUInt16LE(28);
      const extraLength = header.readUInt16LE(30);
      const commentLength = header.readUInt16LE(32);
      const uncompressed = header.readUInt32LE(24);
      const compressed = header.readUInt32LE(20);

      const nameBuffer = Buffer.alloc(nameLength);
      await handle.read(nameBuffer, 0, nameLength, cursor + 46);
      names.push({
        name: nameBuffer.toString('utf8'),
        uncompressed,
        compressed,
        entryOffset: header.readUInt32LE(42),
      });

      cursor += 46 + nameLength + extraLength + commentLength;
    }
    return names;
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
}

/**
 * Extract one ZIP entry by name. Used to pull a single library or DEX header
 * for signature checks without unpacking the whole archive.
 */
async function readZipEntry(zipPath, entryName, { maxBytes = 64 * 1024 } = {}) {
  const handle = await fs.open(zipPath, 'r');
  try {
    const { size } = await handle.stat();
    const tailLength = Math.min(size, 65557);
    const tail = Buffer.alloc(tailLength);
    await handle.read(tail, 0, tailLength, size - tailLength);

    let eocd = -1;
    for (let index = tail.length - 22; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
      if (tail.readUInt32LE(index) === 0x06054b50) {
        eocd = index;
        break;
      }
    }
    if (eocd < 0) throw new Error('not a ZIP archive');

    const entryCount = tail.readUInt16LE(eocd + 10);
    const directoryOffset = tail.readUInt32LE(eocd + 16);

    const header = Buffer.alloc(46);
    let cursor = directoryOffset;
    for (let index = 0; index < entryCount; index += 1) {
      await handle.read(header, 0, 46, cursor);
      if (header.readUInt32LE(0) !== 0x02014b50) break;
      const nameLength = header.readUInt16LE(28);
      const extraLength = header.readUInt16LE(30);
      const commentLength = header.readUInt16LE(32);
      const compressedSize = header.readUInt32LE(20);
      const localOffset = header.readUInt32LE(42);
      const compressionMethod = header.readUInt16LE(10);

      const nameBuffer = Buffer.alloc(nameLength);
      await handle.read(nameBuffer, 0, nameLength, cursor + 46);
      const name = nameBuffer.toString('utf8');

      if (name === entryName) {
        // Skip the local file header to reach the payload.
        const localHeader = Buffer.alloc(30);
        await handle.read(localHeader, 0, 30, localOffset);
        const localNameLength = localHeader.readUInt16LE(26);
        const localExtraLength = localHeader.readUInt16LE(28);
        const dataStart = localOffset + 30 + localNameLength + localExtraLength;

        // Only stored entries are read raw. A deflated entry would need a
        // decompressor; callers use this for short magic checks in stored or
        // small entries and the signature checks below tolerate that.
        if (compressionMethod !== 0) {
          return { name, compressionMethod, buffered: false, note: 'entry is deflated; raw read skipped' };
        }
        const length = Math.min(compressedSize, maxBytes);
        const buffer = Buffer.alloc(length);
        await handle.read(buffer, 0, length, dataStart);
        return { name, compressionMethod, buffered: true, buffer };
      }

      cursor += 46 + nameLength + extraLength + commentLength;
    }
    return { name: entryName, found: false };
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
}

/**
 * Detect the packer of an APK or native binary.
 *
 * Strategy, in order of cost:
 *   1. container markers (APK library names) — definitive for Android shells;
 *   2. raw string markers in the file head and tail;
 *   3. section-name matching for PE/Mach-O via byte search;
 *   4. entropy, which only tells you *that* it is packed, not which packer.
 */
export async function detectPacker(target) {
  const stat = await fs.stat(target);
  const handle = await fs.open(target, 'r');
  const isZip = (() => {
    const magic = Buffer.alloc(4);
    return handle.read(magic, 0, 4, 0).then(() => magic.readUInt32LE(0) === 0x04034b50);
  })();
  const zip = await isZip;
  await handle.close();

  const result = {
    format: zip ? 'zip-container' : 'binary',
    candidates: [],
    entropy: null,
    highEntropy: false,
    evidence: [],
  };

  if (zip) {
    result.format = 'apk-or-zip';
    const entries = await listZipEntries(target);
    const names = entries.map((entry) => entry.name);
    result.evidence.push(`zip contains ${names.length} entries`);

    const dex = names.filter((name) => name.endsWith('.dex'));
    const libs = names.filter((name) => name.startsWith('lib/'));
    result.evidence.push(`dex files: ${dex.length}; native libraries: ${libs.length}`);

    // A shell APK usually keeps only one small loader DEX and hides the real
    // classes in a native library.
    if (dex.length > 0) {
      const firstDex = entries.find((entry) => entry.name === dex[0]);
      if (firstDex && firstDex.uncompressed < 64 * 1024) {
        result.evidence.push(`first dex is only ${firstDex.uncompressed} bytes, typical of a shell stub`);
      }
      const header = await readZipEntry(target, dex[0], { maxBytes: 4096 });
      if (header.buffered) {
        result.entropy = shannonEntropy(header.buffer);
        result.highEntropy = result.entropy > ENTROPY_THRESHOLD;
      }
    }

    const libNames = new Set(libs.map((name) => path.basename(name)));
    for (const signature of PACKER_SIGNATURES) {
      if (!signature.apkMarkers) continue;
      const matched = signature.apkMarkers.filter((marker) =>
        [...libNames].some((name) => name.toLowerCase().includes(marker.toLowerCase())),
      );
      if (matched.length > 0) {
        result.candidates.push({ ...signature, matched: matched.map((marker) => `lib entry ${marker}`), confidence: 'high' });
      }
    }
  }

  // Marker scan on the raw bytes. Bounded so a multi-GB image stays fast.
  const scanLength = Math.min(stat.size, 4 * 1024 * 1024);
  const head = Buffer.alloc(scanLength);
  const fileHandle = await fs.open(target, 'r');
  try {
    await fileHandle.read(head, 0, scanLength, 0);
    if (stat.size > scanLength) {
      const tail = Buffer.alloc(Math.min(512 * 1024, stat.size - scanLength));
      await fileHandle.read(tail, 0, tail.length, stat.size - tail.length);
      for (const signature of PACKER_SIGNATURES) {
        const markers = signature.markers ?? [];
        const matched = markers.filter((marker) => tail.includes(Buffer.from(marker, 'latin1')));
        if (matched.length > 0 && !result.candidates.some((candidate) => candidate.name === signature.name)) {
          result.candidates.push({ ...signature, matched: matched.map((marker) => `tail marker ${marker}`), confidence: 'medium' });
        }
      }
    }
  } finally {
    await fileHandle.close();
  }

  for (const signature of PACKER_SIGNATURES) {
    const markers = signature.markers ?? [];
    const matched = markers.filter((marker) => head.includes(Buffer.from(marker, 'latin1')));
    const patterns = signature.sectionPatterns ?? [];

    // Section names live in PE section headers as short ASCII strings.
    const patternMatched = patterns
      .map((pattern) => pattern.source.replace(/^\^|\$$/g, '').replace(/\\\./g, '.'))
      .filter((literal) => head.includes(Buffer.from(literal.replace(/\$$/, ''), 'latin1')));

    if (matched.length === 0 && patternMatched.length === 0) continue;
    if (result.candidates.some((candidate) => candidate.name === signature.name)) continue;

    result.candidates.push({
      ...signature,
      matched: [...matched.map((marker) => `marker ${marker}`), ...patternMatched.map((literal) => `section name ${literal}`)],
      confidence: matched.length > 0 ? 'high' : 'medium',
    });
  }

  // Entropy fallback: says the target is packed without naming the packer.
  if (result.candidates.length === 0 && !zip) {
    const sampleLength = Math.min(stat.size, 1024 * 1024);
    const sample = Buffer.alloc(sampleLength);
    const entropyHandle = await fs.open(target, 'r');
    try {
      await entropyHandle.read(sample, 0, sampleLength, 0);
    } finally {
      await entropyHandle.close();
    }
    result.entropy = shannonEntropy(sample);
    result.highEntropy = result.entropy > ENTROPY_THRESHOLD;
    if (result.highEntropy) {
      result.evidence.push(
        `entropy ${result.entropy.toFixed(2)} bits/byte in the first MiB exceeds ${ENTROPY_THRESHOLD}; content is likely compressed or encrypted`,
      );
    }
  }

  return result;
}

/**
 * UPX strip. Runs the real `upx -d` and then verifies the output is a readable
 * executable by comparing its size and checking it is not still UPX-marked.
 */
async function stripUpx(target, outputDirectory, { signal } = {}) {
  const upx = await which('upx');
  if (!upx) {
    return {
      stage: 'strip',
      method: 'upx',
      status: 'unsupported',
      detail: 'the upx binary is not on PATH; install UPX from https://upx.github.io and re-run',
    };
  }

  const output = path.join(outputDirectory, `${path.basename(target)}.unpacked`);
  const result = await run(upx, ['-d', '-o', output, target], { signal, timeoutMs: 600_000 });
  if (!result.ok) {
    return {
      stage: 'strip',
      method: 'upx',
      status: 'failed',
      detail: String(result.stderr || result.message).split(/\r?\n/).slice(-3).join(' '),
    };
  }

  if (!(await exists(output))) {
    return { stage: 'strip', method: 'upx', status: 'failed', detail: 'upx reported success but wrote no output file' };
  }

  // Re-detect: a successful strip must remove the UPX markers.
  const verification = await detectPacker(output);
  const stillPacked = verification.candidates.some((candidate) => candidate.name === 'UPX');
  return {
    stage: 'strip',
    method: 'upx',
    status: stillPacked ? 'failed' : 'completed',
    output,
    detail: stillPacked
      ? 'output still carries UPX markers; the stub may be modified or the archive multi-stage'
      : 'stripped image re-reads without UPX markers',
  };
}

/**
 * Runtime DEX dump for Android shells.
 *
 * This does not reimplement a dumper. It requires the device to be attached
 * and rooted, then reports the exact commands a dump needs, because a generic
 * dump implementation without a validated hooking library would produce a
 * corrupt DEX and claim success. The stage reports `needs-device` with the
 * precise precondition that failed.
 */
async function dexDump(target, { packageName, serial, outputDirectory, signal } = {}) {
  const adb = await which('adb');
  if (!adb) {
    return {
      stage: 'dex-dump',
      status: 'unsupported',
      detail: 'adb is not on PATH; install Android platform-tools to dump runtime DEX',
    };
  }

  const devices = await run(adb, serial ? ['-s', serial, 'get-state'] : ['devices'], { signal });
  if (!devices.ok) {
    return { stage: 'dex-dump', status: 'failed', detail: `adb failed: ${String(devices.stderr || devices.message).trim()}` };
  }

  if (!serial && String(devices.stdout).split(/\r?\n/).filter((line) => line.includes('\tdevice')).length === 0) {
    return { stage: 'dex-dump', status: 'unsupported', detail: 'no adb device in `device` state is connected' };
  }

  const targetSerial = serial ?? String(devices.stdout)
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.split('\t'))
    .find((parts) => parts[1]?.trim() === 'device')?.[0]
    ?.trim();

  if (!targetSerial) {
    return { stage: 'dex-dump', status: 'unsupported', detail: 'could not resolve a usable device serial' };
  }

  // Root is required to read another app's mapped DEX memory.
  const root = await run(adb, ['-s', targetSerial, 'shell', 'su', '-c', 'id'], { signal });
  const rooted = root.ok && String(root.stdout).includes('uid=0');
  if (!rooted) {
    return {
      stage: 'dex-dump',
      status: 'unsupported',
      detail: `device ${targetSerial} is not rooted or su is denied; runtime DEX dump needs root`,
    };
  }

  // Frida is the only dumper this pipeline can trust to produce a valid DEX.
  const fridaPs = await run(adb, ['-s', targetSerial, 'shell', 'ls', '/data/local/tmp'], { signal });
  const hasFridaServer = fridaPs.ok && /frida[-_]?server/i.test(String(fridaPs.stdout));
  if (!hasFridaServer) {
    return {
      stage: 'dex-dump',
      status: 'unsupported',
      detail: `no frida-server in /data/local/tmp on ${targetSerial}; push a matching frida-server and start it as root, then re-run`,
      nextSteps: [
        `adb -s ${targetSerial} push frida-server-android-arm64 /data/local/tmp/frida-server`,
        `adb -s ${targetSerial} shell chmod 755 /data/local/tmp/frida-server`,
        `adb -s ${targetSerial} shell su -c '/data/local/tmp/frida-server -D &'`,
      ],
    };
  }

  if (!packageName) {
    return {
      stage: 'dex-dump',
      status: 'needs-input',
      detail: 'packageName is required so the running app can be located on the device',
      nextSteps: [`adb -s ${targetSerial} shell pm list packages | grep -i <app-name>`],
    };
  }

  const pidProbe = await run(adb, ['-s', targetSerial, 'shell', 'pidof', packageName], { signal });
  const pid = String(pidProbe.stdout ?? '').trim();
  if (!pid) {
    return {
      stage: 'dex-dump',
      status: 'needs-input',
      detail: `${packageName} is not running on ${targetSerial}; launch it, complete any login, then re-run`,
      nextSteps: [`adb -s ${targetSerial} shell monkey -p ${packageName} -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1`],
    };
  }

  return {
    stage: 'dex-dump',
    status: 'ready-to-execute',
    detail: `device ${targetSerial} is rooted, frida-server is present, and ${packageName} runs as pid ${pid}`,
    outputDirectory,
    nextSteps: [
      `Load a Frida DEX dumper against pid ${pid} and write the dump into ${outputDirectory}`,
      'Fix the dumped DEX checksum and signature before opening it in JADX',
      'Deduplicate classes across dump passes; multi-DEX shells emit the same class more than once',
    ],
  };
}

/** Build the output directory for a run. */
async function prepareOutput(target, outputDirectory) {
  const directory = outputDirectory ?? path.join(process.cwd(), 'runs', 'rea-unpack', `${Date.now()}`);
  await fs.mkdir(directory, { recursive: true });
  const stat = await fs.stat(target);
  return { directory, size: stat.size };
}

/**
 * Describe what this pipeline can and cannot do. Separate from execution so an
 * agent can be honest with a user before starting.
 */
export function describeUnpackCaps() {
  const automatic = PACKER_SIGNATURES.filter((signature) => signature.strip === 'upx').map((signature) => signature.name);
  const manual = PACKER_SIGNATURES.filter((signature) => signature.strip !== 'upx').map((signature) => signature.name);
  return {
    ok: true,
    supported: PACKER_SIGNATURES.map((signature) => ({
      name: signature.name,
      family: signature.family,
      automatic: signature.strip === 'upx',
      note: signature.note,
    })),
    automatic,
    manualOnly: manual,
    summary:
      `${PACKER_SIGNATURES.length} packers recognised. Only UPX can be stripped offline by this pipeline; `
      + `${manual.length} others are detected and handed back with a dump route. Android shells need a rooted device with frida-server.`,
  };
}

/**
 * Run the unpack pipeline.
 *
 * Stage order in `auto` mode:
 *   1. detect — always runs, everything else depends on it;
 *   2. strip  — when a recognised offline stripper applies;
 *   3. dex-dump — when the target is an Android shell and a device is ready.
 *
 * `ok` is true only when the work the caller asked for actually completed.
 */
export async function unpackTarget({ target, mode = 'auto', packageName, serial, outputDirectory, signal }) {
  const absolute = path.resolve(target);
  if (!(await exists(absolute))) {
    return { ok: false, tool: 'rea_unpack', stages: [], summary: `target not found: ${absolute}` };
  }

  const { directory, size } = await prepareOutput(absolute, outputDirectory);
  const digest = createHash('sha256');
  const handle = await fs.open(absolute, 'r');
  try {
    const chunk = Buffer.alloc(1024 * 1024);
    let position = 0;
    for (;;) {
      const { bytesRead } = await handle.read(chunk, 0, chunk.length, position);
      if (bytesRead === 0) break;
      digest.update(chunk.subarray(0, bytesRead));
      position += bytesRead;
      if (position >= size) break;
    }
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }

  const stages = [];
  const artifacts = [];

  const detection = await detectPacker(absolute);
  stages.push({
    stage: 'detect',
    status: detection.candidates.length > 0 ? 'completed' : detection.highEntropy ? 'inconclusive' : 'clean',
    candidates: detection.candidates.map((candidate) => ({
      name: candidate.name,
      family: candidate.family,
      confidence: candidate.confidence,
      matched: candidate.matched,
      note: candidate.note,
    })),
    entropy: detection.entropy,
    highEntropy: detection.highEntropy,
    evidence: detection.evidence,
    detail:
      detection.candidates.length > 0
        ? `identified ${detection.candidates.map((candidate) => candidate.name).join(', ')}`
        : detection.highEntropy
          ? 'no known signature, but entropy indicates compression or encryption'
          : 'no packer signature found; the target already looks like a plain image',
  });

  const packer = detection.candidates[0] ?? null;

  if (mode === 'detect') {
    return {
      ok: packer !== null || detection.highEntropy,
      tool: 'rea_unpack',
      target: absolute,
      sha256: digest.digest('hex'),
      packer: packer
        ? { name: packer.name, family: packer.family, confidence: packer.confidence, note: packer.note }
        : null,
      stages,
      artifacts,
      outputDirectory: directory,
      nextSteps: packer
        ? [
            `This pipeline cannot remove ${packer.name} automatically. ${packer.note}`,
            'Switch to a runtime route: dump the image at the original entry point, then rebuild the import table.',
            'For Android shells, run rea_unpack with mode dex-dump on a rooted device.',
          ]
        : [],
      summary: packer
        ? `detected ${packer.name} (${packer.confidence} confidence); detection mode does not modify the target`
        : detection.highEntropy
          ? 'no signature matched, but the high entropy means static analysis will show encrypted or compressed bytes, not the real code'
          : 'no packer detected',
    };
  }

  // Strip stage: only when an offline stripper applies.
  if (packer && packer.strip === 'upx' && (mode === 'auto' || mode === 'strip')) {
    const strip = await stripUpx(absolute, directory, { signal });
    stages.push(strip);
    if (strip.output) artifacts.push(strip.output);
  } else if (mode === 'strip' && (!packer || packer.strip !== 'upx')) {
    stages.push({
      stage: 'strip',
      status: 'unsupported',
      detail: packer
        ? `${packer.name} has no offline stripper in this pipeline. ${packer.note}`
        : 'no packer signature found, so there is nothing to strip; the target may already be unpacked',
    });
  }

  // Android shell route.
  const isAndroidShell = packer?.family === 'android-packer';
  if ((mode === 'dex-dump' || (mode === 'auto' && isAndroidShell))) {
    const dump = await dexDump(absolute, { packageName, serial, outputDirectory: directory, signal });
    stages.push(dump);
  }

  const completed = stages.filter((stage) => stage.status === 'completed');
  const actionable = stages.filter((stage) =>
    ['failed', 'unsupported', 'needs-input', 'inconclusive', 'ready-to-execute'].includes(stage.status),
  );

  const nextSteps = [];
  if (actionable.some((stage) => stage.stage === 'dex-dump')) {
    nextSteps.push('Complete the dex-dump preconditions listed in that stage, then re-run rea_unpack with mode dex-dump.');
    nextSteps.push('After the dump, fix the DEX header checksum and signature before running JADX on it.');
  }
  if (packer && packer.strip === 'manual' && packer.family !== 'android-packer') {
    nextSteps.push(`Locate the original entry point, dump the mapped image, then rebuild imports. ${packer.note}`);
    nextSteps.push('Re-run rea_unpack after the dump to confirm the markers are gone.');
  }
  if (packer === null && !detection.highEntropy) {
    nextSteps.push('No packer found; run rea_analyze or rea_decompile directly on this target.');
  }

  const unpacked = completed.some((stage) => stage.stage === 'strip' || stage.status === 'completed' && stage.stage === 'dex-dump');

  return {
    ok: unpacked,
    tool: 'rea_unpack',
    target: absolute,
    sha256: digest.digest('hex'),
    size,
    packer: packer
      ? { name: packer.name, family: packer.family, confidence: packer.confidence, note: packer.note }
      : null,
    stages,
    artifacts,
    outputDirectory: directory,
    nextSteps,
    summary: packer
      ? `${packer.name} detected. `
        + (completed.some((stage) => stage.stage === 'strip')
          ? 'Offline strip completed and verified.'
          : completed.length > 0
            ? `Stages completed: ${completed.map((stage) => stage.stage).join(', ')}.`
            : `No stage could remove ${packer.name} on this host; see nextSteps.`)
      : detection.highEntropy
        ? 'No signature matched but content is compressed or encrypted; static code will not be readable.'
        : 'No packer detected; target is already a plain image.',
  };
}

```

`lib/updater.js`:

```js
/**
 * Update check.
 *
 * A running plugin cannot replace its own files: Node has them open, and on
 * Windows even a rename fails while a module is loaded. So "hot update" here
 * means the part that is actually possible and safe —
 *
 *   1. ask the registry what version exists,
 *   2. compare it against the running one,
 *   3. tell the user, with the exact command to run,
 *   4. let them restart into the new code.
 *
 * What it deliberately does NOT do: download a tarball and overwrite itself.
 * That path needs write access to the DSH profile, leaves a half-updated tree if
 * it fails midway, and produces a plugin whose loaded modules and files disagree
 * — the exact failure mode that makes "it says 2.9.1 but behaves like 2.8.0"
 * bugs. The package manager already does this correctly.
 *
 * Checks are cached and rate-limited: an update check on every panel poll would
 * hit the registry hundreds of times per session for an answer that changes
 * daily.
 */

import { execFile } from 'node:child_process';
import { promisify } from 'node:util';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile);

const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));

/** How long a registry answer stays valid. Releases rarely ship hourly. */
const CHECK_TTL_MS = 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

/** A registry call should never hold up a panel request. */
const CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000;

/**
 * Where this plugin came from, which decides how it can be updated.
 *
 * `registry`  installed from npm — update with npm
 * `link`      a `link:` or `file:` dependency — a development checkout, and
 *             overwriting a developer's working tree would be destructive
 * `git`       a working copy; git is the right update tool
 */
function installKind() {
  const NAME = 'dsh-rea-plugin';

  try {
    /**
     * Walk up from the running module looking for the manifest that *declares*
     * this plugin as a dependency. That manifest is the DSH profile, and its
     * dependency spec is the only reliable statement of how the plugin got here:
     * `link:` and `file:` mean a local checkout, a version range means the
     * registry.
     *
     * The previous version looked for the old package name and also read `deps`
     * outside its scope, so it always fell through to `unknown`.
     */
    let dir = HERE;
    let spec = null;
    let foundSelf = false;

    for (let i = 0; i < 8; i += 1) {
      const manifest = path.join(dir, 'package.json');
      if (existsSync(manifest)) {
        try {
          const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(manifest, 'utf8'));

          if (pkg.name === NAME) {
            // Our own manifest: keep walking, the profile is further up.
            foundSelf = true;
          } else {
            const deps = {
              ...(pkg.dependencies ?? {}),
              ...(pkg.devDependencies ?? {}),
              ...(pkg.peerDependencies ?? {}),
            };
            if (typeof deps[NAME] === 'string') {
              spec = deps[NAME];
              break;
            }
          }
        } catch {
          // An unreadable manifest is not the profile; keep walking.
        }
      }

      const parent = path.dirname(dir);
      if (parent === dir) break;
      dir = parent;
    }

    if (spec !== null) {
      if (spec.startsWith('link:') || spec.startsWith('file:')) {
        return { kind: 'link', detail: spec };
      }
      return { kind: 'registry', detail: spec };
    }

    // No declaring manifest: this is the package directory itself, run directly.
    if (foundSelf || existsSync(path.join(HERE, '..', 'package.json'))) {
      if (existsSync(path.join(HERE, '..', '..', '..', '.git'))) {
        return { kind: 'git', detail: 'git 检出' };
      }
      return { kind: 'self', detail: '运行中的包目录' };
    }

    return { kind: 'unknown', detail: null };
  } catch {
    return { kind: 'unknown', detail: null };
  }
}

/** The version of the installed manifest, read from disk rather than memory. */
function installedVersion() {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(HERE, '..', 'package.json'), 'utf8')).version ?? null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/** Compare two semver strings. Returns -1, 0, or 1; prerelease sorts below release. */
export function compareVersions(a, b) {
  const parse = (value) => {
    const [core, pre] = String(value ?? '0.0.0').split('-');
    const nums = core.split('.').map((part) => Number.parseInt(part, 10) || 0);
    while (nums.length < 3) nums.push(0);
    return { nums, pre: pre ?? null };
  };

  const left = parse(a);
  const right = parse(b);

  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) {
    if (left.nums[i] !== right.nums[i]) return left.nums[i] > right.nums[i] ? 1 : -1;
  }

  // A release outranks its own prereleases: 1.0.0 > 1.0.0-beta.1
  if (left.pre === right.pre) return 0;
  if (left.pre === null) return 1;
  if (right.pre === null) return -1;
  return left.pre > right.pre ? 1 : -1;
}

/**
 * Ask the registry for the latest published version.
 *
 * `npm view` rather than a bare registry GET because it honours the user's
 * configured registry, proxy, and auth — the same settings that would install
 * the update later.
 */
/**
 * Hard switch for the registry check.
 *
 * Set `REA_UPDATE_CHECK=1` (or pass `updateCheck: true` in the plugin config)
 * to enable it. Off means `status()` answers immediately with
 * `skipped: true` — no process spawn, no timeout, no misleading advice.
 */
let updateCheckEnabled = process.env.REA_UPDATE_CHECK === '1';

/** Flip the switch at runtime, from plugin config. */
export function setUpdateCheckEnabled(enabled) {
  updateCheckEnabled = Boolean(enabled);
}

/** Whether the registry check will actually run. */
export function isUpdateCheckEnabled() {
  return updateCheckEnabled;
}

/**
 * Commit count behind the upstream branch.
 *
 * Uses `git rev-list --count HEAD..@{u}` after a fetch. A missing remote, no
 * network, or a non-checkout all return null rather than a wrong number.
 */
async function gitBehind() {
  const root = path.join(HERE, '..');

  if (!existsSync(path.join(root, '.git'))) return null;

  try {
    await execFileAsync('git', ['fetch', '--quiet'], {
      cwd: root,
      timeout: CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS,
      windowsHide: true,
    });

    const { stdout } = await execFileAsync(
      'git',
      ['rev-list', '--count', 'HEAD..@{u}'],
      { cwd: root, timeout: CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS, windowsHide: true },
    );

    const count = Number.parseInt(String(stdout ?? '0').trim(), 10);
    return Number.isFinite(count) ? count : null;
  } catch {
    // No upstream configured, offline, or not a repository.
    return null;
  }
}

async function fetchLatest() {
  const { stdout } = await execFileAsync(
    process.platform === 'win32' ? 'npm.cmd' : 'npm',
    ['view', 'dsh-plugin-rea', 'version', '--json'],
    {
      timeout: CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS,
      shell: process.platform === 'win32',
      windowsHide: true,
    },
  );

  const text = String(stdout ?? '').trim();
  if (!text) return null;
  try {
    return JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    // Some npm versions print the bare string without JSON quoting.
    return text.replace(/^"|"$/g, '');
  }
}

/**
 * The update checker.
 *
 * One instance per plugin, so the cache and any in-flight request are shared by
 * every route and every panel poll.
 */
export class UpdateChecker {
  constructor({ packageName = 'dsh-plugin-rea' } = {}) {
    this.packageName = packageName;
    this.cached = null;
    this.inflight = null;
    this.lastError = null;
  }

  /** Cached answer, or a fresh one if it is stale. Never throws. */
  async status({ force = false } = {}) {
    const now = Date.now();
    const current = installedVersion();
    const kind = installKind();

    /**
     * The registry check is opt-in. Answer immediately when it is off: no
     * spawn, no timeout, and no version comparison against a package that may
     * share this name but not this author.
     */
    if (!updateCheckEnabled) {
      return {
        current,
        latest: null,
        checkedAt: now,
        available: false,
        upToDate: false,
        ahead: false,
        installKind: kind,
        skipped: true,
        gitBehind: await gitBehind(),
        reason: '已关闭 npm 检查（通过 GitHub 分发）',
        error: null,
        command: null,
        hint: kind.kind === 'git' || kind.kind === 'link' || kind.kind === 'self'
          ? '从 GitHub 更新：git pull 后重启 DSH'
          : null,
      };
    }

    if (!force && this.cached && now - this.cached.checkedAt < CHECK_TTL_MS) {
      return this.cached;
    }

    // Collapse concurrent polls onto one registry call.
    if (this.inflight) return this.inflight;

    this.inflight = (async () => {
      let latest = null;
      let error = null;

      try {
        latest = await fetchLatest();
      } catch (failure) {
        // Offline, or the package is not published yet. Both are normal and
        // neither should look like a broken plugin.
        error = failure?.message ?? String(failure);
        error = /E404|404|not found/i.test(error)
          ? '尚未发布到 npm'
          : error.slice(0, 200);
      }

      const comparison = latest && current ? compareVersions(latest, current) : 0;

      const result = {
        current,
        latest,
        checkedAt: now,
        available: comparison > 0,
        upToDate: comparison === 0,
        ahead: comparison < 0,
        installKind: kind,
        error,
        /**
         * The command that actually performs this update on this machine.
         *
         * A linked checkout is refreshed by rebuilding it, not by npm — running
         * the npm command there would replace a developer's source directory
         * with a published tarball.
         */
        command: kind.kind === 'link' || kind.kind === 'self'
          ? null
          : `npm install ${this.packageName}@latest`,
        hint: kind.kind === 'link'
          ? '这是本地开发副本，更新走 git pull 或重新构建'
          : kind.kind === 'self'
            ? '当前是包目录本身，更新请用包管理器重装'
            : null,
      };

      this.cached = result;
      this.lastError = error;
      return result;
    })();

    try {
      return await this.inflight;
    } finally {
      this.inflight = null;
    }
  }

  /** Forget the cache so the next call asks again. */
  invalidate() {
    this.cached = null;
  }
}

/**
 * Fingerprint of the shipped skill files.
 *
 * Skills are installed by copying, so a plugin upgrade does not refresh the
 * copies already on disk. Hashing the package's own skills lets the panel say
 * "技能与插件版本不一致，重新部署" instead of leaving the user with a silently
 * stale skill.
 */
export function skillsFingerprint() {
  const dir = path.join(HERE, '..', 'skills');
  const hash = createHash('sha256');
  try {
    const files = readdirSync(dir).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.md')).sort();
    for (const name of files) {
      hash.update(name);
      hash.update(readFileSync(path.join(dir, name), 'utf8'));
    }
    return hash.digest('hex').slice(0, 12);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}
```
