`vendor/rea-docs/docs/ghidra-provider.md`:

```md
# Ghidra provider semantics

REA imports one target into an ephemeral Ghidra database. Linux/macOS support
read-only analysis and atomic function-name/entry-comment edits; Windows P0 is
read-only. GUI controls and persistent database mutation are unavailable.
Executable bytes remain unchanged.

Use [installation](installation.md#ghidra) for supported hosts, prerequisites,
configuration, startup deadlines, resource controls, and cleanup recovery.
[Linux Ghidra launches](installation.md#linux-owned-process-prerequisite) also
require a procps-compatible `ps` on REA's `PATH` for process ownership checks.
[Windows P0](windows-ghidra-p0.md) has its own admission and lifecycle boundary;
[NativeAOT observations](ghidra-nativeaot.md) include a built-in read-only PE
snapshot parser and a separate optional annotation extension. Check the
[release boundary](installation.md#released-package-and-main) when using npm.

See [import language and analysis seeds](installation.md#ghidra-import-language-and-analysis-seeds)
to override the header-detected language or seed analysis.

Provider selection and profile identity follow
[MCP contracts](mcp-contracts.md#identity-and-discovery). One deep
provider stays bound to the target; runtime failure never selects another
provider automatically. The contracts below describe Ghidra observations,
not equivalence with another engine's pseudocode or analysis database.

## Admitted inventory semantics

| Concern          | Ghidra contract                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Program identity | One `analyzeHeadless` import produces exactly one Program; `list_documents` therefore returns exactly one name.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Addresses        | Default memory uses lowercase `0x` hexadecimal. Non-default and external spaces use `<percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>` and remain round-trippable. The handshake commits image base and default address-space name.                                                                              |
| Symbols          | `list_names` includes address-bearing memory and external symbols, including dynamic symbols, while excluding variable and no-address namespace records. Each item reports primary, dynamic, external, symbol type, and source facts.                                                           |
| Procedures       | Both non-external and external functions are listed. A local thunk remains distinct from its resolved target; exact and qualified name lookup fails on ambiguity rather than guessing.                                                                                                          |
| Strings          | Only Ghidra-defined string `Data` is observed. Items report charset, byte length, and whether a required null terminator is missing. The API cannot distinguish a present terminator from fixed/Pascal layouts when no terminator is missing, so that state is named `present_or_not_required`. |
| Memory           | Memory-block end addresses are exclusive. Read/write/execute, initialization, overlay, address space, and image base are direct Ghidra observations.                                                                                                                                            |
| Inventory        | Procedure, symbol, and string listings plus searches return the complete matching collection in one response; callers do not provide offsets or result-count limits.                                                                                                                            |
| Search           | Literal and Java-regex searches return every match in the immutable provider-defined inventory; string search does not cover every text sequence in artifact bytes. Search waits for a reply or caller cancellation; there are no caller-supplied offsets or result-count limits.               |
| Analysis state   | The socket is exposed only after default auto-analysis completes. Established operations wait for their reply or caller cancellation; there is no fixed response-size ceiling.                                                                                                                  |

String-search completeness applies only to Ghidra-defined string `Data`. Packed
or undefined literals, including Rust strings, may be absent; an empty result
does not prove text is absent. Both list and search Evidence carry this
limitation. When an address is known, use `read_bytes` and `xrefs` to inspect
bytes and references.

## PE debug-symbol coverage

The post-analysis handshake reports Ghidra's PDB Program Information attributes:
the referenced file, GUID, hexadecimal age, legacy signature, version, and
`PDB Loaded` state. Absent attributes remain null. PE Evidence carries a
limitation when a PDB reference is present but Ghidra reports it as not loaded,
or its load state is unknown. A bridge without this report leaves PDB coverage
unknown. A reported loaded state is a Ghidra observation, not an independent
PDB identity or complete symbol-coverage attestation, and retains an inline
coverage caveat. Handshake PDB strings share a 4096 UTF-16-unit serialization
budget (at most 24 KiB after JSON escaping); whole attributes that do not fit
are omitted with an explicit resource limitation, rather than truncated.

Original names and types may be missing even when auto-analysis completes.
An empty name search does not establish that a function is absent; use
`list_procedures` and address-based analysis to inspect recovered functions.
REA imports a private executable copy and does not admit a caller-selected
PDB companion. This reporting does not search symbol servers, copy a sibling
PDB, or change analyzer settings.

## Loaded addresses and file offsets

Ghidra computes overview procedure and string counts from the same inventories
used by `list_procedures` and `list_strings`, without transporting those rows
solely to count them. Counts include external functions and only Ghidra-defined
strings; they do not establish discovery of unidentified functions or undefined
string bytes. Complete inventories remain available through the list tools.
Overview reuse follows the target/profile snapshot lifetime and is invalidated
by session metadata edits.

`rea analyze <path> --provider ghidra --json` and MCP `binary_overview` report
the observed loaded `image_base` in `normalized_result`. They retain each
segment's reported `image_base` and `address_space`. A provider that does not
report a base, or whose segments disagree, omits the overview field, following
the existing contract on main. REA does not substitute zero or the first
segment's address. All reported bases and address spaces remain visible in the
complete segment inventory, including conflicting observations.

`function` and most MCP procedure selectors use procedure names or
provider analysis addresses. Ghidra `decompile` / MCP `procedure_pseudo_code`
also accept source-file byte offsets. Existing symbols and analysis addresses
take precedence; a `0x`-prefixed number that resolves to no procedure falls back
to its observed source mapping. Use `--file-offset=0x...` on the CLI or
`procedure: "file-offset:0x..."` through MCP to select file coordinates explicitly.
Multiple mapping candidates fail as ambiguous rather than selecting a bank or
address space. A successful conversion retains the file offset, mapped address
and procedure entry in raw Evidence and `locations`.

If an offset maps to loaded target bytes but no procedure starts at or contains
the mapped address, the failure preserves both the original file offset and
analysis address. This differs from an unmapped offset and does not recommend
retrying the same offset syntax.
If the function resolves but the backend fails or cancels decompilation, the
failure retains the selector, mapped address and procedure entry without
changing the backend failure code.

Both mapping directions require a complete original `FileBytes` source whose
SHA-256 matches the admitted target. Auxiliary files and partial source objects
remain visible in the load-image inventory but do not establish offsets in the
original target. Ghidra's object-local offsets are not silently treated as
original-file coordinates. Original-source identity is checked once per source
object per session; analysis-memory edits do not change the original bytes.

ELF virtual addresses and file offsets are
different coordinates. Ghidra can rebase a PIE ELF during import: in the
source-owned verification fixture, ELF entry `0x1013` becomes Ghidra procedure
`0x101013` with image base `0x100000`. That example is not a general conversion
rule.

Use `list_procedures` to select an observed procedure address. To relate file
bytes to loaded memory, call MCP `inspect_native_load_image` or:

```sh
rea search <path> . --kind procedures --mode regex --provider ghidra --json
rea inspect-native-load-image <path> --provider ghidra --json
rea decompile <path> <observed-procedure-address> --provider ghidra --json
rea decompile <path> --file-offset=0x1013 --provider ghidra --json
rea address-to-file-offset <path> <observed-procedure-address> --provider ghidra --json
```

The load-image result preserves source-file indexes, file offsets, address
spaces, and inclusive mapping ranges. Follow the mapping for the selected
source file and region; adding `image_base` to an arbitrary file offset is not
valid. For a linear byte-addressed, file-backed mapping, a file offset `F` in
`[mapping.file_offset, mapping.file_offset + mapping.length)` maps to
`mapping.start + (F - mapping.file_offset)` in the reported `address_space`.
If several mappings cover the same file offset, keep those candidates distinct
and select the procedure from the observed inventory. Uninitialized regions may
have no file backing. ELF mappings are observed
without independent format-specific load-image verification, as the result's
status and limitations state.

An unsuccessful numeric procedure lookup reports the current Ghidra image base
and gives the CLI commands above alongside the corresponding MCP operations.
Repeat any target-format, architecture, and entry-point options used to open the
target. Other procedure operations keep their analysis-address semantics;
file-offset fallback applies only to decompilation.

Overview workflow revision 3 binds this output to snapshot identity. Older
serialized overview Evidence remains readable; it is not replayed as a current
overview merely because its source artifact is unchanged.

## Admitted function-analysis semantics

Concurrent callers share one startup while retaining independent cancellation.
Only the final departing caller abandons startup and waits for its cleanup.
New attempts wait for that cleanup; failed cleanup retains its original error
and owned directories until a successful close. Closing the provider reports a
provider-state failure to live callers rather than cancelling their signals.

Configured analysis extensions and seeds use owned file reads during profile
resolution and launch snapshots. A changed read extent or descriptor state
refuses the commitment. Failed source or snapshot descriptor closes remain
owned and block new admission until cleanup succeeds; the physical failure
and exact cancellation reason remain available. Provider shutdown joins all
profile stages before retrying their retained descriptors.

| Concern                 | Ghidra contract                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Decompiler lifetime     | One persistent `DecompInterface` is opened for the imported Program and disposed during bridge shutdown. Native decompilation has no fixed per-function deadline. External functions or functions without bodies return `null`; cancellation and native failure remain distinct.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Serialization           | A FIFO sends one Program request at a time. Caller cancellation removes queued work promptly and is passed to active socket waits. This is an adapter safety commitment, not a claim that every Ghidra API is thread-safe.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Function identity       | Every function result carries the entry address and Ghidra FunctionManager classification for external, thunk, and resolved thunk target. These are observations, not proof that unresolved targetless calls have been recovered.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Assembly and pseudocode | Assembly is complete Ghidra Listing text; pseudocode is Ghidra decompiler output. Neither is original source, and cross-provider comparison never treats Hopper and Ghidra text as equal or unequal semantic facts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Instruction fast path   | `read_function_instructions` returns every raw Listing instruction for the requested function without invoking the decompiler or whole-program name/string inventories.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Calls and references    | Callers/callees contain only resolved functions. Reference edges preserve exact ReferenceManager type and call/jump/data/read/write/indirect/computed/conditional/terminal/external facts. Targetless computed flow remains unknown. Synthetic entry-point references without actionable memory sources are omitted explicitly.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| CFG                     | Dossiers use `BasicBlockModel` and retain only non-call successors inside the function body. CFG topology is address-normalized for comparison; provider-specific block construction remains a declared difference.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P-code value flow       | Function dossiers include up to 3,000 high-p-code operations, at most 64 inputs per operation, and 12,000 def-use edges. Results identify memory reads/writes, branches, and calls by p-code opcode, and mark decompiler-dead operations. Large results report truncation, an omitted-operation lower bound, and known omitted-input/edge counts. The dossier is an intra-function graph; `trace_native_values` composes derived parameter/argument and return/output dependencies across resolved calls. It does not resolve memory aliasing, call side effects, runtime behavior, persistent state, or business meaning. |
| Result extent           | Function instruction scans and native API boundary observations remain complete. P-code flow is the explicit bounded exception; its count fields distinguish exact retained counts from lower-bound or known-omitted counts. Caller cancellation and provider failures remain distinct.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

Function extents and instruction completeness refer to Ghidra's analyzed body.
An inferred no-return call can terminate that body before subsequent bytes.
Pseudocode, assembly, procedure info, instruction windows, incoming and outgoing
references, callee and caller reads, and dossiers report observed terminal call sites in Evidence limitations,
including resolved callee names, addresses, and FunctionManager flags when
available. On x86-32, the same views also report the exact Borland/Delphi-style
FS exception-registration pattern when its handler address falls outside the
function body. This is a static registration observation; it does not establish
handler execution or change the body. Instruction windows and dossiers also
retain these warnings in their result limitations. An unresolved callee or
unestablished terminal-flow basis remains explicit. These observations qualify
the analysis; they do not prove that a no-return flag is incorrect or recover
excluded code. Analysis profiles version this observation contract so older
snapshots cannot replay unqualified results.

On non-Windows hosts, the ephemeral import repair clears no-return flags on the
known returning external ABI names `malloc`, `__tls_get_addr`, `memcpy`, `memset`,
`strlen`, and `__errno_location`. This relies on their expected ABI behavior;
external implementations are not inspected. The repair re-disassembles affected
terminal calls and refits their owning functions, preserving independent function
entries. If a recovered caller reveals a decoded return, its propagated no-return
flag and affected callers are repaired in the same pass. Unknown imports and
genuine no-return imports keep their flags. Analysis profiles version this repair
so snapshots produced before it are not reused. Windows P0 does not run it.

`npm run verify:ghidra` compiles the versioned C oracle into debug and stripped
host-native targets (x86-64/AArch64 ELF on Linux or Mach-O on macOS), plus a native
DWARF 4 type-layout object. It proves the admitted operations, external functions, resolved thunks, exports, stripped-name
behavior, direct and targetless indirect calls, typed references, strings/xrefs,
multi-block CFG, bounded p-code def-use/effect links, semantic enhanced workflows, cancellation, startup deadlines,
serialized concurrency, malformed-target rejection, profile identity, and
process/project cleanup against real Ghidra 12.1.4. Unit fixtures separately
cover startup deadlines, process exit, queued cancellation, and malformed wire
output.

`npm run verify:ghidra:cross-format` adds AArch64 ELF, x86-64 PE, and x86-64
Mach-O target coverage. It requires `clang`, LLD, and `lld-link`; set
`REA_CLANG`, `REA_LLD`, or `REA_LLD_LINK` to select them. The verifier checks
these tools before compilation. Keeping this matrix separate lets Linux
host/provider acceptance run with only the host compiler.

`npm run verify:ghidra:windows` checks source-owned native x86-64 PE applications;
`-- --x86`, `-- --arm`, or `-- --arm64` selects another target architecture;
`-- --dll` selects DLLs. Choose one architecture and optionally combine it with
`--dll`. These static fixtures contain source-owned encoded instructions; they
are not compiler-produced programs. See the [Windows verification scope](windows-ghidra-p0.md#native-authority-and-target-identity)
for real-provider coverage and exclusions.
These lanes check all 26 read-only operations, target/snapshot/import SHA-256 linkage,
and project, endpoint, process, and runtime cleanup. The independent native
lane checks DACLs, handle admission, cancellation, and Job Object lifecycle.
`npm run verify:ghidra:windows:package` packs and installs REA into an isolated
prefix, then checks ordinary-user CLI/MCP operations against canonical contracts.
It accepts the same architecture and DLL flags and verifies the selected PE role
in the analysis profile.
All lanes require matching native controls; package startup alone establishes
only package compatibility.

## Masked byte search

`search_bytes` (`rea search-bytes PATH '48 8B ?? ?? 89' --provider ghidra`)
searches initialized analyzed memory, including loader fixups. Supply hexadecimal
byte pairs, with `??` for any byte. An optional equal-length hexadecimal `mask`
selects bits: `pattern: "a0"`, `mask: "f0"` matches bytes from `a0` through `af`.
Wildcards remain unconstrained even with an explicit mask. At least one bit
must be constrained.

Optional `start` and `end` addresses are inclusive and select one address space.
A match must end at or before `end`, so `end` set inside a match excludes it.
Without bounds, loaded memory blocks are eligible, in Ghidra address order.
Blocks that are not loaded (file parts such as `.symtab`) and overlay blocks are
listed in `searched.skipped_not_loaded` and are not searched; pass `start` or
`end` in their address space to search them.
Overlapping matches are included; matches never cross block boundaries.
Each match reports its address, segment, unique source file offset (or null),
and containing procedure (or null).

Pages default to 100 matches and accept 1 to 1000. Pass `next_cursor` as `cursor`
with the same target, profile, pattern, mask and bounds to continue. `complete`
means no further matches remain. `searched.blocks` and `searched.bytes` describe
the inclusive memory ranges examined for this page, including lookahead for the
next match. Coverage can overlap between pages; do not sum it as unique memory.
`searched.skipped_uninitialized` lists eligible uninitialized blocks on every
page. These blocks are never searched. Cancellation returns a typed error,
discards the active Ghidra database, and does not return a successful partial page.
Hopper byte search remains unavailable until its implementation is verified.

```

`vendor/rea-docs/docs/ghidra-psp.md`:

```md
# PSP static ELF analysis through Ghidra

This specialization builds on [generic MIPS support](ghidra-mips.md) for
[#1330](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/1330). It reuses REA's existing
CLI/MCP, Ghidra bridge, Evidence and snapshot workflows. Allegrex instructions,
PSP loading and calling conventions remain owned by
[ghidra-allegrex](https://github.com/kotcrab/ghidra-allegrex).

## Initial boundary

The initial profile is limited to Linux x64, little-endian ELF32 `ET_EXEC`,
`EM_MIPS` and the PSPSDK declaration `e_flags=0x10a23001`. Those bits declare
MIPS II, Allegrex, EABI32 and NOREORDER; they are not proof of every instruction's
semantics. The profile also requires an inspected version-0 MIPS ABI flags
record declaring ISA level 2/revision 0, 32-bit GPR and CPR1, no CPR2,
single-precision hard float (`fpAbi=2`), no ISA extension or ASEs,
`flags1=1` and `flags2=0`. These are the declarations independently reported by
PSPDEV v20261001's GNU readelf 2.44 and its 24-byte section dump. Missing,
uninspected, contradictory and other producer declarations are refused.
The PSP profile is not an exception to the generic MIPS32r2/o32 policy; that
separate gate is unchanged. Profile revision v2 records this corrected boundary.

PRX, relocatable/shared images, PBP/ISO/CSO containers, runtime emulation and live
code overlays are outside this first profile. Other hosts and flag combinations
are not silently admitted. File names do not identify a PSP target.

## Bring your own compatible extension

Install the extension in the selected Ghidra distribution at
`$GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR/Ghidra/Extensions/ghidra-allegrex`, with its
`Module.manifest`, `extension.properties`, language files and loader JARs.
User-home installations are not searched because REA uses an isolated analysis
home. REA never downloads, installs, rebuilds or vendors the extension.

The published compatibility experiment used Ghidra **12.1.3**, extension
**v21.4**, PSPDEV **v20261001** and JDK 21. New public-provider results must be
reported separately from that historical bridge experiment. The extension's
`version` property declares its compatible **Ghidra version**, not its release
tag; the property must match the selected installation. Other same-version
builds are not described as independently verified merely because they pass
this metadata check. A malformed or unloadable extension still fails real import.

REA fingerprints installed extension files before resolving the analysis
profile and checks that identity again immediately before launch. Symlinks,
nonregular files, missing components and incompatible metadata are refused.
Inspection is bounded to 1,024 entries, 16 directory levels and 64 MiB, with
streamed file hashing and 64 KiB properties. Rebuilds or content changes yield a
different profile; an old snapshot is not silently reused with the new profile.
This is content identity, not a signature or a sandbox for installed code.
Do not modify the Ghidra installation while a session is running.

## Ordinary public interfaces

```bash
rea analyze /absolute/path/to/psp.elf --provider ghidra --json
rea function /absolute/path/to/psp.elf function_name --provider ghidra --json
```

MCP uses `open_binary` with an absolute path and `provider_id: "ghidra"`, then
ordinary inventory and function operations. The loader is explicitly
`PspElfLoader`, language `Allegrex:LE:32:default`, compiler `default`. The
handshake must confirm the language and compiler before serving observations.
Missing prerequisites return `PSP_EXTENSION_UNAVAILABLE` with an installation
remedy; no provider fallback or automatic installation occurs.

Evidence retains the `mips` architecture family and its PSP-specific profile,
including extension content identity. It also carries the VFPU and static-only
limitations. The extension does not model VFPU prefix effects completely;
nonempty decompiled code is not proof of correct vector behavior. Existing
session-local metadata editing does not change executable bytes or turn a
snapshot into a persistent Ghidra project.

## Verification

Use the existing real MIPS verifier with its PSP option. Required tools are
caller-supplied `make`, `psp-config`, `psp-gcc`, `psp-readelf`, `psp-objdump`,
`PSPDEV`, `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` and a compatible `JAVA_HOME`.

```bash
npm run build:cached
node scripts/verify-real-ghidra-mips.mjs --psp
# In a disposable installation without Allegrex, test actual public refusals:
node scripts/verify-real-ghidra-mips.mjs --psp-missing-extension
# Generic MIPS must remain generic with Allegrex installed:
npm run verify:ghidra:mips
```

The generic verifier also exercises a section-truncated firmware fixture. That
check uses generic MIPS symbols and language expectations and runs only in generic
mode; the PSP report explicitly records carved-PSP coverage as not run.

The maintained PSP fixture builds from `tests/conformance/psp/`, never executes,
and is independent of commercial game data. PSP GNU tools supply ELF/ABI,
raw ABI-record, symbol and encoding observations; REA's parsed target and saved
snapshot must agree with the independent ABI declaration. Public CLI/MCP must
recover known functions, a direct
call, the immediate `0x1234`, BITREV, a global word and a marker. The verifier
checks observed loader/language, original bytes, Evidence, snapshot reopening,
and an A-B-A target switch with different global contents at the same address.
A snapshot for A must not open B. Cleanup must finish before success is reported.

These checks are selected static facts, not full behavioral equivalence, VFPU
semantics or arbitrary PSP compatibility. Independently published PSP binaries
are supplemental calibration targets after payload classification and license
review; unsupported PRX/PBP must not count as a successful static-ELF case.

`vendor/rea-docs/docs/ghidra-riscv.md`:

```md
# RISC-V ELF analysis through Ghidra

This lane extends native ELF analysis for `EM_RISCV` targets. It does not
execute RISC-V code, emulate a boot sequence, or rehost firmware. It addresses
[#2063](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/2063) and follows the same
lane shape as [generic MIPS support](ghidra-mips.md).

## Admission boundary

ELF `EM_RISCV` (243) is retained as the provider-neutral `riscv` family. The
target also retains the raw ELF declarations that decide a lane: class, byte
order, `e_type`, and `e_flags`. Recognition does not mean every provider or
RISC-V variant is supported. Existing PE, managed and Mach-O architecture sets
are unchanged. Headerless inputs use the separate [raw-binary admission
boundary](raw-binary.md); raw RISC-V images are not supported.

The Ghidra lane admits little-endian ELF32 and ELF64 `ET_EXEC` images that
declare `EF_RISCV_FLOAT_ABI_DOUBLE` in `e_flags`, with no `EF_RISCV_RVE`,
`EF_RISCV_TSO`, or any bit outside `EF_RISCV_RVC | EF_RISCV_FLOAT_ABI`. These are
header declarations, not proof that every instruction conforms to that ISA.

Provider selection returns the specific unsupported constraint rather than
guessing a compatible profile:

| Declaration                                     | Outcome                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Little-endian ELF64 `ET_EXEC`, double-float ABI | admitted, `RISCV:LE:64:default` + `gcc`                                                  |
| Little-endian ELF32 `ET_EXEC`, double-float ABI | admitted, `RISCV:LE:32:default` + `gcc`                                                  |
| Big-endian                                      | refused; Ghidra 12.1.4 ships no big-endian RISC-V language                               |
| `ET_REL`, `ET_DYN`, other `e_type`              | refused with the declared value                                                          |
| `EF_RISCV_RVE`                                  | refused; the embedded 16-register profile (x0–x15) needs its own processor specification |
| `EF_RISCV_TSO`                                  | refused; the total-store-order memory model is unverified here                           |
| Soft, single, or quad float ABI                 | refused; the pinned generic compiler specification models double-float                   |
| Reserved or newer `e_flags` bits                | refused with the offending bits named                                                    |

`e_type` is the only load-shape declaration this lane reads. A fixed-address
`ET_EXEC` declaration does **not** establish static linkage: `PT_INTERP` and
dynamic dependencies are not inspected, and the session records that boundary as
a limitation rather than inferring a load model.

## Why the language is pinned

Ghidra's header-based selection is not reliable for RV32. The 12.1.4
`riscv.opinion` pins `variant="default"` for the 64-bit constraint and leaves the
32-bit constraint unpinned with the comment that the loader "must choose between
'default' and 'AndeStar' variants". Measured against the installed release tree:

| Fixture                                         | Ghidra auto-selection         |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| RV64 ELF, `e_flags 0x5` (RVC, double-float ABI) | `RISCV:LE:64:default:gcc`     |
| RV32 ELF, `e_flags 0x5`, no Andes declaration   | `RISCV:LE:32:AndeStar_v5:gcc` |

So an ordinary RV32 image lands on an Andes processor model unless the language
is stated. REA therefore pins `RISCV:LE:32:default` or `RISCV:LE:64:default`
with the `gcc` compiler specification per class, records
`language_selection: provider-pinned-v1`, and refuses a caller-selected
`REA_GHIDRA_LANGUAGE_ID` or `REA_GHIDRA_COMPILER_SPEC_ID` that disagrees with the
pin without changing the requested override. An override that matches the pin is
accepted and recorded as `configured-v1`.

## Evidence

The lane identity is `elf32-exec-le-double-float-generic-v1` or
`elf64-exec-le-double-float-generic-v1`, and `riscv_elf` retains `elf_class`,
`byte_order`, `type`, and the raw `flags` alongside the read-only booleans
`float_abi_double`, `rvc_declared`, `rve_declared`, and `tso_declared`. Those
fields report declarations the header makes; none of them is evidence of the
original compiler, of instruction conformance, or of a floating-point calling
convention beyond the ABI the pinned language models.

## Verification and limits

Ghidra 12.1.4 PUBLIC with a 64-bit JDK 21+ is required, and on macOS the release
tree ships no host decompiler binary, so `Decompiler/os/<platform>/decompile` and
`sleigh` must come from your own build; see
[installation](installation.md#ghidra).

Run `npm run verify:ghidra:riscv` with an existing Ghidra 12.1.4 installation,
JDK 21+, and a RISC-V-capable Clang, LLD and LLVM readelf. The verifier acquires
no tools and never executes target code. Select installed tools explicitly when
they are not on `PATH`:

```sh
GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=/path/to/ghidra_12.1.4_PUBLIC \
JAVA_HOME=/path/to/jdk-21 \
REA_RISCV_CLANG=/path/to/llvm/bin/clang \
REA_RISCV_LLD=/path/to/lld/bin/ld.lld \
REA_RISCV_READELF=/path/to/llvm/bin/llvm-readelf \
npm run verify:ghidra:riscv
```

The lane builds the committed freestanding C and assembly sources into RV32 and
RV64 `ET_EXEC` fixtures. Independent LLVM readelf observations establish ELF
declarations and symbol addresses. Public CLI and stdio MCP workflows verify
function enumeration, decompilation, pinned language/compiler identity, decoded
probe bytes, global data, and direct calls. It validates advertised MCP output
schemas and both JSON representations, saves and reopens snapshots, rejects
header-mutated soft-float and unsupported high-bit declarations, and checks
unchanged source bytes and owned cleanup. Failures retain the diagnostic
workspace; successful runs remove it and report the observed process lineage.

Module tests cover admission and malformed headers. Call-graph completeness,
string inventories, dynamic linkage, Andes or RVE/TSO images, and big-endian
targets are **not** established by this lane. `.riscv.attributes` ISA extensions
are not inspected; the generic language pin remains an analysis convention.

`vendor/rea-docs/docs/go-binaries.md`:

```md
# Go binary build metadata

`inspect_go_binary` / `inspect-go-binary` answers which Go compiler version,
modules, replacements and build settings are embedded in one selected local
executable or library. It reads the file without running it and requires no
Go installation, active binary target, Hopper, Ghidra or IDA.

```bash

```

The CLI resolves relative paths against the caller's working directory. MCP
requires an absolute filesystem path and preserves that exact selection:

```json
{
  "name": "inspect_go_binary",
  "arguments": { "path": "/artifacts/application" }
}
```

For build identity and counts, select `detail: "summary"`. MCP retains the same
complete Evidence and returns `normalized_result.parent_evidence_id`. Read
selected dependency versions without reopening the file:

```json
{
  "name": "inspect_analysis_view",
  "arguments": {
    "source": {
      "kind": "retained-evidence",
      "evidence_id": "ev_<parent digest>"
    },
    "view": {
      "kind": "go",
      "collection": "dependencies",
      "paths": ["golang.org/x/crypto"],
      "fields": ["path", "version", "replacement"],
      "offset": 0,
      "limit": 10
    }
  }
}
```

Go views support `dependencies` (exact `paths`) and `settings` (exact `keys`),
optional original `indices`, field selection, and pagination. Filters intersect;
empty filter arrays select no rows and `fields: []` returns only row identity.
Each row keeps its original `index`, scoped to the parent Evidence and collection;
duplicate module paths and setting keys keep distinct indices. Page offsets
count matching records. Exhausting retained rows does not establish complete
runtime dependencies. Original bytes, unknown lines and all complete metadata
remain in the parent and can be exported as an Evidence bundle.

One-shot CLI summaries save complete Evidence before returning the projection:

```bash
rea inspect-go-binary ./application --detail summary --evidence_output ./go-evidence.json --json
```

`--evidence_output` is required for CLI summary delivery and never overwrites an
existing file. The default CLI/MCP reply remains complete.

[Measured workflows](../experiments/analysis-efficiency/go-build-views.md) include
catalog repetition and extra calls. Identity/count questions benefit from a
single summary. In the tested Codex full-catalog configuration, a compound
question about identity and one dependency uses fewer tokens in captured request JSON with
one complete inspection than with a summary followed by a lookup. The complete
reply remains useful for that initial question; retained views support later
selected reads. Token figures are serialization estimates, not model usage.

## Observations

The inline Evidence result contains the artifact path, SHA-256, byte length,
container format, architecture, word size and byte order. A recognized
`build_info` record contains:

- `go_version`, preserved as embedded UTF-8 text rather than forced into a
  semantic version, or `null` when the embedded bytes are not UTF-8;
- `go_version_bytes_base64`, preserving the exact compiler-string bytes;
- exact file offsets and byte lengths for the header, compiler string and module
  string;
- `module_text`, the decoded module-information body, or `null` when the complete
  body cannot be represented as UTF-8;
- `module_bytes_base64`, the original module-string bytes including Go framing;
- `module.path`, the embedded package path;
- `module.main`, the main module's path, version, checksum and optional
  replacement;
- `module.dependencies`, with the same fields and their original order;
- `module.settings`, retaining ordered key/value entries and duplicate keys;
- `module.unparsed_lines`, `module.unparsed_line_bytes_base64` and
  `module.complete`, which says whether every present module-text line was
  parsed. It does not establish that the dependency inventory is complete.

Missing checksums are `null`; empty fields and development/local replacement
versions remain unchanged. Build settings such as `GOOS`, `GOARCH` or `vcs.revision`
are reported when present. Their absence does not establish a build choice.
Go strings may contain arbitrary bytes. Non-UTF-8 records remain available as
base64 while other decodable module records are still reported; the reader does
not insert replacement characters or reject the entire artifact for those
strings.

When no main-module (`mod`) record was decoded, `module.main` is `null` and
dependency coverage is unknown. Successfully decoded dependency records remain
visible. GOPATH-mode builds may contain only a package `path` and build settings;
their empty dependency array does not establish the absence of dependencies.
The result's limitations state this explicitly. A module-mode build with a main
module record and no dependency records has an observed empty dependency list.

## Supported boundary

The built-in TypeScript reader supports ELF, PE and thin Mach-O images with Go's
inline or historical pointer build-info encoding. Source ranges refer to the
original stable file snapshot, including pointer-backed strings. It does not
scan arbitrary byte strings as compiler metadata or interpret a fat Mach-O
container as one selected architecture.

For ELF images without a named build-info section, discovery checks each
nonempty writable, non-executable load segment in program-header order. This
includes sectionless PIE images with metadata in a later data segment. Named
sections retain priority, and alignment, file mapping and record validation
remain required.

Historical moduleless Go binaries can store their empty module-string header in
declared zero-initialized virtual memory rather than file-backed bytes. The reader
recognizes this only when the complete optional module header lies in that memory
without a conflicting file mapping. Its module contents are empty and
`module_location` has zero bytes, anchored at the build-info field containing the
module-header pointer. Compiler strings and other unmapped pointers remain strict
file-backed reads.

`build_info: null` means no recognized record was found in the inspected image.
It does not prove that the binary is not Go. Stripping, old builds, deliberate
removal and obfuscation can limit metadata. A malformed supported container or
recognized build-info record returns an input-format failure. Unsupported
containers receive a separate unsupported-target failure.

Symlinks and nonregular files are rejected. The shared stable reader detects
replacement and observed in-place changes during acquisition. Missing files,
host permission denial, changed artifacts and cancellation retain distinct
errors. The selected file is never modified; this inspection creates no
temporary files, starts no subprocesses and accesses no network endpoint.

An input above 256 MiB returns `resource_constraint` with resource `file-size`
and `reported_limits.maximum_input_bytes`. Select a suitable input within that
fixed allowance; changing an output-write or transport budget does not admit it.

Resource guards bound the selected file and cumulative header searches to 256 MiB
each, aggregate embedded strings
to 1 MiB, structural table decoding to 16 MiB and the complete normalized metadata
report to 8 MiB. Identical search spans with the same virtual alignment are
searched once; partially overlapping spans consume the cumulative search budget
and fail with a CPU resource constraint when it is exhausted. Oversized results
fail without partial success. MCP also applies
its [response transport budget](mcp-contracts.md), which counts both text and
structured content; a report within the metadata limit can still require export
from retained Evidence. These limits are not operating-system memory or CPU
isolation.

Embedded metadata is evidence of file content. It does not authenticate a
compiler, dependency, commit or supply chain, and it does not establish runtime
behavior. Function names, source mappings, types and decompiled code are outside
this tool's coverage. Use the [native workflow](native-investigation.md) when
those questions require a disassembler.

## Real producer verification

`npm run verify:go:binary` exercises compiler-built fixtures through the public
CLI and MCP, comparing their metadata with Go's standard `debug/buildinfo`
reader. The verification lane requires Go; normal inspection does not.

`vendor/rea-docs/docs/godot-pck.md`:

```md
# Godot PCK archives

`inspect-artifact` and `extract-artifact` read ordinary Godot PCK formats 2, 3
and 4 without running the game or requiring Godot. Official Godot 4.4.1, 4.6.1
and 4.7.1 produced these respective formats in verification; other engine
releases have not been verified. Format 1 is unsupported.

Inspection retains the original header and directory facts, including engine
version, flags, declared file count, source paths, offsets and declared MD5.
Observed plaintext bytes receive content-addressed SHA-256 identities. MD5 is a
container integrity claim, separate from the observed SHA-256. A mismatch fails
by default; `--integrity-policy record-and-continue` retains the observed bytes
and an explicit untrusted contradiction. An all-zero MD5 is an unknown claim,
not a verified digest.

## CLI

Start with a compact summary and keep the complete Evidence bundle:

```sh
rea inspect-artifact /artifacts/game.pck --detail summary \
  --evidence_output /evidence/game.json --json
rea extract-artifact /artifacts/game.pck --json
```

Summary delivery requires `--evidence_output` and never overwrites that file.
The response contains `summary` Evidence and an `evidence_bundle` receipt.
Without `--detail summary`, inspection keeps its complete inline delivery.
Extraction creates a new temporary directory and returns its path. It rejects
unsafe paths and verifies container identity before creating output.

The same CLI commands locate a PCK at the beginning of a file or through its
12-byte EOF trailer in an executable carrier. They do not scan arbitrary
payloads or discover packs behind additional trailing signatures. The root
content SHA-256 covers the whole carrier; its content classification remains
native, while the inventory records the PCK role and exact pack bounds.
Ordinary native `open_binary` detection remains unchanged.

## MCP and selected facts

For a standalone pack, call `open_binary` with its absolute path, then
`inspect_artifact` with `{"detail":"summary"}`. The complete inspection and its
nested inventory stay in the session. Use the summary's
`normalized_result.parent_evidence_id` as the source of subsequent views:

```json
{
  "name": "inspect_analysis_view",
  "arguments": {
    "source": {
      "kind": "retained-evidence",
      "evidence_id": "<parent_evidence_id>"
    },
    "view": {
      "kind": "inventory",
      "collection": "occurrences",
      "logical_paths": ["scripts/main.gd", "project.binary"],
      "fields": [
        "logical_path",
        "declared_integrity",
        "hash_status",
        "format_metadata"
      ],
      "offset": 0,
      "limit": 32
    }
  }
}
```

Occurrences retain `occurrence_id`, `artifact_id` and `parent_occurrence_id`
even when `fields` is empty. Batch occurrence IDs with `occurrence_ids`, or
join returned content IDs to `collection: "nodes"`, `artifact_ids: [...]` and
`fields: ["sha256", "size"]`. Filters intersect; an omitted filter selects all
available rows and an empty array selects none. Pagination follows the filtered
canonical order. Multiple occurrences may share one content ID.

Views reuse authenticated immutable inventory facts and lazy lookup indexes;
they do not reopen the source. These are historical observations, including
after the source changes or disappears. Close the target with `close_binary`
when finished. To read an exported bundle through the CLI, select its complete
inspection record as `source: {kind: "inline", evidence: ...}` in a JSON request
file for `rea inspect-analysis-view request.json --json`.

## Coverage and limits

PCK summaries expose root format metadata, available graph counts,
`available_hash_status_counts`, and `source_coverage`. Inventory pages preserve
producer coverage alongside page coverage. `source_complete` means all declared
retained graph rows are available; it does not establish that an encrypted or
otherwise unknown directory was examined. Missing matches in unknown coverage
are not evidence of absence.

Encrypted directories retain their header and declared file count with unknown
entry coverage. Individually encrypted members retain directory metadata with
unknown content identity; REA does not decrypt them. Sparse bundles likewise
retain header facts with unknown member coverage. Extraction refuses an
unreadable directory or encrypted member. This capability does not recover
keys, decode Godot resources, decompile GDScript bytecode, analyze signals,
apply patch/removal entries or execute targets.

Readable logical member bytes, including repeated physical ranges, share the ZIP
archive expansion policy: at most the larger of 256 MiB or 500 times the PCK's
encoded byte span. Embedded carrier bytes do not enlarge that budget. The full
directory is checked before any member is yielded, hashed or extracted. Encrypted
members are not read and do not consume this plaintext-work allowance. Small
bounded aliases remain valid. This is a processing/output resource bound, separate
from the directory metadata retention budget and format validity.

`vendor/rea-docs/docs/harmony-analysis.md`:

```md
# Static HarmonyOS package inventory

REA inventories HarmonyOS application packages through the shared hardened
ZIP artifact reader in `src/artifacts/`, then projects the authenticated
inventory into an execution-free application graph. This is the first
increment of the HarmonyOS roadmap (#1431): package identification and
component inventory only.

Recognized root formats:

- `.hap` — installable application module
- `.hsp` — runtime shared package
- `.app` — distribution App Pack (HAP/HSP children are listed by path). The
  App Pack classification applies to verified-ZIP-magic root inputs only; a
  nested ZIP member ending in `.app` inside another package, such as an IPA,
  keeps the generic `zip` classification.

HarmonyOS `.har` shared libraries are intentionally not classified by suffix:
`.har` also names HTTP Archive JSON, so a Harmony shared archive requires
verified ZIP bytes and is deferred with an explicit limitation.

## Usage

No external SDK, toolchain, or engine is required. Inventory the package and
project the graph; CLI and MCP use the same workflow and return
artifact-bound Evidence inline:

```sh
rea inspect-artifact /path/to/Example.hap --format json > inspection.json
node --input-type=module -e 'import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"; console.log(JSON.stringify({ inventory_evidence: [JSON.parse(readFileSync("inspection.json", "utf8"))] }));' > projection-input.json
rea project-harmony-application-graph projection-input.json --format json
```

The MCP tool `project_harmony_application_graph` takes the same
`inventory_evidence` input. The projection reports:

- exact component paths, artifact IDs, and hashes (manifests, Ark bytecode,
  resources, native libraries, JavaScript, signing)
- a packaging-model hint: Stage is claimed only from a `module.json` entry,
  FA only from `config.json`, otherwise `unknown`
- FA resources under `assets/<module>/resources/` as well as Stage `resources/`
- unavailable component paths with unknown IDs and hashes, including encrypted entries; these make projection coverage partial
- App Pack child package paths without recursive inventory
- runtime-family hints (`ark`, `native`, `javascript`) from paths and formats
- path-based N-API bridge hypotheses between bytecode and `libs/<abi>` native
  libraries

File and slice occurrences supply component and child-package paths; directory
trees and symlinks retain their identities in the source inventory without
being classified as code files. Ark and JavaScript runtime hints summarize the
classified bytecode and JavaScript lists; supported source extensions share the
same classification rule as their component rows.

Every claim is path-presence only. Manifest semantics (module identity,
abilities, entry points, permissions, dependencies), Ark bytecode contents and
versions, resource resolution, signing verification, and observed native
boundaries are out of scope for this increment and stay in the projection's
`limitations` array until a dedicated HarmonyOS provider exists. REA fails
closed on packages whose inventory cannot be authenticated.

## Verification lane

`npm run fixtures:harmony` downloads the SHA-256-pinned 1.0.1 HAP release
from the MIT-licensed [harmony-next-pipeline source repository](https://github.com/ohosvscode/harmony-next-pipeline)
into ignored `_reference/harmony-integration/`. The pin records the source
revision, release asset ID, size, and digest. The downloaded artifact is not
redistributed; bundled component licenses have not been independently audited.

```sh
npm run fixtures:harmony
REA_HARMONY_TEST_HAP=_reference/harmony-integration/entry-default-unsigned.hap \
  npm run verify:harmony
```

The lane exercises the compiled CLI and actual SDK-connected stdio MCP:
`inspect_artifact` authenticity, projection determinism, Stage-model path hints,
exact manifest/bytecode/resource component sets, empty native and bridge sets,
complete-inventory coverage, and CLI/MCP parity. It checks that this fixture has
no META-INF signing entries; that does not establish whether the package is signed.

The release artifact's compiler/SDK versions and reproducible source build have
not been independently established. This lane does not complete the pinned
toolchain acceptance in #1431 and does not verify Ark decoding or signatures.
Set `REA_HARMONY_ENTRYPOINT` to an installed package's `scripts/rea.mjs` to run
the same checks against that package; the default lane uses the repository build.

`vendor/rea-docs/docs/http3-capture-lab.md`:

```md
# Verify real HTTP/3 MITM captures

This optional Linux laboratory checks native mitmproxy captures through REA's
public CLI and MCP. It changes no runtime contracts or adapters and establishes
only the specific producer, mode and clients exercised here.

## Prepare a disposable guest

The exercised image is [Omarchy 4.0.4, build 440](https://nightly.omarchy.org/stable/4.0.4/440/omarchy-4.0.4.qcow2),
SHA-256 `43412b896fe3d730e373a51a8acf99343d7c3e6dee78aa9f9bd7fca181127264`.
Download it without installing guest packages on the host, check its digest,
and use a **new qcow2 overlay** with that file as a read-only backing image.
The matching [boot artifacts](https://nightly.omarchy.org/stable/4.0.4/440/unpacked/)
include the kernel, initrd, cmdline and upstream vm-boot recipe. Use a fresh SSH
key, loopback forwarding and guest disk; do not reuse another investigation's
writable overlay or host trust configuration. Shut the guest down before
switching overlays. Preserve the image and boot artifact hashes with evidence.

This sealed guest already supplies cURL 8.22.0 with OpenSSL 3.6.4, ngtcp2 1.25.0,
nghttp3 1.18.0 and nghttp2 1.70.0. **No guest rolling package upgrade is needed.**
Run `curl --version` and verify HTTP2 and HTTP3 features before starting. A stock
cURL from another distribution may omit HTTP/3. For a different guest, building
cURL requires a compatible TLS library, ngtcp2 and nghttp3; follow the
[official build instructions](https://curl.se/docs/http3.html), install to a guest
private prefix, and record exact source revisions and build inputs. That alternative
has not been exercised by this laboratory; it is not the pinned reproduction path.

Use a fresh VM overlay over a sealed Linux image. Use user-mode networking with
SSH forwarding bound to host loopback; keep host directories unmounted. Install
and build dependencies inside the guest, then remove its default route before
generating traffic. Host trust, routes and installed packages stay unchanged.

Record the image digest, REA source revision and these dependency versions:

- REA's `.nvmrc`, `package.json#packageManager` and locked npm dependencies.
- Official Linux x86_64 mitmproxy **12.2.3** standalone archive. SHA-256:
  `2e95286b618fa6fd33e5e62a78c2e5112571d85f42ec2bac29b97ee242bdb5c5`.
- A private Python virtual environment using the complete pinned graph in
  `scripts/fixtures/http3-lab-requirements.txt`. Save `pip freeze` and build/download logs.
- OpenSSL and cURL advertising HTTP3 and HTTP2 in `curl --version`.

The verified guest used Python 3.14.7, cURL 8.22.0, ngtcp2 1.25.0 and nghttp3
1.18.0. Other dependency profiles need verification. Back up the guest's
`/etc/hosts` before adding `127.0.0.1 lab.test`. Reserve guest TCP/UDP loopback
ports 18443 and 19443. These changes belong only to the disposable guest.

From the guest REA checkout, use its pinned Node/npm toolchain:

```sh
npm ci
npm run build:cached
python3 -m venv /absolute/lab/venv
/absolute/lab/venv/bin/pip install --no-deps -r scripts/fixtures/http3-lab-requirements.txt
/absolute/lab/venv/bin/pip check
/absolute/lab/venv/bin/pip freeze > /absolute/lab/python-requirements.txt
```

Before removing the guest default route, download the official mitmproxy archive
and verify it, then extract to the guest's private tools directory:

```sh
mkdir -p /absolute/lab/tools
curl --fail --location https://downloads.mitmproxy.org/12.2.3/mitmproxy-12.2.3-linux-x86_64.tar.gz \
  --output /absolute/lab/mitmproxy.tar.gz
printf '%s  %s\n' 2e95286b618fa6fd33e5e62a78c2e5112571d85f42ec2bac29b97ee242bdb5c5 \
  /absolute/lab/mitmproxy.tar.gz | sha256sum --check --strict
tar -xzf /absolute/lab/mitmproxy.tar.gz -C /absolute/lab/tools
/absolute/lab/tools/mitmdump --version
```

Pin the REA revision with `git rev-parse HEAD` or archive SHA-256. Build using
the exact `.nvmrc` and npm version; do not copy a different checkout's `dist`.
For stronger offline dependency reproduction, preserve downloaded Python
archives, their digests and built wheels along with the image and toolchain.
The requirement versions pin the runtime graph, not every transient build tool;
source builds and alternate interpreters are not guaranteed byte-identical.

## Run the narrow profile

Select absolute executables and a new evidence directory. The producer refuses
to reuse a directory. No certificates are installed in a system trust store;
clients and proxy receive explicit paths to freshly generated test CAs.

```sh
REA_MITMDUMP_COMMAND=/absolute/lab/tools/mitmdump \
REA_HTTP3_PYTHON_COMMAND=/absolute/lab/venv/bin/python \
npm run verify:web:http3 -- /absolute/evidence/run-1
```

The producer sends three concurrent binary POSTs on one HTTP/3 connection to the
same URL through mitmproxy reverse mode to an aioquic HTTP/3 origin. The origin
waits for all complete requests, then dispatches responses in reverse order of
completion at the origin. QUIC stream send/receive orders need not coincide. A cURL HTTP/3-only
request checks a second client implementation. Mitmproxy's real save addon
writes `normal.mitm`; no native flows are synthesized.

A second proxy run disables HTTP/3. cURL `--http3` falls back to HTTP/2, reaching
an HTTP/1.1 TLS test origin. `fallback.mitm` must retain those lower protocols,
so a successful HTTP request cannot masquerade as an HTTP/3 success.

## Acceptance and evidence

Each execution creates `verifications/<run-UUID>/` with its own diagnostics.
`verification-latest.json` belongs to the most recently registered attempt and
changes atomically from `running` to `passed` or `failed`. Registration and
the ownership check/replacement use the same SQLite transaction lock. An older
attempt finishing later keeps its own reports without replacing the marker.
The `.verification-lock.sqlite` pathname must remain in place while attempts
may run; SQLite releases the lock on connection close or process death.
Lock acquisition waits for the current owner without a timeout or lease
stealing. The verifier has per-command deadlines, but no overall run deadline;
a live stalled lock owner can therefore delay publication until it exits.
Only a successful attempt writes its own `verification.json`, after
all cleanup and input-integrity checks. `result.json` also records failures and
the original error separately from cleanup errors. Older successes remain in
identified history; a legacy root `verification.json` is archived before a rerun.
A killed verifier may leave `running`, which must never be interpreted as success.

Capture inputs live in `captures/`. To inspect them again without new traffic:

```sh
REA_MITMDUMP_COMMAND=/absolute/lab/tools/mitmdump \
npm run verify:web:http3 -- /absolute/evidence/run-1 --inspect-existing
```

Acceptance for the current run:

- Every positive native record reports HTTP/3, UDP, ALPN h3 and successful TLS
  timestamps on both legs. Connection IDs, producer TLS labels, exact TLS setup
  timestamps and connection errors match the UUID-matched producer observation
  on each leg. Endpoint handshakes independently observe QUIC v1.
- Native flow UUIDs remain distinct. Three endpoint streams share a connection
  on each leg. Origin dispatch reverses completed receipt. Client and capture
  ordering is observed, while association is verified independent of their order.
- CLI and MCP agree. Request/response bytes, lengths, SHA-256, ordered duplicate
  headers, method, scheme, authority and path match independent observations.
  Readable header names and values, request URL fields and ALPN also match;
  non-UTF-8 header bytes retain a null display value rather than replacement text.
- Actual MCP advertised schemas validate, Evidence preserves source digests and
  provider provenance, and the complete returned Evidence matches the retained MCP session records.
- The fallback capture reports client HTTP/2 over TCP and origin HTTP/1.1, with
  cURL independently reporting version 2. Input files remain unchanged.
- Every cleanup action is attempted on success and failure, and final lineage
  contains no live descendants. Recorded producer groups are inspected separately
  after token-verified cleanup, including after their launcher has exited.

Retain captures, endpoint/producer JSONL, proxy diagnostics, cURL output, manifest,
CLI/MCP output, advertised schema and session bundle. Export public certificates
and dependency/source provenance separately. Do not commit evidence, private
keys, dependencies or VM disks. Shut down the guest after exporting evidence.

The reverse proxy can preserve authority `lab.test:18443` while recording origin
port 19443. Mitmproxy's serialized flow/connection UUIDs are not stream IDs.
Endpoint stream IDs are scoped observations; this test invents no cross-leg
mapping. Mitmproxy 12.2.3's `QUICv1` label alone does not prove negotiation: the
fixture checks the negotiated `_quic._version` in pinned aioquic 1.2.0.

Coverage is native capture, Linux reverse mode, QUIC v1 and these clients.
Empty/absent/incomplete/redacted body semantics, cancellations, resets,
certificate failures, malformed captures, HAR and qlog are separate increments.
Local/WireGuard, browsers, QUIC v2, migration, 0-RTT, mTLS, replay, sustained load
and loss tolerance remain unverified by this profile. Passing it does not
establish general HTTP/3 support in REA.

Official references: [mitmproxy protocol support](https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/blob/v12.2.3/docs/src/content/concepts/protocols.md),
[HTTP/3 implementation](https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/blob/v12.2.3/mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/_http3.py),
[serialized HTTP state](https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/blob/v12.2.3/mitmproxy/http.py),
[aioquic configuration](https://github.com/aiortc/aioquic/blob/1.2.0/src/aioquic/quic/configuration.py).

## Verifier regressions

After building REA, run these inside the same isolated guest:

```sh
node --test scripts/lib/http3-verifier-lifecycle.test.mjs scripts/lib/http3-capture-assertions.test.mjs
/absolute/lab/venv/bin/python scripts/fixtures/http3-lab.test.py
```

These cover different QUIC stream completion orders, stale success reports,
multiple failed closes, separately owned process groups and partially acquired
resources, plus producer TLS fact mismatches on both legs and altered readable
fields with unchanged binary evidence. They test verifier
semantics; they do not add HTTP/3 provider coverage.
